author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Amid continuing displacement, Marawi students face educational barriers
content:
The 2024 data of the Philippine Statistics Authority showed that the BARMM had the lowest basic literacy rate among all regions in the country at 81 percent. Lanao del Sur ranked third among the region’s five provinces.


MARAWI CITY, Lanao del Sur — Affecting one’s education due to financial difficulties is a typical problem of poor communities in many parts of the country. But for families displaced after the Marawi Siege in 2017, having such a problem amid their continuing displacement hits differently.


There were many occasions that the children of Nurania Unte, 33, were not able to go to school due to financial constraints. Her family is now living in Hijrah village, Barangay Sultan Corobong, a remote temporary shelter in the Islamic City of Marawi.


Nurania Unte, an internally displaced person, watches people outside her house in Hijrah village, Barangay Sultan Corobog, one of the remote temporary shelters in Marawi City. Photo by Franck Dick Rosete/Bulatlat


Her husband’s average salary in a week, ranging from P2,500 to P4,000 (approximately US$39 to $62), for working as a construction worker remains insufficient to meet their daily needs. Since it is a project-based work, there are days when the family breadwinner is jobless.


To ensure school attendance, Unte’s three children, in many instances, were forced to walk for more or less 30 minutes from their temporary shelter to the nearest Dulay Elementary School as they cannot afford the P20 fare. 


“Almost all families here have the same problem,” she told

Bulatlat

 in Filipino.


Before the five-month Marawi Siege, Unte used to live in Barangay Papandayan. The village was not part of the 24 barangays classified as most affected areas (MAA). But the lack of financial capacity to repair their house left her family with no choice but to bear the dire situation in the shelter.


Barangay Sultan Corobong, previously part of Barangay Dulay Proper, is one of the newly created villages in Marawi, following the reported increase in the population in certain areas after the siege.


The community in Hijrah village, home of reported around 1,000 internally displaced persons (IDPs), needs free transportation as the reported cost of a back-and-forth fare stood at P240 (US$3.75) going to the city proper. “The residents here don’t have stable jobs,” Nasser Dimaampo Bongcaran, the temporary shelter president, said in Filipino.


Photo shows some of the temporary housing units in Hijrah village, Barangay Sultan, Corobong, Marawi City. Photo by Franck Dick Rosete/Bulatlat


Jelilah Casarigan, mother of seven, recalled the days that her eldest daughter ended up making the sacrifice by not being able to go to school to prioritize other siblings, and she cries every time it happens.


“My child is diligent in her studies,” Casarigan, who lives in the Bakwit village, a temporary shelter in Barangay Pindolonan, Saguiaran, Lanao del Sur, told

Bulatlat

in Filipino. “Sometimes we struggle with our finances because my [construction worker] husband does not always have a job.”


The 2025 data of the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) showed that Lanao del Sur registered the second highest unemployment rate among five provinces in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) at 7.99 percent, which translates to 44,000 unemployed individuals.


https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/30904271/visualisation.json?ref=embed-script


Unlike the IDPs in Hiraj village, families residing in the Bakwit village, on top of the utility bills, have started paying P500 (approximately $8) for monthly rent just this year, following the eviction notice they had received from the landowner.


Read:


Displaced Marawi residents face eviction from temporary shelter


The Casarigan family was awarded a permanent shelter in Saguiaran town, a few kilometers away from Marawi City, but they have yet to transfer since there was no electricity and water connections yet. 


Same struggles


Families in permanent shelters have been dealing with the same struggles. Ibralyn Macaraguit, mother of six, gives P70 ($1.09) to one of her children studying high school a day, of which P60 ($0.98) serves as the back-and-forth fare.


The lack of local transportation also gives them headaches, leaving her child to go on foot for more or less 30 minutes from Racman Pimping Maniri Dumarpa (RPMD) National Science High School in Barangay Papandayan going to their house in Darussalam village, a …

author: Harriet Williamson
title: King’s College London Made a Pro-Palestine Student Write an Essay As Punishment – Then Reported Her to Prevent for It
content:
A top UK university reported a student to the government’s counterterrorism programme over a “reflective essay” it forced her to write after suspending her for charges related to pro-Palestine activism, Novara Media can reveal.


Niamh Grant, a 22-year-old Social Sciences student at King’s College London (KCL), was informed by a student welfare adviser in emails seen by Novara Media that the university had referred her to Prevent for the essay.


The “reflective essay” was set as a condition for Grant returning to her studies at the prestigious Russell Group university following a suspension in May 2025 over pro-Palestine protests as part of the 2024 student solidarity encampment movement – in which Grant was a leader in negotiations with KCL. 


The university required Grant to reflect on the “health and safety issues” caused when she entered a kitchen area of the university and was part of a group that created an obstruction which “led to the physical injury of staff” at a protest in 2024 – something she denies. It also invited her to reflect on a protest policy which was no longer in effect after it received criticism from civil rights organisations Liberty and Amnesty International.


In the essay, Grant wrote of her horror at the suffering of Palestinians, saying: “From the Palestinian people, one message resounds: to end the genocide. It is not enough to simply acknowledge Palestinian suffering, not enough to sympathise, and not enough to feel guilt. This belief must induce an imperative.”


Turning to KCL, she wrote: “I believe that to be a student is to care about the morality of my institution, and it is because I care about the responsibility given to me as King’s student that I care about my university’s investments in the Israeli arms trade.”


KCL did not consider this essay satisfactory, with the head of student conduct and appeals telling Grant: “I cannot consider this essay provides the necessary assurance that you will not cause any further health and safety concerns, that you appreciate how your actions impacted other members of the King’s community and that you understand the importance of the university’s policies and procedures as related to protest and behaviour.”


Grant then submitted a second reflective essay, where she suggested the university should have “a bit of humility… before it begins to lecture other people and groups about violence, crimes and the obstruction of other people’s lives”. 


Grant drew comparisons with the student struggle against investments in South Africa’s apartheid regime, criticising the university for “disciplin[ing] their own students before citing them as ‘courageous’ years later when it is convenient”.


She also wrote that she drew inspiration from Imam Hussein, a historic figure in Islam who sacrificed his life in standing up against oppression. Grant compared her smaller sacrifice of the interruption of her studies to the greater sacrifice of Hussein, also known as

Husayn ibn Ali

, the grandson of the Prophet Muhammad who was killed in the 7th century.


In her essay, Grant wrote that Hussain and his family had left an example of “how we should sacrifice for the cause of fighting injustice and establishing justice on Earth”. 


From correspondence seen by Novara Media, the reference to Hussein appears to be the basis of the university’s Prevent referral. 


Grant told Novara Media that the Prevent referral was “incredibly Islamophobic” and a “method of intimidation”. She believes a Christian student who wrote that they took inspiration from the sacrifice of Jesus Christ would not have been flagged to the government’s counter-terror scheme. 


Grant said she “made an effort to explain what it means to have my degree taken away from me” and said her words were “deliberately decontextualised” to “create a justification for the Prevent referral”. 


“This isn’t something that exists in a vacuum,” she added. “It’s something that universities and schools have in their arsenal to weaponise against visibly Muslim students.” 


Prevent is part of the

 UK government’s counter-terrorism strategy

 and places a legal duty on “specified authorities”, including schools and universities, to have a “due regard to the need to prevent individuals from being drawn into terrorism”.


Dr Layla Aitlhadj, director and senior caseworker at Prevent Watch, told Novara Media that to have a reflective essay referred to Prevent is “horrifying” because it tells students that they …

title: Primeros Auxilios en contexto de manifestación callejera, segunda edición
content:
Movilización de jubiladxs el 24 de septiembre del año 2025. Fotografía: Andrés Manrique (ANRed).


Muchas veces, el primer objetivo de la represión es inducir temor para desairar primero y después desarticular las resistencias populares. Contra ello, ANRed libera la segunda edición de

 “Primeros Auxilios en contexto de manifestación callejera”

, una recopilación de medidas y cuidados básicos a la hora de hacernos de las calles.


Saber de primeros auxilios en contextos donde predomina la violencia puede ser un aporte muy valioso, que tiene en sí mismo un efecto tranquilizador. Además, las personas que no recibieron entrenamiento en primeros auxilios suelen dudar al momento de actuar, o tienen miedo de ayudar por falta de seguridad para recordar las maniobras.


Si bien no frenará la decisión política de mutilar, intentamos generar conciencia sobre la importancia de cuidar nuestros cuerpos, con los que trabajamos y sostenemos nuestras vidas y las de otros, y enfatizamos en aquellas cosas que sí podemos hacer para cuidarnos. En particular, esta guía está orientada a la prevención.


Recordamos que los cuidados son siempre una tarea colectiva, históricamente menospreciada pero fundamental para cualquier resistencia. Este es nuestro aporte.


Estamos hace 32 años en las calles, practicando la comunicación alternativa, comunitaria y popular. Acompañando las luchas siempre, mostrando lo que otros omiten y silencian.

author: Malik Chiconela Santana
title: Mozambique: A Judicial Solution to a Political Problem
content:
Venâncio Bila Mondlane, the leader of the Mozambican opposition, finds himself awaiting trial (scheduled for November 17) for his alleged role as the progenitor of the seismic protests that followed the 2024 elections and threatened to topple the state. Mondlane is president of the recently formed National Alliance for a Free and Autonomous Mozambique (ANAMOLA) party. He is accused of five crimes by the Public Prosecutor’s Office, namely

public justification of crime, incitement of collective disobedience, public instigation of crime, instigation of terrorism, and incitement of terrorism

. A conviction could mean up to 20 years in prison for the presidential runner-up, the crippling of the opposition, and a transition in the state’s handling of political opponents.


Mondlane’s road to the 2024 ballot was lined with legal and procedural obstacles.

Blocked

 from contesting the leadership of his party at the time, the Mozambican National Resistance (RENAMO), he left it and allied his campaign with the Democratic Alliance Coalition (CAD), whose electoral eligibility was confirmed on May 9, but was excluded by the National Election Commission (CNE) on July 18. The Constitutional Council (CC) upheld the decision on appeal, arguing that the parties who had formed CAD failed to notify the

Ministry of Justice and Constitutional and Religious Matters

 of their intention to form a coalition. The court framed the decision as a purely technical issue; however, its consequences were undeniably political. Mondlane found himself politically isolated only two months before the elections. Forced to reorganize his campaign, Mondlane forged a last-minute partnership with the Optimistic People for the Development of Mozambique (PODEMOS), running as an independent with the party’s political and parliamentary support.


This chronology illustrates how the political agency of Mondlane and his supporters was repeatedly at odds with applications of the electoral law. It may not establish that each application of electoral law was politically motivated, but, at the very least, it raises a broader question of how ostensibly procedural outcomes can reshape the field of political competition, and suggests that legal procedure is not necessarily neutral.


After the October 9, 2024, vote, the CNE declared Daniel Chapo, candidate of the ruling Mozambique Liberation Front (Frelimo), the winner with about 70%, to Mondlane’s 20%. In December, after more than 300 complaints of electoral crimes and irregularities had been lodged with local and district courts, the Constitutional Council revised those figures to roughly 65% and 24% respectively. The revision was, in effect, an admission that the election commission’s results were dubious at best and fictional at worst. The CC altered the results when, as a body of electoral oversight, it could only order the CNE to recount the votes or annul the elections. Unsurprisingly,

the Mozambican Bar Association

 (OAM), opposition parties, and civil society groups expressed concerns over the CC’s vague legal reasoning and the lack of an evidentiary basis for its alteration of the results.


What ensued in the wake of these opaque elections was a six-month period of unprecedented violence. In Mozambique, several elections have been followed by periods of armed conflict. What made this period unprecedented, however, was that the antagonism was not between the state and an organized army, but rather between the state and a mobilized mass of unarmed civilians. According to a

report

 by the Mozambican NGO Plataforma Decide, 411 civilians were killed, some 3,700 were injured, and around 7,200 were illegally detained between October 2024 and January 2025. These figures were disputed by the then commander-general of the police, Bernardino Rafael, who stated that 96 civilians were killed. Even so, charges have only been brought

against two officers

, and, with no updates, it is unclear whether the prosecution is pursuing these cases at all.


The protests began on October 21, when Mondlane called for a peaceful march in tribute to Elvino Dias, his lawyer, who was assassinated by assailants of no particular origin as he prepared an appeal challenging the preliminary election results. This march, like many that followed, was dispersed violently, including through the use of tear gas and live ammunition. In an environment where constitutionally protected political activities are met with violence, the …

author: Unknown
title: Protests in Qamişlo: 25 Rojava University students injured
content:
A total of 25 students were injured on November 16 in Qamişlo during protests against the planned incorporation of Rojava University into Syria’s state higher education system. The university’s Student Council announced the figures at a press conference on Sunday. For the first time, the council also confirmed that shots had been fired on university grounds during the crackdown. The council condemned the use of tear gas and firearms against the protesters as a serious violation of the university’s autonomy and the safety of its students.


The statement was issued on the university campus in Qamişlo in the presence of students. Mehebad Adil Serhan read it in Kurdish, while Fadiya Ebdullah read it in English. The Student Council explained that the delay in issuing the statement was due to its efforts over the past few days to care for the injured students and investigate the consequences of the events.


Dispute over the future of Rojava University


The clashes were triggered by a visit from a delegation from Damascus on Monday. The delegation held talks with the university administration about the planned incorporation of Rojava University into al-Furat University in Hesekê. Following the meeting, students demanded information about the decisions reached and the future of their university. When the delegation refused to make a statement, the students blocked its departure.


The conflict stems from two measures introduced by Syria’s transitional government. In addition to the planned incorporation of Rojava University into al-Furat University, the dispute concerns the Ministry of Education’s decision to revoke the recognition of equivalency for degrees awarded by certain faculties. Students regard these measures as an attack on their university’s independent academic and institutional identity.


The protests were therefore directed not merely against an administrative restructuring, but also against interference in academic self-governance and the students’ future. When the students insisted on receiving information about the planned changes, security forces of the transitional government attacked the protesters.


“Unjustifiable under any circumstances”


The Student Council described the actions as a serious violation of university autonomy and a direct threat to the safety and health of students. The protests, it said, had been an expression of legitimate demands and a commitment to preserving the academic and administrative independence of their university. Rather than resorting to violence, it added, those responsible should have sought dialogue and listened to the students’ concerns.


“What we witnessed on university grounds was the use of tear gas and firearms, which left 25 students injured. These shocking scenes are unacceptable under any circumstances and cannot be justified in any way,” the council stated. It condemned the use of military force, weapons, tear gas, and smoke agents on campus as “an attack on the inviolability of the educational institution and the dignity of all students.”


The statement did not specify whether the students’ injuries were caused by tear gas, gunfire, or other forms of violence.


Protection against reprisals and preservation of university autonomy


The council also strongly opposed any potential reprisals related to the protests. “We firmly reject any decision or measure aimed at arresting or prosecuting students for their participation in the peaceful defense of their rights,” the statement read. Such actions would further exacerbate tensions within the university, the Student Council warned and therefore demanded binding guarantees for students’ safety and protection against intimidation, pressure, and all forms of discrimination.


Regarding the university’s future, the council reaffirmed its commitment to preserving its academic and administrative independence. “Students must be able to voice their concerns peacefully and participate in decisions affecting their education and the university’s institutional future. We reject the imposition of decisions with far-reaching consequences without dialogue and mutual understanding,” the council declared. It also stressed that students must not be made to bear the consequences of decisions that jeopardize their academic future.


Appeal to international academic and human rights organizations


The Student Council called on international academic institutions, human rights organizations, and student representative bodies …

title: İklim Eylem Ağı'ndan COP31 eleştirisi: "Şimdiye kadarki en kötü COP"
content:
Uluslararası İklim Eylem Ağı (Climate Action Network International-CAN), Antalya'da düzenlenen COP31'in ardından yayımladığı değerlendirmede konferansın iklim finansmanı, adil geçiş, fosil yakıtlardan uzaklaşma ve iklim değişikliğine uyum konularında beklenen sonuçları vermediğini savundu.

Örgüt, iki hafta süren müzakerelerde özellikle Avrupa Birliği öncülüğündeki gelişmiş ülkelerin daha önce verilen taahhütlerin uygulanmasını engellediğini ileri sürdü. Türkiye ve Avustralya'nın konferans başkanlıklarının ise müzakereleri anlamlı sonuçlara yönlendirmekte başarısız olduğunu belirtti.

CAN Uluslararası İcra Direktörü Tasneem Essop, konferansın sonuçlarına ilişkin değerlendirmesinde, “Bu, şimdiye kadarki en kötü COP idi. İnsanların hayal bile edilemeyecek ölçekte acı çektiğine tanık oluyoruz ve bu konferansın insanları giderek ağırlaşan iklim krizinden korumak için adımlar atmasını umuyorduk. Bunun yerine zengin ülkeler, fark yaratabilecek önlemleri etkisiz hâle getirdi” ifadelerini kullandı.

Gelişmiş ülkelerin iklim kriziyle mücadele için mali kaynak sağlama yükümlülüklerinden kaçındığını savunan Essop, Avrupa Birliği'nin fosil yakıtlara ilişkin ifadelerin metinde bulunmamasını gerekçe göstererek sonuç metnine karşı çıkmasını da eleştirdi.

Essop, Avrupa ülkelerinin kendi fosil yakıt kullanımlarını sona erdirme ve gelişmekte olan ülkelere finansman sağlama yükümlülüklerini yerine getirmediğini ileri sürdü.

CAN tarafından yapılan açıklamada, COP31 başkanlıklarını yürüten Türkiye ve Avustralya'nın müzakerelerdeki tutumuna da eleştiri yöneltildi.

İki ülkenin temel müzakere başlıkları yerine kapsamlı bir genel karar metnine ağırlık verdiğini savunan örgüt, bunun iklim finansmanı, adil geçiş ve emisyon azaltımı konularındaki görüşmelerden dikkati uzaklaştırdığını öne sürdü.

Açıklamada, konferansa fosil yakıt şirketleri, karbon giderimi teknolojilerini destekleyen kuruluşlar ve yapay zekâ sektöründen çok sayıda temsilcinin katıldığı belirtildi. Karbon yakalama, kullanma ve depolama sektöründen 700 lobicinin konferansta olduğu kaydedilen açıklamada, bu teknolojilerin fosil yakıt üretiminin devam etmesine gerekçe oluşturabileceği uyarısında bulunuldu.

CAN tarafından yapılan açıklamada ayrıca, COP31'de iklim değişikliğine uyum için ayrılan finansmanın üç katına çıkarılmasına ilişkin somut bir uygulama planı oluşturulamadığı vurgulandı.

Açıklamada, gelişmekte olan ülkelerin 2035 yılına kadar iklim değişikliğine uyum için yıllık 305 milyar dolara ihtiyaç duyacağı, enflasyon dikkate alındığında bu ihtiyacın 420 milyar dolara ulaşacağı belirtildi.

Açıklamada, Paris Anlaşması'nın gelişmiş ülkelerin kamu kaynaklarından iklim finansmanı sağlamasına ilişkin 9.1 maddesinin hatırlatılmasına rağmen bu yükümlülüğün nasıl yerine getirileceğine ilişkin somut bir plan ortaya konulmadığı vurgulandı.

CAN Uluslararası Siyasi Stratejiler Başkanı Jacobo Ocharan, fosil yakıt sektörünün karbon yakalama teknolojileri üzerinden üretimini sürdürmeye çalıştığını ileri sürerek, “Konferans başkanlıklarının görevi bu müzakerelerin bütünlüğünü korumaktı. Bunun yerine kirleticilere fosil yakıtlardan uzaklaşmayı geciktirmek için yeni bir gerekçe sundular” dedi.

CAN Güney Asya Direktörü Dr. Sanjay Vashist ise Türkiye ve Avustralya başkanlıklarını, fosil yakıt çıkarlarını ve zengin ülkelerin ayrıcalıklarını iklim adaletinin önüne koymakla suçladı.

CAN Enerji Dönüşümü Kıdemli Yöneticisi Janet Milongo, sonuç metninde fosil yakıtlardan uzaklaşmaya ilişkin somut bir yol haritası bulunmadığını savundu. Milongo, hükümetlerin fosil yakıtları açıkça ifade etmekten kaçınırken karbon yakalama teknolojilerine geniş yer verdiğini belirterek, bunun kirletici sektörlere yeni fırsatlar sunduğunu ileri sürdü.

CAN Uyum Çalışmaları Sorumlusu Pooja Dave, COP30'da verilen finansman taahhüdünün yeniden hatırlatılmasının yeterli olmadığını ifade ederek, “Başlangıç noktası veya uygulama planı olmadan uyum finansmanını üç katına çıkarma taahhüdünü tekrarlamak hiçbir şey ifade etmiyor. Sel, kuraklık ve ölümcül sıcaklıklarla karşı karşıya kalan aileler teknik raporların arkasına sığınamaz. Her gecikme yılı hayatlara mal oluyor” dedi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: anonym
title: Demo 1×1 Flyer für Gen-Z Proteste
content:
Wir haben zu oft gesehen wie Menschen sich filmen, unvermummt Pyro zünden oder ohne Handschuhe Steine auflesen. Daher haben wir einen kleinen Demo 1×1 Flyer geschrieben.


Druckt den Flyer vor den Protesten und verteilt ihn auf den Demos. Ihr könnt auch Einweghandschuhe auf der Demo verteilen (am besten sollten Menschen 2 Paare übereinander ziehen). Animiert und zeigt Menschen auch wie man sich mit einem Tshirts vermummt, wenn es Action gibt.


Wichtig: Ergänzt die lokale Nummer des Ermittlungsausschuss vor dem Drucken. Schreibt denen auch und fragt, ob sie an dem Tag aktiv sind.


Druckt nur in linken Läden und sagt den Menschen vorher, dass ihr solche brisanten Sachen drucken wollt. Am besten Face-to-Face, notfalls mit verschlüsselter Mail anschreiben. Normale Drucker speichern die Text, die mit ihnen gedruckt wurden.


Druckt nur DNA frei. Das bedeutet habt recht frisch gewaschene lange Klamotten an. Kauft neues Papier und neue Tüten zum Transport der Flyer. Vorher nochmal alle Arbeitsutensilien und Unterlagen mit Chlor reinigen. Beim Drucken nicht in Gesicht, Haare oder auf eure Klamotten fassen und Einmalhandschuhe tragen.


Am besten helfen mehrere Menschen beim verteilen auf der Demo. Wenn am Anfang noch nicht alle schwarz angezogen sind, in bunt aber recht unkenntlich die Flyer verteilen. Nur mit Handschuhen verteilen. Möglicherweise auch weitergeben lassen.


Demo 1×1


Redet nur mit Personen über Aktionen, die mitmachen. Ihr wisst nie wer mithört oder sich im schlimmsten Fall verplappert. Redet nur face-to-face ohne Handys.


Seid am besten zu zweit auf der Demo, organisiert euch evtl. in einer größeren Gruppe. Redet vorher über alle möglichen Aktionen und ob ihr die Konsequenzen, wie Knast, ertragen könnt.


Überlegt euch ein Handzeichen und ein Wort (z.B. „Backofen“) das ihr ruft, wenn ihr euch auf der Demo verliert. Ruft auf keinen Fall eure echten Namen.


Nehmt keine Handys oder Smart-Watch mit und macht keine Fotos oder Videos (potenzielle Beweismittel). Solltet ihr euer Handy dabeihaben, schaltet es jetzt aus!


Keine Gespräche über Politik, die Demo oder Straftaten bei An- und Abreise.


Bei Vorkontrollen, nett sagen, dass ihr einkaufen geht. Ansonsten nur angeben: Name, Adresse, Familienstand, Staatsangehörigkeit und Berufsbezeichnung. Keine Arbeitsstelle oder Name eurer Schule oder Uni.


Keine Straftaten ohne Handschuhe und Vermummung, sowie in Klamotten die ihr im Alltag anhabt. Fingerabdrücke, Kleidung und DNA sind Beweismaterial.


Vermummung ist strafbar. Wechselt euer Outfit (nicht nur die Vermummung) nur für die Zeit, in der ihr unerkenntlich sein wollt. Zieht euch nur in Menschenmassen, oder Gebüschen um, wenn ihr nicht gefilmt werdet und geht dann weg.


Cops versuchen während und nach der Demo Menschen festzunehmen. Auch Zivicops ohne Uniform folgen Menschen in der Demo. Wenn euch Menschen folgen, sagt ihnen nett & bestimmt, dass sie gehen sollen.


Cops beklagen, dass (brennende) Barrikaden auf den Straßen ihnen erschweren Menschen mit Autos zu verfolgen und wenn einzelne Streifen von mehreren Menschen angegriffen werden, sie erst mehr Kräfte zusammenzuziehen müssen.


Bei Festnahme: Keine Aussage oder Unterschrift! Du hast das Recht auf einen Anruf – ruf den EA an! Keine Mitarbeitspflicht; also nicht laufen, reden oder vermummen für Videos/Bilder. Grimassen schneiden bei Fotos. Bei DNA-Abnahme Beschluss von Richter*in verlangen. Nach Verhaftung zu Sprechstunde der Roten Hilfe gehen.


Redet niemals über vergangene Straftaten, erst recht nicht mit Handys oder online.


Cops versuchen oft Personen in vermeintlichen Smalltalk zu verwickeln. Am besten einfach ignorieren und nichts sagen, dann könnt ihr euch nicht verplappern.


Nehmt euch Zeit für eine emotionale Nachbesprechung und meldet euch, wenn nötig, bei „Out Of Action“.


Packliste


Personalausweis, Schlüssel, Bahnkarte, Bargeld, Wasserflasche (still)


Telefonnummer des EA (Ermittlungsausschuss) mit Edding auf den Arm schreiben, dieser kontaktiert solidarische Anwält*innen bei Verhaftungen


Nummer des EA:


Cops filmen; versucht euch so anonym wie möglich zu kleiden (keine Rückschlüsse auf Geschlecht, Tattoos, Körperbau, Körperbehaarung…)


blaue Jeans und billige/alte Schuhe


schwarze Überziehjacke ohne Logos (gibt es günstig z.B. bei Decathlon)


schwarzes Shirt fürs Gesicht (legal bei Anreise, illegal beim Tragen)


neue Arbeitshandschuhe in einer Tüte (DNA-frei)


Die schwarzen Klamotten und Schuhe, also Sachen in denen …

author: Ezra
title: OG FFM: Aufenthaltsverbote nach den GenZ-Protesten in Frankfurt am Main
content:
OG FFM: Aufenthaltsverbote nach den GenZ-Protesten in Frankfurt am Main


Das Resümee auf Seiten der Teilnehmer*innen an den Protesten gegen soziale Ungleichheit, steigende Lebenshaltungskosten, Kürzungen im Bildungsbereich und die Wehrpflicht ist erschütternd. Viele, gerade junge Menschen, erlebten während und nach der Demonstration brutale Polizeigewalt. 

„Im Nachgang der Demonstration meldeten sich viele Betroffene bei uns und anderen Organisationen und berichteten von Verletzungen, die durch den Polizeieinsatz entstanden sind. Neben zahlreichen Augenverletzungen durch den massiven Einsatz von Pfefferspray gab es auch schwere Gehirnerschütterungen, Rippenbrüche und Knochenbrüchen“, so Anna Kaiser von der Roten Hilfe Ortsgruppe Frankfurt. 

Auch in Sozialen Medien ist einerseits das rücksichtslose Vorgehen der Polizei gegen alle Teilnehmenden der Proteste dokumentiert. Andererseits zeugen Berichte von den unbeholfenen und widersprüchlichen Polizeitaktiken vor Ort. Teilnehmende, welche den Protestzug verlassen wollten, wurden von der Polizei teilweise gewaltsam daran verhindert und kollektiv in der Frankfurter Innenstadt eingekesselt.

Einige der Protestierende erhielten in den letzten Tagen Post durch das Polizeipräsidium Frankfurt, genauer die

SOKO

 3110. Ihnen wurde ein Aufenthaltsverbot für die Frankfurter Innenstadt angedroht. 

„Nach wochenlanger medialer wie stadtpolitischer Hetze gegen die Proteste schien es Aufgabe der Polizei zu sein, Bilder der Eskalation mindestens hinzunehmen, oder sogar mit zu produzieren“, so Anna Kaiser. „Die nun folgenden Grundrechtseinschränkungen dienen dazu, die rassistische und autoritäre Hetze zu untermauern.“ Viele der Verbote sollen willkürlich bis Januar 2027 ausgesprochen werden.

Die Gewalt und die jetzigen Versuche, die geplanten Proteste gegen die Wehrpflicht am 20. November zu kriminalisieren, zeugen davon, dass die Polizei kein neutraler Akteur ist. Die Rote Hilfe empfiehlt, nicht mit der Polizei zu kooperieren, gegen Auflagen und Aufenthaltsverbote Widerspruch einzulegen und sich juristisch und politisch dagegen zu wehren.

Rote Hilfe – Ortsgruppe Frankfurt am Main


Ezra


21.11.2026 - 00:46


Pressemitteilung


Während der GenZ-Regelt-Proteste in Frankfurt am Main am 31.10.2026 erlitten dutzende, meist junge Menschen durch den brutalen Einsatz der Polizei schwere Verletzungen – vom Rippenbrüchen bis zur schweren Gehirnerschütterungen. Darüber hinaus erhielten einige Protestierende in den letzten Tagen eine schriftliche Androhung eines Aufenthaltsverbots für die Frankfurter Innenstadt. Teilweise bis Januar 2027. Die medialen Szenen, welche die Polizei mitzutragen hat, dienen nun für weitreichende repressive Grundrechtseinschränkungen.

author: Unknown
title: MP Cengiz Çiçek: Targeting ill prisoners is an ideological attack
content:
The vigil launched outside the Ministry of Justice to demand the medical treatment and release of ill prisoners entered its 10th day. The vigil is led by the MED Federation of Legal Solidarity Associations of Prisoners’ Families (MED TUHAD-FED), with the support of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) and the Free Lawyers Association (ÖHD).


DEM Party MP for Istanbul Cengiz Çiçek addressed the vigil on Wednesday, saying that the action was not only a political but also a moral responsibility. Çiçek said that the action represented an insistence on upholding all human values and that human values, law, justice and peace were necessary for everyone.


Çiçek said that a former minister had been released on health grounds after 18 days, while thousands of political prisoners had been held in prison for decades, describing this as a political choice by the government.


Çiçek emphasized that the Peace and Democratic Society Process was not merely about ending armed conflict but also encompassed the struggle against systemic and structural inequalities.


Çiçek said that the Kurdish question could not be reduced to weapons and must be addressed as a question of democracy and law. He added that the issue of ill prisoners was not limited to the individuals whose names had been made public.


Çiçek said: "The reality of ill prisoners is not limited to the people whose names have been mentioned. Through these people, an attack is being carried out against the ideas and philosophy that oppose this system, raise the cry of rebellion and voice dissent. This is an ideological attack. It is a political attack."


Çiçek said that the authorities are using treatment to force ill prisoners to abandon their struggle, adding, "No. We will not surrender."


'We did not call for peace in the grave'


Çiçek said that the struggle for justice for ill prisoners was also a struggle for peace and democracy, emphasizing that the demand for peace voiced by Kurds and democratic circles did not mean accepting a dishonorable peace.


Çiçek added: "We Kurds, democrats and revolutionaries did not mean that we were begging for peace when we called for it. We did not call for peace in the grave. We have never regarded a peace in which we receive the lifeless bodies of our people from prisons as genuine peace. Nor did we call for a dishonorable peace."


Çiçek underlined that they were active participants in the struggle for democracy while assuming responsibility for ensuring a permanent end to armed conflict within the framework of the Peace and Democratic Society Process. He added that they maintained this position under the leadership of the mothers wearing white headscarves.


'Let us strengthen the struggle together'


Çiçek addressed all sections of society dissatisfied with the government's policies and current practices, saying that the vigil should not be regarded solely as the struggle of families whose relatives were in prison.


Çiçek said that the action was a call to collectively strengthen the struggle for a democratic republic and democracy. He urged all opposition groups to support the vigil and strengthen the struggle.


The vigil outside the Ministry of Justice continue today at 2 p.m.

author: Main alba channel
title: Prisonniers de la démocratie.Vostfr
content:
Prisonniers de la démocratie


Titre original :  Presos de la democracia


Réalisation :   Basilis Chatzigabriel


Année :           2006


Langue :   espagnol sous-titré en français.


Durée :          47 minutes


À la mort de Franco, le capitalisme espagnol s'est mis à lorgner sérieusement du côté de l'Union européenne. Pour l'intégrer, il devait se parer d'habits plus démocratiques et ce fut "La Transition".


Mais les hommes politiques, les juges, les militaires, les policiers étaient restés en place.


La répression contre les mouvements sociaux était toujours aussi féroce. Les prisons étaient pleines de prisonniers sociaux et politiques qui s'organisaient pour s'évader ou se mutiner.


Afin de réprimer ces mouvements, le pouvoir s'est inspiré des expériences menées dans d'autres pays, comme l'Allemagne, pour créer des prisons de haute sécurité où l'arbitraire régnait en maître.


Miguel et Guille, deux militants révolutionnaires incarcérés à cette époque, nous racontent les conditions et les conséquences de leur détention en tant que Prisonniers de la démocratie.

title: Kağıthane’de tamirciyi darbedip araçla kaçırdılar iddiası: 2 kişi tutuklandı
content:
Kağıthane'de devriye ekiplerinin durdurduğu 3 kişinin yanındaki motosikletin çalıntı çıkmasının ardından, aracı tamir ettiği belirtilen Suriye uyruklu Moussa El A.'nın çalıştığı depoya gelen şüphelilerce tekme ve yumruklarla darbedildiği öne sürüldü. İddiaya göre El A.'yı otomobil bagajına koymakta başarılı olamayan grup, yaşanan arbede sırasında kendisini zorla otomobile bindirerek kaçırdı. Saldırganların elinden kurtulmayı başaran El A.'nın şikayeti üzerine yürütülen işlemlerde Yusuf Bilal Y. ve Vedat Y. tutuklandı.

Saldırı, 8 Ekim Perşembe günü saat 23.00 civarında Gürsel Mahallesi'nde yaşandı. Alınan bilgilere göre devriye ekipleri, hal ve hareketlerinden şüphelendikleri 3 kişiyi durdurdu. Ekiplerin, yanlarındaki plakasız motosikletin kime ait olduğunu sorması üzerine, aracın Moussa El A.'dan alındığı ve Umut T.'ye satmak için bir araya geldiklerini ileri sürdü. Şasi numarasının silindiği tespit edilen motosikletin, motor numarası üzerinden yapılan incelemede çalıntı olduğu ortaya çıktı.

Motosikletin çalıntı olduğunun belirlenmesi üzerine Yusuf Bilal Y.'nin, tamirci Moussa El A.'nın bulunduğu depoya gittiği öne sürüldü. Aracı El A.'nın sattığını savunan Yusuf Bilal Y.'nin saldırısının ardından, bir müddet sonra Ö.Y.'nin babası 38 yaşındaki Vedat Y. de depoya geldi. El A.'yı dışarı çıkararak darbeden zanlıların, kendisini zorla otomobile bindirmek istediği iddia edildi. Otomobile binmek istemeyen El A.'nın şüphelilerden polis çağırmalarını talep ettiği, bunun üzerine şüphelilerin telefonla olay yerine başka kişileri çağırdığı kaydedildi.

Sokakta 4-5 kişinin tekme ve yumruklarla vurduğu öne sürülen El A.'nın otomobilin bagajına konulmak istendiği, direnmesi nedeniyle sokakta arbede çıktığı aktarıldı. Yaklaşık 2 dakika süren ve bağırışların duyulduğu arbedenin ardından El A.'yı bagaja sokamayan grubun, onu zorla otomobile bindirerek bölgeden uzaklaştırdığı ve araç içinde de darbettiği iddia edildi. O anların güvenlik ya da cep telefonu kamerasına yansıdığı belirtildi.

Kaçırıldığı kişilerin elinden kurtulan El A., motosikletin çalıntı olduğunu saptayan polis ekiplerinin bulunduğu noktaya gitti. Vedat Y.'nin kendisine vurduğunu ifade eden El A., şüphelilerden şikayetçi oldu. M.G. ve Ö.Y. Kağıthane Çocuk Büro Amirliğine, diğer kişiler ise işlemleri için polis merkezine sevk edildi. Soruşturma kapsamında yakalanan Yusuf Bilal Y. ve Vedat Y., sevk edildikleri mahkemece tutuklanarak cezaevine gönderildi.

İddiaya göre hadise öncesinde mahalleden tanıdığı 2 kişi, tamir edilmesi amacıyla El A.'ya motosiklet getirdi. Saat 17.00 sıralarında teslim aldığı aracın arka fren teli ile balatasını yenileyen El A.'nın, motosikleti saat 20.30 civarında teslim ettiği belirtildi. Aracın çalıntı olduğunun anlaşılması sonrasında motosikleti El A.'dan satın aldığını öne süren Ö.Y.'nin, sorumluluktan kaçmak amacıyla tamirciye iftira attığı iddia edildi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

content:
Service outages, like the ones we've seen take down everything from airlines to email, seem to be coming faster than ever. For over 35 years, EFFector has been your guide to understanding the intersection of technology, civil liberties, and the law. This issue covers ALPR at the ballot box, surveillance wearables, and how digital monoculture makes service outages worse.

author: Darius Tahir
title: Health Tech Is Pushing Data-Collecting “Smart” Implants That Raise Cost of Care
content:
Doctors can charge for examining data collected by devices that have little evidence for benefiting patient health.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Steve Russak, 70, of Santa Rosa Valley, California, woke up from knee replacement surgery last year to a text message. It was from the company that made his new knee. Over the next few days, the company, Zimmer Biomet, texted four times. Russak didn’t understand the inquiries asking him to use an app, he said.

Finally, a company representative called and offered help setting up some accessories, Russak told KFF Health News. “I said, ‘What? I don’t know what you’re talking about.’”

It turned out Russak did not receive just any old replacement of bone and cartilage. He’d had a “smart knee” put in — an artificial joint called the Persona IQ with a lithium-ion battery, sensors, and transmitter that, should he authorize it, would send data about his gait and range of motion to his clinicians and Zimmer.

Russak is suing the doctor, Zimmer, and Canary Medical, a health technology company that helped develop the device. In his lawsuit, Russak claims the knee was an “unauthorized implantation” and that, according to Zimmer’s “patient-facing materials,” he should have been given the option to opt out of data collection or decline the knee altogether, but wasn’t.

Russak said he doesn’t want to set up the device to collect and transmit data for several reasons, including his privacy. Now that it’s in his body, though, he said it poses potential disruptions. For example, Russak said he recently couldn’t get an MRI because of compatibility issues.

Neither the doctor nor the doctor’s lawyer responded to multiple requests for comment.

The case is ongoing, with the next hearing scheduled for December. Russak said he has dropped the fraud and breach of fiduciary duty allegations originally filed against the doctor but is continuing to sue on other grounds, including lack of informed consent. The doctor has yet to respond to the complaint in court.

Both Zimmer and Canary filed initial responses denying “each and every allegation” in Russak’s complaint. They have offered a variety of defenses, including that any damages are the fault of another party or, as Zimmer’s response said, caused by actions or reactions “not reasonably foreseeable.”

Canary Medical did not respond to requests for comment. Zimmer spokesperson Troy Kirkpatrick declined to comment on lawsuits against the company but said that “nearly 90%” of surveyed patients who received Zimmer’s joint replacements report they would choose an orthopedic device with remote monitoring capabilities again in the future.

“The transmission of post-operative recovery data requires patient authorization at the time the patient sets up an account and is designed to support patient-surgeon relationships and postoperative care,” Kirkpatrick said in an emailed statement. He added that Zimmer takes privacy and compliance with regulations “very seriously.”

The smart knee is part of a burgeoning trend in American medicine. While Zimmer introduced its device as “the world’s first and only” FDA-approved smart knee in 2021, there’s now a range of internet-connected devices — from implants to external products such as blood pressure monitors — that report data about patients’ conditions to doctors or other medical professionals. To proponents, the products offer the chance for better care: They can provide measurements showing whether a patient’s glucose is swerving out of control, for instance.

However, enhanced monitoring comes with potential drawbacks, including threats to privacy, and some doctors and researchers caution there is little evidence that smart devices improve health outcomes.

There’s “a lot of enthusiasm for remote monitoring technologies. There is tremendous potential,” said Sanket Dhruva, a University of California-San Francisco cardiologist and digital health researcher. But there’s a need for more rigorous data, he said. “We’re getting all this data — is this helping our patients recover better? That’s what we really care about.” Nonetheless, such devices generally mean more money for doctors, who can charge to examine the information they collect.

Both Medicare and private insurers reimburse clinical professionals for reviewing data from smart devices. In 2024, nearly 1 million Medicare beneficiaries …

author: Unknown
title: Narges Mohammadi calls for the protection of women against cyber threats
content:
Women in Iran face legal and societal threats. While women's rights organisations continue to call for the strengthening and enforcement of existing laws and institutions that safeguard women's dignity and security, Nobel Peace Prize-winning activist Narges Mohammadi has released a video message.


In her message, shared on a digital platform, Narges Mohammadi called for solidarity with and support for women who are subjected to organised cyber threats and interference because of their activities in social, political, media and human rights fields.


Narges Mohammadi said that, in recent years, she herself has faced harassment, insults, death threats and widespread gender-based cyber violence, adding that these attacks continued even while she was imprisoned.


Addressing the methods of cyber harassment targeting women, Narges Mohammadi explained that these attacks include organised smear campaigns, the exposure of personal information, insults, misogyny, the spread of misinformation and the circulation of fabricated images generated using artificial intelligence (AI). She emphasised that the aim of these attacks is to isolate, intimidate and silence women.


Drawing attention to statistics, Narges Mohammadi said that more than 70 percent of women journalists, activists and those in leadership positions experience cyber harassment. She warned that such attacks must not silence women or force them to withdraw from public life.


At the end of her statement, Narges Mohammadi reiterated the need for solidarity and collective support to protect women facing smear campaigns and cyber threats.

author: EDRi
title: EDRi-gram, 19 November 2026
content:
What has the EDRi network been up to over the past few weeks? Find out the latest digital rights news in our regular newsletter. In this edition: Making sense of the Digital Fairness Act, a very unmerry birthday to the Digital Omnibus, and more!

Last week, the European Commission put digital fairness on the menu with a proposal for its long-awaited Digital Fairness Act (DFA) – and we have some food for thought.

This law will strengthen consumer protection against manipulative and exploitative commercial practices, such as fake notifications designed to keep bringing us back to an app, endless scrolling that keeps us online way longer than you intended, and other personalised techniques used by online services that exploit our vulnerabilities. First things first, proposal actually takes some important steps forward by introducing new prohibitions on deceptive design, extending specific protections beyond the biggest online platforms, and recognising the harms associated with addictive digital features. However, we were left wondering – why promise digital fairness yet leave the users to do all the work instead of holding manipulative online services responsible? Read our analysis on Tech Policy Press.

Despite it all, the DFA proposal – something that actually might protect our rights online – is a welcome respite in the current wave of deregulation in the EU. This week, we’re also reckoning with the fact that November 19, 2026 marks one year since the Commission published the proposals for the Digital Omnibus. We, along with many other civil society organisations, had warned that this would be a massive reopening of EU’s core digital protections that would risk dismantling the very foundation of human rights and tech policy in the EU. One year on, it seems like we were granted Apollo’s gift of prophecy. On this unfortunate occasion, we’re standing strong with 100 organisations, experts, academics and more to urge EU lawmakers to not simplify away our rights.

In this edition, you can also explore our extremely thorough guide to the European Parliament’s 1840 amendments to the Digital Omnibus on Data, focusing on what they would mean for privacy, data protection and, ultimately, people’s rights. Yes, 1840, you read that right. Hungry for more? Also read our thoughts on the EU governments’ position on the Digital Omnibus.

1,840 amendments, one basic question: will the Data Omnibus simplify EU digital rules or weaken people’s rights? author: By Jo Kimmy, Contributor
title: From Hospitals to Palantir HQ: Protests Across England Over Controversial Healthcare Data Deal
content:
London, England — “We need to take our power back! Our UK government needs to represent the interests of the British public, who elected them into power, not the Zionist entity,” said Taby Khan, a health research scientist protesting outside The Royal London Hospital.


On October 1, doctors, nurses, health care workers and members of the public took to the streets at more than 40 locations across England, demanding an end to the controversial £330 million ($442 million) contract between the National Health Service (NHS) and U.S. technology company Palantir.


The mobilization was organized by the Palestine Solidarity Campaign, Health Workers for a Free Palestine, Amnesty International, Medact, Keep Our NHS Public, and other groups. They argue that a company known for its work with military and immigration agencies, including the development of AI and surveillance technologies, should not have access to the sensitive health data of

60 million people

 in England.


The protests began outside hospitals across the country, including four locations in London, before culminating in a demonstration outside Palantir’s London headquarters.


Located in central London, Palantir’s London office is the company’s

largest globally

, employing more people than its Silicon Valley headquarters. In front of the building, with its dark, heavily tinted windows and no visible signs identifying it as Palantir’s offices, hundreds of people chanted, held signs and displayed a giant symbolic notice calling for the contract to be terminated.


The demo was largely peaceful, although verbal tensions arose between anti-Palantir protesters and Zionist agitators who were trying to disrupt the demonstration and provoke tensions. Some protesters accused the police of allowing these tensions to develop.


The protest brought together concerns that might otherwise remain separate: the privatization of public services, the security of patient information, the expansion of surveillance technology and Palantir’s involvement in war crimes.


Palantir and the NHS: Who Owns Britain’s Health Data?


The NHS was officially

established

 on July 5, 1948, marking the first time a Western country provided free medical care to its entire population, regardless of status.


The relationship between the NHS and the U.S. tech company

began with an “emergency” contract

 under which Palantir offered to support the vaccination program and data management projects. In 2023, with little consideration for alternative solutions, Palantir was awarded the

contract

 to deliver the

NHS Federated Data Platform (FDP)

.


As the

NHS Data Professionals

 explain: “duplications and local variations prevent smooth linkage across datasets and regions.” The FDP is intended to help NHS organizations connect information held across different systems, making it easier to coordinate services, plan capacity and support operational decisions.


The underlying challenge is real: information can be fragmented across hospitals, general practices and regional services, making it difficult to build a joined-up picture of patient care.


Data analysts have raised concerns about the FDP’s highly centralized structure. Palantir supplies data engineers and manages the underlying infrastructure, which provides limited transparency and leaves NHS organizations with less ability to independently adapt the software to their needs.


From Military Intelligence to Public Healthcare


“Palantir is here to disrupt…and, when it’s necessary, to scare our enemies and, on

occasion, kill them.” –

Alex Karp, Palantir CEO


During the protest in front of Palantir’s London headquarters, a letter written by an anonymous NHS data analyst was read aloud. In it, the analyst described how she had begun to hate her job, working with software developed by a company responsible for the deaths of hundreds of her healthcare colleagues.


Palantir initially focused on government, military and intelligence agencies before expanding into the commercial and wider public sectors. The NHS FDP operates on the Foundry software, which is marketed as a system for the “modern enterprise.” Its other products include Gotham, used for “defense and resilience,” and Apollo, which manages software deployment.


The company’s military business is central to why many healthcare workers oppose its role in the NHS. Its

close involvement in U.S. and Israeli military operations

, alongside accusations of complicity in war …

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Giorgio Agamben: The death of the word?
content:
Michelangelo,

Cumaean Sibyl

 (c. 1511), Sistine Chapel, Vatican City


This short article was originally published under the title “Morte della parola?” in the Italian newspaper

Paese Sera

 on 8 February 1968. It has been republished in the latest issue of the French magazine

Entétement

, although the original version can be found on the

La Voce di Fiore

 archive website. A Spanish translation of the same can be found at th magazine

Ficción de la razón

.


A book has recently been published in Paris,

Of Grammatology

 (1967), a work destined to cause a stir not only in the field of linguistic studies. Jacques Derrida, one of the most original figures in the new wave of French philosophical criticism, begins with the observation that, today, “through a movement whose necessity we can barely glimpse, everything that, for at least twenty centuries, has tended to be defined under the name of language, is beginning to be summarised under the name of writing”. It does indeed seem that writing—which, according to Rousseau, was nothing more than a complement to speech—is gradually freeing itself from its subordination to the phonetic medium, to the point of reversing its traditional relationship with language: writing would therefore not be a technique in the service of language, but rather, on the contrary, it is language that can be considered a specific case, an aspect, of writing.


To better understand the phenomenon to which Derrida refers when he speaks of writing dissociated from the phonetic element, one need only consider the example of mathematics, whose symbolic notation does not refer to any spoken language. If we consider that today we are witnessing a process of mathematisation across all the sciences, the “liberation” of writing described by Derrida becomes an extremely concrete phenomenon (readers who have followed recent news regarding the

in vitro

 synthesis of living matter, carried out by certain American scientists, will recall having heard talk of writing and “programmes” even in relation to the most elementary processes of the living cell). The “liberation” of writing described by Derrida becomes an extremely concrete phenomenon.


On the basis of these premises, Derrida deduces the need for a pure science of writing, which considers writing prior to speech and independently of it: this science is, precisely, “grammatology”; and, to define its aims, it suffices to substitute this term for “semiology”, the term Saussure uses to outline the programme of his famous

Course in General Linguistics

: “We shall call it grammatology… and, as it does not yet exist, we cannot say what it will be; but it has a right to exist, and its place is determined in advance”. The age of speech, which began under the creative power of the verb, is drawing to a close before our very eyes; the character of this new age might be summed up in the following formula: “In the beginning was the written word’’.


Whilst it is true that, from this perspective, linguistics must become a mere branch of grammatology, Derrida seems, however, to overlook the fact that a science already exists which considers language not as speech, but as code and writing; consequently, grammatology itself should necessarily be understood as a sub-branch or a section of that science. This is cybernetics, which, from its beginnings in Wiener’s theories, defined its world as a universe of writing and coding. The very idea of grammatology is already fully contained within the notion of “programme”, one of the key concepts of cybernetics. Etymologically, “programme” —pro-grammer— means “to put the letter (that is,

writing

) first”, whilst “prophecy” means, by contrast, “to put the word first”. Indeed, in the programme assigned to an electronic brain, everything that constitutes the living, phonetic element of language is erased to make way for a system of absolute writing that can be deciphered but not pronounced. It is fair to say that, up to now, our civilisation has known two types of language that have gradually diverged: the language of science is, essentially, written language —code, writing—, whilst the language of poetry and philosophical thought is spoken language —breath, word—. Nevertheless, these two domains—which, for convenience’s sake, we might call the “sphere of the programme” and the “sphere of prophecy”—are drawing ever closer together today thanks to cybernetics; through the mathematisation of human phenomena, cybernetics …

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Harassment won’t stop a son’s search for his missing father
content:
Marklen Lariosa, son of missing Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) labor organizer William Lariosa, speaks during a rally in Davao City on the first anniversary of his father’s disappearance on April 10, 2025. Photo by Kath Cortez/Davao Today

“Family members searching for their disappeared loved ones have to endure threats and harassment from state forces on top of the terrible uncertainty and emotional turmoil they are already going through.”

Is it a mistake for a son to demand justice and accountability?

Marklen, son of disappeared labor organizer William Lariosa, raised this question following the recent incident of harassment and surveillance he experienced. Members of his family were alarmed after two unidentified individuals were looking for his residence on the night of October 25.

He told Bulatlat that this was the first time such an event had happened since his father, a labor organizer under Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) Southern Mindanao, was abducted in Quezon, Bukidnon, on April 10, 2024.

Marklen could not think of other possible reasons, suspecting that the incident may have something to do with his continuing involvement in campaigns and mobilizations that demand the surfacing of Lariosa. “Is it a mistake for a son to search for his missing father?” he further asked.

Read: After 2 years, son laments continuing disappearance of Mindanao labor organizer

Neighbors of the Lariosa family in their hometown in Davao de Oro province were the ones who encountered the two individuals. They reportedly wore helmets and were on board a black motorcycle, introducing themselves as “collectors” when they were asked.

For Marklen, the response and presence of the two raised suspicions. Aside from the fact that they visited the community around 7 p.m., which is outside the regular working hours, Marklen said that he did not apply for any financial loan.

After the incident, he was concerned for the safety of his family, prompting them to lodge a blotter report with the barangay. However, he stood firm that it won’t stop him from continuing his cause.

Desaparecidos, an organization of families and friends of enforced disappearance victims, denounced the incident, urging the government to put an end to this kind of harassment.

“Family members searching for their disappeared loved ones have to endure threats and harassment from state forces on top of the terrible uncertainty and emotional turmoil they are already going through,” JL Burgos, Desaparecidos chairperson, said in a statement.

Rights groups Karapatan and the Center for Trade Union and Human Rights (CTUHR) also expressed strong condemnations about what happened.

Marklen, a member of the National Board of Desaparecidos, has raised a possibility that the two individuals who recently visited their neighborhood might be connected to those who visited their house several times prior to the disappearance of his father.

He said they were visited by individuals who allegedly introduced themselves as state agents once in 2022 and three times in 2023, accusing Lariosa of being involved in communist insurgency. There were warnings, he added, that they would get dragged into it if they would not cooperate.

The series of visits was reportedly the primary reason why Lariosa was forced to take refuge in Bukidnon. Marklen affirmed that his father, who remains missing, had been a labor organizer.

On July 8, the Supreme Court required certain commanders and elements of Philippine Army units to comment on the petition for review on certiorari filed by the family.

Read: Military ordered to reply to missing Mindanao labor organizer’s case

Since 2024, KMU Southern Mindanao has documented 57 cases of human rights violations against its members and organizers.

The labor group released a statement on October 24, presenting the faces of some individuals, including former high-ranking New People’s Army (NPA) member Roberto Rosete Jr., who allegedly harassed KMU’s leaders and members.

Read: Groups decry surveillance of KMU office in Southern Mindanao

Marklen called for an end to any form of harassment and intimidation against families of the disappeared, pointing out that achieving justice is their only goal. (RVO)

author: Shan Kenshin Ecaldre
title: Peasant organizer persists despite surveillance
content:
Jesus Monasterial. (Photo from Photo from Tanggol Magsasaka-TK)

Repeated surveillance restricted his movements and caused anxiety over his family’s safety.

When he was a university student, he questioned the purpose of agricultural education. Now he is organizing landless farmers and fisherfolk.

Jesus Monasterial has spent more than two years working with rural communities in Southern Tagalog. However, his work resulted in repeated surveillance by state forces, peasant groups said.

On October 31, Tanggol Magsasaka–Timog Katagalugan reported that a police intelligence operative identified as “Bruno” had been asking about Monasterial’s whereabouts in Lian, Batangas. The operative was reportedly previously assigned in Nasugbu.

At the time, Monasterial was assisting a protest camp in Barangay San Diego, where farmers, fisherfolk, and residents opposed the possible demolition of several houses.

“I was on my way back to the people’s protest camp in San Diego when news reached us that someone had been asking about my personal information,” he said.

The camp was established by Samahang Mangangawil 1979 and the San Diego Homeowners’ Association, with support from the Katipunan ng mga Samahang Magbubukid sa Timog Katagalugan (KASAMA-TK) and Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas–Timog Katagalugan (PAMALAKAYA-TK).

The incident prompted fellow organizers to discuss security measures. They also plan to file a complaint before the Commission on Human Rights (CHR).

Monasterial’s involvement in peasant organizing began at the University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB) where he was enrolled in BS Agricultural Biotechnology.

Coming from a family of farmers in Bicol, where his grandparents worked as agricultural tenants, he became increasingly critical of an agricultural education system that he said served the interests of transnational corporations rather than addressing farmers’ lack of land and government support.

Through the League of Filipino Students–UPLB, he became involved in social issues action and joined community immersions with farmers in Tartaria, Silang, Cavite, as well as Mangyan communities in Mindoro and Dumagat communities in Rizal.

These experiences led him to leave his studies and become a full-time organizer. He now serves as deputy secretary-general of KASAMA-TK.

His work involves staying in communities, conducting consultations and political education, and helping establish local farmers and fisherfolk associations.

“Being a full-time organizer means devoting my entire time to the communities and being far from my loved ones,” he said, adding that he had to set aside his plan to finish college.

The October 31 incident was not the first reported surveillance involving Monasterial.

On July 19, 2026, soldiers from the 16th Infantry Battalion of the Philippine Army reportedly sought to identify the organizers of KASAMA-TK’s Regional Peasant Consultation in Barangay Malinis, Lemery, Batangas.

On September 21, a man introducing himself as “Del” Dela Cruz reportedly approached a member of Sugarfolks’ Unity for Genuine Agricultural Reform (SUGAR-Batangas), attempting to persuade the member to leave the organization and provide information about its activities.

According to Tanggol Magsasaka–Timog Katagalugan, the man showed footage of a protest outside the Department of Agriculture regional office led by the Alyansa ng Magsasaka para sa Kumpensasyon (AMK), SUGAR-Batangas, KAISAHAN, and KASAMA-TK. He allegedly warned the member against working with Monasterial, claiming that the organizer was “already drawing attention.”

The protest resulted in a dialogue with government representatives to demand agricultural inputs and implements for farmers and farmworkers affected by successive calamities.

The groups also cited previous incidents in Barangay Casile, Laguna; Lupang Ramos and Tartaria, Cavite; and Coron, Palawan.

title: Kurdistan Regional Government: We reject the use of military rhetoric and threats
content:
Kurdistan Region’s Prime Minister Masrour Barzani chaired the KRG Council of Ministers’ meeting today. The meeting focused primarily on the KRG’s position regarding measures taken yesterday by the federal government of Iraq.


The Council of Ministers reaffirmed that the Kurdistan Region is committed to fulfilling all its constitutional obligations and demands the full provision of its constitutional rights: “The KRG has consistently expressed its readiness to resolve outstanding issues with the federal government within the framework of the Constitution. Consequently, the KRG expresses its deep concern and strong protest regarding the statement issued on behalf of the spokesperson for the Commander-in-Chief of the Iraqi Armed Forces, which violates both the Constitution and the constitutional rights of the Kurdistan Region. This statement is a dangerous indication of a lack of belief in the federal system and represents an attempt to return Iraq to a centralized regime, which contradicts the Iraqi Constitution. The KRG rejects the use of military rhetoric and threats, which appear to stem from a premeditated, long-standing plan directed against the constitutional structure of the Kurdistan Region.”


The Council of Ministers reaffirmed that the Kurdistan Region has consistently supported measures to combat corruption and illegal activities, and has cooperated and coordinated with the federal government and will continue to do so to eliminate illicit practices. It called for the comprehensive eradication of corruption and oil smuggling across all of Iraq.


The Council of Ministers stressed that the Kurdistan Region is the product of the sacrifices of the heroic Peshmerga and thousands of martyrs; it is not a gift bestowed upon the people of Kurdistan: “The Kurdistan Region has played an active and influential role in establishing the current federal system in Iraq, regards itself as a co-owner of that system, and will never relinquish its constitutional rights, which extend far beyond salaries, budgets, and financial entitlements. They also encompass political rights and the legitimate cause of the people of Kurdistan.”


The KRG Council of Ministers stressed that issues between the Kurdistan Region and the federal government must be resolved through dialogue, negotiations, and mutual understanding within the constitutional framework, calling for the full implementation of the permanent Iraqi Constitution.


“The primary reason these issues remain unresolved is the failure to implement the Constitution, particularly Article 140, which has been neglected for years, with no steps taken to normalize the situation in the disputed Kurdish territories. In accordance with the Constitution, the Federal Council of Iraq should be established, and the Federal Supreme Court reconstituted on a constitutional basis that reflects all components of Iraq.”


The Council of Ministers expressed its gratitude to the Kurdistani people, as well as to all political parties, forces, and components, urging them to maintain their national stance, unity, and solidarity in defense of the constitutional rights of the people of Kurdistan and the Kurdistan Region's constitutional framework. It also called upon the Kurdistan Region's representatives in the Iraqi Parliament and the federal government to continue their national role in defending the rights of the Kurdistani people.


The Council of Ministers reaffirmed its support for freedom of opinion and expression. However, it emphasized that anyone who acts against the constitutional structure of the Kurdistan Region, constitutional principles, or Kurdistan’s national interests and incites people to create chaos and oppose the rights of the Kurdistani people should face appropriate legal action.

author: Mike Ludwig
title: Trump Judicial Nominee at Center of GOP Drama Signed Off on Deadly Boat Strikes
content:
Nominated to be a federal judge, T. Elliot Gaiser signed off on deadly airstrikes experts call extrajudicial executions.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Media coverage of Republican infighting over judicial nominee T. Elliot Gaiser has focused on the strong words exchanged between Texas Senators John Cornyn and Ted Cruz. President Donald Trump nominated Gaiser to become a federal judge in Texas, but Cornyn blocked a crucial committee vote on November 18 to advance the pick forward.

“Everyone knows that I am a notorious cusser and screamer and that Ted is a fragile thing,” Cornyn said on November 21 in a social media post describing a previous heated exchange between the two lawmakers. Cornyn has argued that Gaiser is not from Texas and has little trial experience, while Cruz accuses Cornyn of handing an open judicial seat to Democrats.

However, what has received far less attention is Gaiser’s role in producing the legal opinion that greenlit the U.S. military’s deadly airstrikes on civilian boats in the Caribbean and Pacific Ocean that the Trump administration has accused, without evidence, of smuggling drugs. The strikes have killed more than 200 people in what human rights groups say are effectively extrajudicial executions in blatant violation of U.S. and international law.

“We’re talking about legal opinions used to justify military strikes that have killed hundreds of people, alongside a broader pattern of putting the president’s personal interests ahead of the law,” said Michael Teter, co-founder of the Legal Accountability Center, in a statement.

Gaiser currently serves as assistant attorney general in the Justice Department, where he leads the Office of Legal Counsel (OLC). He is also Trump’s nominee for a lifetime federal judgeship in the Northern District of Texas. Cornyn used a procedural maneuver last week to block the Senate Judiciary Committee from advancing Gaiser’s nomination. However, Cornyn remains under pressure from Cruz and other conservatives to reverse course and allow a vote on Gaiser as Republicans race to confirm Trump nominees before a Democratic majority takes over in January.

Meanwhile, the Legal Accountability Center filed a bar complaint against Gaiser on November 18, calling for an investigation into his role in providing legal cover for the deadly airstrikes on civilian boats in international waters. The complaint also cites a series of opinions released by the OLC that allegedly prioritize Trump’s personal interests over federal law, including a controversial opinion declaring that the Presidential Records Act, a key oversight law, is unconstitutional and does not apply to Trump.

“Government lawyers have a duty to tell the president when the law says ‘no,’ not simply find ways to justify whatever he wants to do,” Teter said, adding that the allegations are “extraordinarily serious.”

At the center of the complaint is a secret legal opinion written under Gaiser’s leadership to provide legal justification for the Trump administration’s airstrikes on civilian boats suspected of smuggling drugs. Issued on September 5, 2025, the legal opinion followed an infamous September 2 attack in which two shipwrecked survivors of an initial U.S. airstrike were killed by a secondary (or “double tap”) strike while clinging to the wreckage in the water.

Rep. Jim Himes (D-Connecticut), who serves on the House Intelligence Committee and saw video of the strikes, pointed out that the second strike was impermissible by U.S. military manual standards. The bar complaint against Gaiser alleges he failed to exercise independent judgment and provided legal cover for unlawful killings.

While the legal opinion remains classified, court filings indicate the 49-page memo was signed by Gaiser, according to the bar complaint. Members of Congress who have seen the memo have publicly outlined its legal reasoning, which rests on a theory that the U.S. is engaged in a formal armed conflict with drug smugglers. The Washington Office on Latin America (WOLA), a human rights group, calls this reasoning “badly flawed.”

The first Trump administration official to advocate on the record for military strikes on civilian vessels appears to be Emil Bove, Trump’s former personal attorney known for his extremism and loyalty to the president. In February 2025, Bove criticized traditional anti-drug …

author: Harriet Williamson
title: US Military Set to Detonate Toxic Lead Bomb in Iowa
content:
Children, pregnant women and chronically ill people in Iowa are being advised to evacuate as the US army prepares to blow up a stockpile of munitions laced with lead on Wednesday. 


Nearly five tonnes of unstable bomb-making chemicals stored at a base in Middletown, Iowa, are scheduled for detonation despite serious risks to human health. 


The detonation is expected to send a toxic plume of lead-containing dust particles over eastern Iowa and into the neighbouring state of Illinois, where toxins will likely settle on farmland, homes and playgrounds. 


There is no safe level of exposure to lead, which is a neurotoxin. 


350 farms could be exposed

 to the toxic lead dust, according to the US Department of Agriculture. 


Children and pregnant women are particularly at risk as exposure to lead can interfere with fetal brain development, cause cognitive damage and increase the likelihood of miscarriages and premature births. 


In adults, lead exposure is linked to decreased kidney function, fertility issues and heart problems, along with

 increased risks

 of various cancers.


Iowa has the

second-highest rate of cancer

 among US states, and is one of only three states where rates of cancer are rising. 


A lawsuit was filed by environmental groups to block the detonation, but the US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled on Monday that it could go ahead.


Journalist Abby Martin called it “an emergency of [the US army’s] own making because of their own negligence and disregard”. 


She told

 BreakThrough News on Tuesday

: “I just can’t wrap my mind around the fact that an industry that has a budget of over $1tn cannot incorporate a safe disposal mechanism for these toxic chemicals it is constantly manufacturing.


“I think at the end of the day, they just know they can override local governments.”


Federal officials say the detonation is needed because the degraded material could explode on its own. 


The US army initially contracted a company to chemically neutralise the weapons after it became aware of the degrading cache at a military base in March,

the New York Times reported

. However, it cancelled the deal just two months later and decided to blow up the munitions instead. 


Environmental

assessment documents

 from the US military state that while the chemical route for disposal “offered environmental protections by avoiding a blast plume, it was eliminated from detailed study due to unacceptable risk to human safety”. This was because the process required more “hands-on” handling by workers over long days.


The Department of Health and Human Services (HSS) told pregnant women, children and those with chronic illnesses

to evacuate on Tuesday

, with HHS principal deputy assistant secretary for preparedness and response saying “you definitely want to be out of that area”.


The Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown makes medium and large calibre munitions for the US Department of Defense.

title: NPA-Mindoro reports failed AFP attack, 4 gov’t casualties
content:
The New People’s Army (NPA) reported the death of four government troopers in a clash at Bulalacao, Oriental Mindoro on Monday, thwarting a 1

st

 Infantry Battalion-Philippine Army strike operation.


The NPA said a unit of its Lucio de Guzman Command successfully defended itself against the raid at its temporary encampment in Sitio Gatol, Barangay San Roque, withdrawing safely after the firefight.


An ABS-CBN report of the incident quoted 203rd Infantry Brigade-Philippine Army commander Brig. Gen. Melencio Ragudo claiming only two soldiers were wounded and are at a stable condition at a hospital. The report also stated that said the clash started at around 8:35 AM.


The NPA, however, said civilians who were at the scene after the encounter reported that four soldiers were killed. The Red army likewise refuted 1st IB’s claim that firearms and equipment were seized from the guerillas.


The NPA added that its fighters spotted the approaching soldiers and opened fire on them before they could reach the camp.NPA-Mindoro spokesperson Madaay Gasic said their latest victory against the Armed Forces of the Philippines demonstrate the Red army’s will to fight and the people’s “unwavering support.” Gasic also belied Ragudo’s claim civilians tipped off the miitary about the NPA’s presence in the area.


“The people of Bulalacao and all the people of Mindoro celebrate the heroic resistance of their army against the enemy,” Gasic said. #
