author: Unknown
title: Do you remember 17 octobre ? - Réflexions et propositions pour le mouvement
content:
Courte brochure publiée le 12 novembre dernier. Réflexions et propositions pour le mouvement.


Disponible sur :

https://sanscontrolerevolution.wordpress.com/2026/11/12/do-you-remember-17-octobre/


Les blocus lycéens continuent, malgré la propagande du gouvernement sur «

 

l'essoufflement du mouvement

 

» pour pousser à la résignation. La semaine de rentrée, des dizaines de lycées ont été bloqués, et ce malgré le changement de politique répressive visant au déblocage coûte que coûte et à l'intimidation des lycéens et les manipulations des rectorats, qui déclarent qu'un établissement n'est pas bloqué dès qu'il y a 15 élèves dedans. Les pratiques qui ont fait la radicalité des luttes lycéennes depuis septembre n'ont pas disparu. Comme avant les vacances de la Toussaint, qui auraient pu tout éteindre, des portails ont brûlé, des mortiers ont été utilisés à l'intérieur même des établissements, des proviseurs ont été attaqués, des lycées ont été incendiés comme à Toulouse ou à Lyon. Cependant, si l'on regarde ailleurs qu'aux portes des lycées, peu de choses se passent depuis le 17 octobre, ou plutôt ce qui se passe pourrait malheureusement augurer d'une lente mort de la lutte actuelle qui serait décidée par les syndicats, contentée par les quelques ajustements octroyés par l'État, tout le monde se mettant d'accord pour éteindre la conflictualité et «

 

traduire

 

» la révolte dans la bataille des urnes en 2027 (c'est-à-dire rentrer chez soi et retrouver la normalité mortifère d'avant).


Le 17 octobre a été l'occasion d'une formidable explosion de la révolte et a permis un certain élargissement de la lutte à la question de la vie quotidienne sous la domination capitaliste, que l'on pourrait résumer ainsi : toujours plus d'exploitation, toujours plus d'autorité, toujours moins de thunes pour vivre. Ce jour a signifié l'entrée en lutte de nombreuses personnes, donnant une nouvelle ampleur aux luttes initiées par les lycéens, et a témoigné d'un débordement considérable de l'encadrement externe (le maintien de l'ordre) et interne (syndicats, partis, pacificateurs démocrates). Depuis, lors des jours de mobilisations, il est compliqué de retrouver l'énergie dévastatrice du 17 qui s'était déversée sans contrôle dans les rues. Le 24 et le 31 ont été l'occasion pour l'État de montrer les muscles et pour la gauche de reprendre globalement le contrôle sur le mouvement en assignant tout le monde au calme et à la discipline. Le 5 novembre et le 7 novembre n'ont pas été différent. À part quelques affrontements et barricades ne sortant pas vraiment de la normale, les manifs partout en France ont été bien tenues ou rendues presque complètement inoffensives. Il semble que le 17 octobre a été un point de bascule dans la gestion du maintien de l'ordre. Après avoir tenté d'enterrer le mouvement à petit feu par les fermetures administratives de lycées et de facs et les manifs perlées, l'État a opté depuis cette date pour la force brute en réprimant tout azimut. En plus de la répression judiciaire extrêmement ferme, les flics sont envoyés en nombre devant les lycées pour débloquer à tout prix et intimider, les occupations étudiantes sont délogées très rapidement et les manifs servent de démonstration de force avec leurs lots d'interpellations massives et de tabassages. Le but est clair, il est toujours le même : faire peur à tout le monde, créer le sentiment d'impuissance et faire rentrer tout le monde chez soi. Mais il est clair que ces tactiques de masquages qui confinent à la méthode Coué («

 

plus que 20 lycées bloqués sur l'ensemble du territoire

 

» quand chacun d'entre nous en connait déjà une vingtaine) n'ont qu'un temps et doivent avoir une efficacité immédiate sur le retour à la normale, sinon ça se voit. La vitalité du mouvement lycéen peut facilement les déjouer… mais encore faut-il pour cela qu'il perdure et s'amplifie.


Hors des lycées, l'essentiel de la mobilisation se passe aujourd'hui dans les manifs syndicales, depuis que le mouvement a été réduit à ce que l'on connaît classiquement des mouvements sociaux portés par la gauche. Ces manifestations à intervalles définis sont sérieusement encadrées et régulées efficacement par la police. Les appels sur les réseaux sociaux à aller dans d'autres endroits que les points de rassemblements déclarés légalement sont des échecs. universités populaires

author: Unknown
title: Stains : non à la “classe défense” et à ses dérives au collège Joliot Curie
content:
Communiqué des personnels du collège Joliot Curie de Stains, mobilisé⋅es contre la “classe défense et sécurité globales”, le 24 novembre 2026


Jusqu'à preuve du contraire, utiliser une arme factice ou faire du collège une officine de recrutement de l'armée ne font pas partie des missions de l'école. C'est pourtant ce qu'ont vécu nos élèves de quatrième lors d'un atelier organisé dans le cadre du dispositif “classe de défense et de sécurité globales”.


Le 5 novembre 2026, au Fort de l'Est à Saint-Denis, nos élèves ont participé à des ateliers dits “pédagogiques” au cours desquels ils ont été mis en situation de guerre, affublés de fusils d'assaut factices et jetant des cailloux “comme si c'étaient des bombes”, leur a-t-on dit, entre deux remarques ordurières prononcées par des encadrants militaires telle que : “vous me faites chier avec vos wesh”.


Pendant ces ateliers, certain-es élèves n'étaient même pas encadré-es par des enseignant-es de notre collège. À la fin de la session, le colonel de la caserne a cru bon de leur déclarer qu'il les considérait comme de “probables futures recrues”.


Mais beaucoup plus grave, un de nos élèves a été victime d'une agression raciste négrophobe. Une encadrante lui a dit en le voyant : “Toi, tu as une bonne tête à servir”.


Les faits sont d'une extrême gravité. Ils nous indignent et nous révoltent. En aucun cas, nous ne pouvons ni n'avons le droit de mettre nos élèves en danger.


À l'heure où les discours suprémacistes prospèrent, à l'heure où un racisme décomplexé – pourtant puni par le code pénal – se donne des airs d'opinion, à l'heure où l'armée est davantage financée que l'école, à l'heure où les seules réponses apportées à une jeunesse qui doute, à une jeunesse qui s'inquiète pour son avenir, sont un pouvoir brutal et des dogmes autoritaires, nous refusons la militarisation de la jeunesse. Nous rappellerons que cette même institution (avec parmi elle, les escadrons de gendarmerie mobile, le

GIGN

 – groupe d'intervention de la gendarmerie nationale, les militaires de l'opération «

 

Sentinelle

 

») est en train de réprimer les lycéens et lycéennes qui revendiquent des conditions de travail décentes, en les mutilant et les blessant avec des armes de guerre (

LBD

, grenades de désencerclement, gaz lacrymogènes).


Des élus et des médecins ont d'ailleurs très récemment mis en garde l'opinion, et notamment l'Assemblée nationale, sur les troubles gynécologiques de long terme provoqués par les gaz lacrymogènes utilisés massivement contre des enfants depuis le début de la mobilisation lycéenne.


Quelle est donc cette logique absurde, d'une hypocrisie insoutenable, qui punit un élève quand il utilise un pétard, qui le mutile quand il réclame qu'on respecte ses droits, mais qui l'entraîne au combat militaire lors d'ateliers qui ressemblent à la guerre

 

?


En tant que personnels de l'éducation, nous affirmons que nos élèves ne doivent pas être formé-es à l'obéissance et au sacrifice. Ils n'ont pas à subir le racisme, le sexisme, les insultes d'une institution qui les maltraite en dehors de l'école.


C'est pour toutes ces raisons que nous, personnels du collège Joliot Curie de Stains mobilisés contre la classe défense, demandons la fermeture immédiate du dispositif, ainsi qu'une enquête sur les violences verbales et l'insulte raciste dont nos élèves ont été victimes.


Source :

title: ‘Trump Out 9’ freed after prolonged detention following protests
content:
8 of Trump Out 9 outside MPD upon their release. Photo from Anakbayan

“Last detained minor is free at last!” Salinlahi Alliance for Children’s Concerns” said in a statement, November 23, following the release of one of the minors last to be freed among the activists violently and arbitrarily arrested at Liwasang Bonifacio, dubbed the “Trump Out 9.”

Salinlahi said a release order for the nine detainees—including J, who is a minor—had already been issued as early as Friday, November 20. The group said, however, that his release “was delayed due to harassment and stonewalling from the Manila Youth Reception Center.”

After nearly five days in detention, eight of the nine youth activists and workers collectively known as the “Trump Out 9” were initially released on bail from the Manila Police District (MPD) on November 20.

The first three to be released were Philippine Normal University (PNU) youth activist Hizeno Aquino, Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) member Domingo Marbid Jr., and Alliance of Concerned Teachers (ACT) volunteer Ronald Artiaga, who were freed without charges. Five others were released on bail: Anakbayan National member William Dela Cruz, Ernanie Rafael of the commuters’ network PARA, PISTON member Cerillo Latoreno, KMU member Carla Nicoyco, and Tambisan sa Sining Novaliches Chairperson Peter John Charles Versoza.

In a statement, Anakbayan welcomed the release of Dela Cruz and seven others. “Anakbayan salutes the release of the Trump Out 9, which includes youth leader William Dela Cruz. This is the result of the people’s collective action to free victims of fascism under the Marcos regime,” the group said.

The youth organization also stressed that while the Trump Out 9 were released, the fight for justice continues. “Even though the Trump Out 9 are now free, this does not absolve the PNP of the crimes it committed. Videos clearly show people being dragged, beaten, and illegally arrested while protesting against Pax Silica and Marcos’s subservience to Trump.”

The minor, J, had been detained at the Manila Youth Reception Center (MYRC) for more than a week.

Alliance of Nationalist and Genuine Labor Organizations (ANGLO) staff Lance Vicher recalled the minor’s dedication to forwarding workers’ rights in an online post. “I still remember: you approached us on May 1 asking for a discussion on the condition of workers. You wanted to organize workers, and when I asked if you were sure, you said, ‘Determination always comes before readiness.’”

Salinlahi Alliance for Children’s Concerns denounced J’s continued detention, demanding that he be released immediately. Moreover, the alliance stressed that quarantine must never be used as an excuse to deprive a child of liberty, legal assistance, and contact with their family, citing Article 37 of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC), which states that detention be used only as a last resort and for the shortest appropriate period, with prompt access to legal assistance.

Kalipunan ng Demokratikong Kabataan (KDK) also decried MYRC’s delaying tactic, “Even though the documents for J’s release are already complete, MYRC claimed it is not possible because there is no officer-in-charge (OIC) to sign today—the same excuse they have been giving every day for the past few days.”

Footage circulating online shows that the nine activists were brutally and unlawfully apprehended during the November 15 Working People’s March at Liwasang Bonifacio, where labor and youth groups had gathered as part of ongoing protests against the impending signing of the U.S.-led Pax Silica initiative during the 49th ASEAN Summit.

In a Facebook post, Zairine Latoreno, daughter of Cerilo, one of the Trump Out 9, decried the forceful arrest of his father, who was inside an L300 vehicle. “Manila police forcibly arrested my father right inside the L300 and towed it. They carried him as if he weren’t human, treating him as if he had killed someone—as if he were one of those who stole from the Filipino people.” After her father was taken out of the vehicle and carried to the police mobile, the police towed the L300.

Zairine also stressed that police forces prevented them from immediately accessing Latoreno and providing medicine for his hypertension. This directly violates Republic Act No. 7438, or the Rights of Persons Arrested, Detained, or Under Custodial Investigation, which indicates that “Any person arrested or detained or under custodial investigation shall be allowed visits by or …

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 26 novembre
content:
Humeur combative pour ce 26 novembre de l'éphéméride des luttes, aux quatre coins du globe. Il faut dire qu'on est bien déterminé-e-s à ne pas se laisser faire.


1920 :

 En Ukraine, les bolcheviks rompent leur seconde alliance avec Makhno, et l'armée rouge attaque Goulai-Polé, siège de la Maknovtchina, mais Makhno réussira à s'enfuir.


1927 :

 A Buenos Aires, l'anarchiste Italien Severino Di Giovanni fait sauter l'usine de cigarettes Combinados. Celle-ci avait lancé une nouvelle cigarette « pour ouvriers » qu'elle avait nommée la « Sacco et Vanzetti » (trois jours plus tôt, les deux anarchistes de Boston avaient été exécutés sur la chais électrique) afin de plaire tout de suite et d'économiser des frais d'électricité.


1970 :

 La Nouvelle Résistance Populaire (liée à la Gauche Prolétarienne) enlève le député Michel De Grailly, instigateur de nombreuses lois répressives et idéologue de la Cour de Sûreté de l'État.


1972 :

 A Dublin, probablement l'IRA fait sauter une bombe à l'extérieur du cinéma Film Centre vers 1h30 du matin.


1977 :

 A Paris, manifestation contre l'expulsion des squats du 14e arrondissement : 1000


personnes dont 300 autonomes : un squat expulsé est démuré, le siège de la SEMIREP et un car de police sont incendiés.


1978 :

 A Belfast, Albert Miles, responsable de la prison de Crumlin Road, est abattu devant chez lui par l'IRA.


1981 :

 A Garac (Gers), le Mouvement d'action révolutionnaire antinucléaire (MARAN) fait sauter un relais hertzien des PTT.


1983 :

 A Toulouse, le CLODO (Comité Liquidant et Détournant les Ordinateurs), composé de 'travailleurs de l'informatique', incendie les locaux de Speery Univac Ordinateur.


1984 :

 A Bierset, près de Liège, les Cellules Communistes Combattantes (CCC) font sauter deux pylônes et leurs installations au sol d'un centre de télécommunications de la base aérienne, qui accueille les chasseurs-bombardiers de l'OTAN.


2010 :

 A Rio de Janeiro, plus de 21.000 policiers surarmés investissent plusieurs favelas de la ville dans le but de les "pacifier", accompagnés de véhicules blindés et de soldats. Au moins 49 personnes sont tuées par balles au cours des plusieurs jours que dure cette "opération".


2013 :

 A Tegucigalpa, capitale hondurienne, des affrontements violents éclatent dans le cadre d'une lutte étudiante contre des résultats électoraux falsifiés.


2014 :

 Au Chili, dans la province de Talagante près de Santiago, le 'Groupe Anarchiste Coordonné (GAC) - Bande Organisée Mauricio Morales / Cellule Incendiaire Sebastián Oversluij' bloque des voies ferrées avec de gros rochers et des pneus incendiés en solidarité avec les anarchistes Tamara Sol Farías et Sebastián Oversluij.


2015 :

 A Tlanepantla dans la province de Puebla au Mexique, une manifestation a lieu contre le maire et sa politique. Rapidement, la manifestation tourne à l'affrontement contre la police venue réprimer la grogne, des molotovs font leur apparition et plusieurs véhicules du maire sont incendiés.


 A Maracaibo au Venezuela, c'est un bus qui est brûlé par un groupe de manifestant-e-s masqué-e-s lors d'une protestation.


2019 :

 A Buenos Aires, des anarchistes incendient une patrouille de police en plein coeur de la nuit.


Voir également

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 26 novembre.

author: Sara Connors
title: Yukon to review worksheet asking students about ‘positives’ of residential school
content:
A worksheet asking high school students in Whitehorse to identify the positives of residential schools has attracted public criticism, prompting the Yukon Department of Education to commit to a curriculum review.


A photo of the worksheet was circulated on social media late last month. The department confirmed in an email to APTN News that the worksheet was part of a Grade 10 teaching resource made available to Yukon schools in October 2024.


The person who shared the photo declined to speak with APTN, but said it came from a high school assignment at a Whitehorse school.


The worksheet includes two experiences shared by residential school survivors whose names are blacked out.


One question asks how some survivors, like one who attended the Carcross residential school, “insist that although there were unquestionably a lot of negative experiences at these schools, there were also many positives. What do you think were some of the positive aspects of residential school?”


Another question quotes a survivor from the Northwest Territories and asks: “To what extent do you think the positive parts of Indian residential school need to be part of what people learn about?”


The questions came as a shock to Francis van Kessel, who is Teslin Tlingit.


“I don’t think we talk about the Holocaust in a positive way because we shouldn’t. So why are we talking about residential schools in a positive [way]?” she said.


van Kessel said her mother and grandmother attended residential school, the wounds of which continue to impact her and her family.


She described the questions as insensitive and dismissive of survivor’s experiences, prompting her to write

a seven-page letter

 to the territory’s education minister demanding the questions be removed, a review of how residential school material is taught and mandatory professional development for educators, among other things.


“There’s no positives in genocide,” she said. “This brought up a lot of emotion for myself, so I’m sure it brings up a lot of emotion in other people. This isn’t the way to teach children about history.”


Francis van Kessel, a descendant of residential school survivors, says she’s hurt by the questions and found them offensive. Photo: Jordan Haslbeck


Yukon NDP MLA and education critic Linda Moen said the questions minimize the harms of residential schools.


She raised her concern with the document in the legislature this month, arguing the questions echo residential school denialism.


“First thing I thought was the lack of empathy, lack of compassion. I think we’re just not there yet as Yukoners and Canadians to start discussing if there were any positive aspects to residential school,” she said.


A Kwanlin Dün First Nation citizen and the daughter of a residential school survivor, she said the questions hit close to home.


“That’s not the narrative that I was given through my entire lifetime, so when I see people being taught in school—schools are there to educate. So, let’s educate the truth,” she said.


Yukon NDP MLA and education critic Linda Moen says the broader community isn’t ready to discuss the positives of residential schools. Photo: Submitted by the Yukon NDP


Melanie Bennett, executive director of the Yukon First Nation Education Directorate (YFNED), said in a statement that the worksheet is a curriculum document that was used as a guide by a Yukon teacher and was “developed with First Nations approval.”


She said that a small number of Elders have shared positive experiences, which were quoted in the document, but warned that “by no means should these rare experiences provide justification for an argument that there were ‘some positive aspects of residential schools’ to quote the school test under scrutiny.”


“YFNED urges educators to not weigh the pros and cons side-by side, equally,” she said. “The overall negative impact of Residential Schools is so completely negative, attempting to destroy language, culture and families, that even if a child experienced loving care or positive educational experiences at residential school, they were still victims of this wholly negative attempt at cultural genocide.”


Survivor says there’s room for nuance


But for Joanne Henry, a residential school survivor and the executive director of the Committee on Abuse in Residential Schools (CAIRS), which helped develop the curriculum on residential schools, the question deserves nuance.


She said the curriculum was designed to pair classroom …

author: Unknown
title: YPJ: We will continue our struggle against all forms of violence every single day
content:
The General Command of the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ) released a statement marking the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women.


The YPJ statement on Wednesday includes the following:


“​On the occasion of November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, we affirm that violence against women is neither an individual issue, a family matter, nor a passing incident; rather, it is a systematic phenomenon fed by authoritarian mentalities, regressive traditions, and policies that deprive women of their right to make decisions freely, control their own bodies, and determine the course of their lives. At their core, these practices aim to silence women’s will, subjugate them, and destroy their identity. Guided by this reality, we assert that protecting women is a fundamental, non-negotiable duty—one that is not limited to the military sphere, but encompasses social, psychological, legal, and moral dimensions as well.


​Our struggle against violence perpetrated against women is rooted in the very essence of our existence and identity. This struggle manifests in protecting female survivors of domestic violence, opposing forced marriage, combating so-called honor crimes, and rescuing women abducted and enslaved by terrorist groups—alongside raising societal awareness, promoting women’s education, and working to build a system that empowers women to defend themselves, voice their demands, seek justice, and make their own decisions with freedom and independence. We do not view this struggle as a temporary duty tied to a specific phase; rather, we consider it a permanent covenant, sealed with the blood of female martyrs.


​We emphasize that violence is not confined to physical assault and murder alone, but also includes silencing women, restricting their freedoms, depriving them of education, work, and participation in social life, subjecting them to psychological pressure, and denying their will and right to self-determination. All forms of violence stem from a single mentality and strive toward a single goal; therefore, all of them must be confronted with the exact same resolve and responsibility. Silence in the face of violence is, in itself, part of the violence.


​We call upon all women to safeguard and fiercely defend their dignity, placing it above all else. A woman’s dignity and freedom are no less vital than water and food; indeed, a life in which a woman is stripped of her dignity and will can never be a free life. We urge women not to isolate themselves or remain silent in the face of violence, and to hold fast to their will and defend their rights. We also stress the necessity for women to unite in confronting the mentality that imposes violence and domination upon them, for only through women’s unity can we defeat this mindset and build a free and just society. Women’s strength lies in their unity and solidarity, and they must recognize this power and harness it to defend their freedom and dignity.


​At the same time, we call upon society as a whole, legal institutions, and all forces that believe in freedom and equality to shoulder their responsibilities in protecting women and defending their rights and dignity. A society in which women do not enjoy freedom can never be a free society, and a society in which women are subjected to violence is a society whose present and future are under threat.


​Finally, we declare that we will continue our struggle against all forms of violence perpetrated against women—not only on November 25, but every single day and in every moment of our lives, with determination, dedication, and faith in women’s freedom. This struggle will persist until the day arrives when no woman is subjected to violence simply for being a woman, and until all women are able to live in freedom, dignity, and safety, far removed from fear and oppression.

”

author: Unknown
title: MSD: Protecting women’s rights requires explicit constitutional and legal guarantees
content:
The Syrian Democratic Council (MSD) released a statement marking the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women as Syrian women look toward a future that ends decades of systemic abuse.


This moment calls for a new chapter built on justice, full equality, and human dignity, said the MSD statement on November 25, which included the following:


“Violence against women extends far beyond murder, abduction, exploitation, and overt discrimination. It includes systematic marginalization and exclusion from leadership roles. Denying women an active voice in political decision-making and public governance is a direct form of violence that must be confronted.


Despite the political transition following December 8, 2024, conditions for Syrian women have deteriorated due to ongoing discriminatory policies. The transitional government and society at large must urgently reassess their approach to women’s rights. We need genuine gender justice in practice—not merely symbolic gestures for the media.


Protecting and sustaining women’s rights requires explicit constitutional and legal guarantees. These frameworks must ensure full equality and safeguard the hard-won gains of Syrian women against any rollback, regardless of the pretext.


Achieving transitional justice is essential to delivering redress for women, who represent a disproportionate share of the Syrian conflict’s victims. This process requires uncovering the fate of abducted and forcibly disappeared women, holding perpetrators accountable, providing reparations, and guaranteeing non-recurrence.


The MSD reaffirms that building a democratic and just Syria is impossible without women serving as equal partners in shaping the nation’s future. Their active leadership is vital to national reconciliation and the reconstruction of both state institutions and society. Women are not merely beneficiaries of peace; they are essential partners in forging and sustaining it.”

author: Unknown
title: HPJ vows to continue their struggle for all women in Iran and the Middle East
content:
The East Kurdistan Women’s Defense Forces (HPJ) issued a written statement on the occasion of November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Referring to attacks against women, the statement said that the patriarchal system aims to strip women of their identity and will and to keep them under oppression in every sphere of life.


In its statement on Wednesday, the HPJ Command said, “The state system, built on the denial and destruction of women, has turned every sphere of life into a genocide against women through a patriarchal mentality for 30,000 years. Women, who created language, culture, defense, and education, have been reduced to a state of voicelessness and defenselessness.”


‘Women are the first to be exploited for the interests of the system and capital’


The HPJ Command pointed out that the system of capitalist modernity is patriarchal and that women were the first gender to be exploited for the interests of the system and capital.


“In reality, the oppression of women means the oppression and subjugation of society and every individual within it. All forms of violence against women are carried out through an organized and ideological system targeting society. Within the three-tiered system, harassment, rape, and massacres of women in the workplace and family, which have been sanctified by men, have reached the level of genocide,” the statement said.


The statement said the 21st century has witnessed the rise of the women’s liberation revolution, noting that women’s struggle against systematic oppression and the attempts to strip them of their identity has spread to different parts of the world.


‘Women must organize and educate themselves’


HPPJ remarked that the struggle waged by women in East Kurdistan against executions, killings, imprisonment, and attacks on women’s bodies has become a source of inspiration for women around the world. Attacks on women’s will and ideas constitute the gravest forms of aggression, it added.


Emphasizing that the killing of women and the suppression of their will amount to the destruction of society and its collective will, the statement issued the following call:


“In response to the executions, imprisonment, and violence carried out in the prisons of the Iranian regime, women must organize and educate themselves and defend society’s will and identity through women’s unity, based on the Manifesto for Peace and Democratic Society and the philosophy of ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’ (Woman, Life, Freedom). A woman who is united with her organization is a woman who has gained free will and the power of self-defense.”


‘All women will become a force of defense for themselves and society’


The HPJ declared that, as the defense force of women in East Kurdistan, they would continue their struggle not only for women in East Kurdistan but also for all women in Iran and the Middle East.


The statement concluded, “We will continue our struggle to achieve women’s freedom and free will on the basis of Leader Abdullah Öcalan’s philosophy and ideology. Through the example of the women of East Kurdistan, all women around the world will establish their own free communes based on free will, thought, and life, and become a force of defense for themselves and society.”

title: Gorran: The constitutional and shared responsibilities of KRI authorities must be recognized
content:
In an attempt to take control of border crossings and oil fields in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI) and the disputed territories, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Tuesday that all border crossings in the Kurdistan region be placed under the authority of the federal border crossings agency and that Baghdad’s powers over oil production and the export of petroleum products be expanded.


According to Sabah al-Numan, spokesperson for the prime minister and commander-in-chief of the Iraqi armed forces, the Kurdistan Regional Government will henceforth be required to process export permits for crude oil and petroleum products exclusively through the Federal Ministry of Oil. Baghdad is thus asserting greater control over the region’s oil trade.


The Gorran Movement issued a written statement regarding Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s decisions and emphasized that combating corruption and resolving problems must not be used as a justification for violating constitutional powers.


Stressing that the region’s constitutional powers must not be weakened and that the position of the Kurds in Iraq’s new political landscape must not be overlooked, the statement called on the Iraqi Federal Government to reconsider the decisions in full coordination with the Kurdistan Regional Government.


The statement noted that the constitution must serve as the basis for resolving disputes and emphasized that the constitutional and shared responsibilities of regional authorities must be recognized, particularly in the management of the energy, oil, and natural gas sectors.


The Gorran Movement stated that it would not accept the use of anti-corruption efforts as a justification for violating the constitutional rights of the people of Kurdistan, describing Baghdad’s recent steps as a warning.


“Baghdad’s actions are a warning bell. Internal divisions, the weakness of national institutions, and the absence of good governance have undermined the status of the Kurdistan Region and led to an erosion of constitutional rights,” the statement said.


The Gorran Movement called on political forces and parties in Kurdistan to come together as soon as possible and set aside secondary disputes. It emphasized the need to develop a unified national strategy to protect the constitutional rights of the people of Kurdistan through a common stance.

author: Unknown
title: Varisheh Moradi: No policy of attrition can shake the foundations of our commitment
content:
Kurdish political prisoner Varisheh Moradi, who has been sentenced to death in Iran for the second time and is held in Evin Prison, wrote a letter on the occasion of November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.


The letter penned by the Kurdish activist reads as follows:


“Systematic violence is an interconnected structure that begins within the home and extends into the public sphere. Yet, in its most blatant manifestation as state violence, it imposes itself through policies of elimination and denial, intimidation, censorship, repression, and detention, reaching its peak in execution. Meanwhile, through economic pressure, the shrinking of people’s means of subsistence, and under the shadow of war and its consequences, those in power have effectively placed a noose around the neck of society as a whole. Although the death sentence has been issued against me personally, this noose is tightening around everyone’s throat, casting the shadow of an imposed death over all of the society. I see the issuance of a death sentence for the second time as an attempt to turn time into an instrument of subjugation, replacing the “possibility of living” with the “anticipation of death.” Yet those in power fail to realize that the foundations of my commitment, and ours, to our historical and intellectual choices are so firmly established that no policy of attrition can shake them.


Against this backdrop, the shadow of war has significantly increased the number of suicides and killings of women across all regions of Iran. In a land whose historical memory is intertwined with narratives of goddesses and divine beings, how have we reached a point where women’s bodies and very existence have become objects of control, possession, and violation in the social sphere, while their independent will leads to their elimination in the political arena? Both have the same root: a patriarchal mentality sustained by the interconnected forces of power, hierarchy, and domination over women, which cannot tolerate the presence in politics of a woman who possesses her own will and has attained self-awareness. This system of thought fears women’s power and the truth of their existence because a conscious woman breaks free from the position of being possessed and objectified, questioning and challenging forms of authority and the foundations of domination.


For this reason, various labels are used to drive women out of social, political, and economic spheres. In politics, they call us “rebels” so that we may be sentenced to death, while in society, under the guise of tradition, they label crimes as “honor killings” to legitimize the same approach. Yet no force or system has the right to monopolize the power to define and name. By what standards and according to which moral values are these names and labels defined, and who has granted themselves such authority?


Nevertheless, the very fact that news of these crimes and femicides no longer remains hidden and shrouded in silence, as it once did, is itself a step forward and the result of years of struggle and perseverance. For years, attempts were made to portray violence against women as a private matter. But this violence is by no means a private matter. It always has psychological, physical, and structural dimensions and is not an individual problem but a collective one, a concern for society as a whole.


Confronting such a structure requires a continuous and comprehensive struggle against violence against women, one that extends from the home into the public sphere through breaking the silence, speaking out, criticizing and challenging mechanisms of domination, and seeking ways to resist them. This resistance is not the work of one individual or one woman, but the collective will and movement of all women.


For in the essence of “Woman, Life, Freedom,” “woman” is not a figure of submission and subordination, but the creative and liberating force of society. “Life,” in opposition to the culture of death and repression, means living with dignity and awareness. And “freedom” can only be achieved by dismantling every form of oppression and domination.


The struggle against violence against women is a defense of women themselves, a safeguarding of the meaning of life, and an opening of the path to freedom for society as a whole.


Jin, Jiyan, Azadî


Varisha Moradi – Women’s Ward, Evin Prison


November 25, 2026”

author: Unknown
title: “Let’s Talk Manifesto”: Internationalist women in Rojava launch podcast
content:
With “Let’s Talk Manifesto,” young women from the Internationalist Commune in Rojava have launched a new podcast project. The initiative is rooted in a collective engagement with the Manifesto of Democratic Communal Society by Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan. The internationalist women aim to connect the perspectives developed in the manifesto with their own experiences of the Rojava Revolution and the realities of women’s lives in different parts of the world.


In each episode, the young women focus on a chapter of the manifesto, discuss its theoretical approaches, and explore how these can be translated into social practice. The aim is to create a shared space for learning, reflection, and political discussion across national borders.


In the tradition of the international women’s struggle


The publication date was deliberately chosen. On November 25, 1960, the Mirabal sisters were murdered in the Dominican Republic for their resistance to the dictatorship of Rafael Trujillo. In 1981, feminist movements from the Caribbean and Abya Yala declared the anniversary of their murder a day of struggle against violence against women. Today, women around the world take to the streets to protest patriarchal violence, commemorate murdered women, and carry on their struggles.


The young internationalist women also situate their project within this tradition. In their statement announcing the podcast’s launch, they draw a connection between the deepening crises of capitalist modernity, the destruction of the foundations of social life, and attacks on the organized women’s movement. “We see that women who organize, unite, and struggle for a different life are the first to become targets of attacks. This is because their organizing poses a fundamental threat to the existing patriarchal and capitalist order,” the internationalist women stated.


Collective education as a practice of self-defense


The podcast draws on the comprehensive understanding of self-defense developed by the Kurdish women’s movement, which goes beyond protection against physical attacks to encompass the acquisition of knowledge, collective education, and social organizing. “As young women in particular, we can develop perspectives, devise solutions, and contribute to building a new society. In this sense, self-defense also means developing the ability to shape one’s own living conditions autonomously,” the initiators say.


From theoretical engagement to social practice


The internationalist women view the Manifesto of Democratic Communal Society as a potential response to the current global crisis. Through their podcast, they aim to deepen discussions about alternative forms of social coexistence and make them accessible beyond Rojava. “Our podcast, ‘Let’s Talk Manifesto,’ is an invitation to read, question, and discuss together and, above all, to put the ideas developed into practice. Because a different society does not emerge on its own. It emerges wherever people come together, learn from one another, and begin to organize their lives collectively.”


A new episode of “Let’s Talk Manifesto” is released every Wednesday on

Spotify

. Further information about the project is available on the

Internationalist Commune’s website

and

Instagram account

.

author: Natália Perez
title: Fim anticlimático da COP31 traz também um ganho para a humanidade, defende Claudio Angelo
content:
Dizer não a um acordo ruim é uma boa decisão? Essa é a pergunta que fica depois do fim da 31ª Conferência do Clima das Nações Unidas (COP31), o principal evento do mundo para discutir os esforços para conter o aquecimento global e as mudanças climáticas.


Para Claudio Angelo, que é coordenador de política internacional do Observatório do Clima e já acompanhou catorze COPs, dizer não à proposta apresentada pela presidência da conferência foi muito importante. Na verdade, até positivo.


“Isso foi o resultado mais positivo dessa COP e teve uma importância muito maior do que muita gente poderia imaginar […] Esse texto vai ser rejeitado, o lugar dele é a lata de lixo da história, e vocês não me venham aqui em outra COP, na qual vocês não estejam prontos para falar de combustível fóssil, porque essa é a única coisa que importa”, diz, explicando porque países em desenvolvimento e até mesmo europeus optaram por recusar a carta final do evento. O Brasil não se opôs nem defendeu o texto, se omitiu.


A visão de Angelo destoa de como muitas manchetes chamaram o

fim da COP31

, com veículos adjetivando o resultado como frustrante. A conferência foi presidida pela Turquia, com a Austrália sendo a presidente das negociações. O texto final deixava de fora o mapa do caminho para fim do uso dos combustíveis fósseis, que foi

defendido

 pelo Brasil na COP 30, em Belém, no ano passado. O uso desses combustíveis, a sua queima, são os principais causadores do aquecimento global no mundo.


Angelo entende que mais do que vilanizar determinados países, é preciso entender como funcionam negociações multilaterais como a COP, e suas complexidades.


“Não dá para ser muito maniqueísta em relação às COPs, porque todos os países têm interesses e frequentemente alguns deles estarão alinhados entre si, têm um ponto da negociação, e outros serão inimigos em outro ponto da negociação […] A verdade é que quem quer salvar o planeta é a Greta. Os países querem se salvar, se salvar das decisões da COP. Então, eles vão lá, sobretudo para se proteger. Isso os torna heróis em alguns lugares, vilões em outros, omissos em outros, e é assim que a coisa funciona no multilateralismo.”


Na entrevista para o podcast da

Agência Pública


Bom dia Fim do Mundo

, Angelo ressalta a importância das decisões da COP 30 em Belém, e também aponta os limites dessas conferências, até mesmo frente ao lobby do petróleo, que avança sobre governos dentro e fora desses espaços.


Apesar das dificuldades, Angelo acredita que o “não” no fim da COP31 reforça que, nos próximos eventos, não será possível fechar qualquer acordo sem colocar o fim dos combustíveis fósseis na balança. “Posso ser inocente, otimista demais, mas eu acho que está ficando muito mais difícil – e depois de Antalya [Turquia], vai ficar praticamente impossível — fazer uma conferência do clima que não trate de combustível fóssil. E isso é um ganho imenso para a humanidade.”


Leia a entrevista abaixo:


A COP31 acabou com uma decisão consensual, classificada por muitos como um fracasso. Por outro lado, muita gente também avaliou que seria pior ter acatado o texto político principal da COP, proposto pela co-presidência turco-australiana. O que estava na mesa dessa discussão e qual o significado da rejeição dessa decisão?


A COP31 foi ruim o suficiente, não foi só a decisão de capa [o texto político principal] que foi ruim. Houve problemas também nos trilhos formais de negociação: a gente teve uma decisão sobre financiamento que poderia ter sido melhor, não vimos explicitado, por exemplo, o jeito como a triplicação do financiamento à adaptação vai acontecer.


Os países em desenvolvimento e a sociedade civil estavam demandando 120 bilhões de dólares por ano, e um plano de entrega desse dinheiro. Isso não aconteceu por causa dos países desenvolvidos que chegaram em Antalya com uma determinação a não falar de dinheiro. E que é muito fácil para eles chegar com esse tipo de determinação, porque é aquela coisa: “devo, não pago, nego enquanto puder”.


Também por conta da resistência dos países desenvolvidos a gente terminou com uma decisão pior no chamado mecanismo de transição justa. Esse mecanismo foi criado na COP 30 em Belém, e precisaria ser formatado e operacionalizado agora em Antalya. Isso não aconteceu porque os países desenvolvidos não estão prontos para ter nenhuma nova instituição funcionando debaixo das Nações Unidas, para que eles não sejam chamados a colaborar financeiramente, manter …

title: TBMM'de HGS önergesi AKP ve MHP oylarıyla reddedildi
content:
Yeni Yol Grubu’nun Hızlı Geçiş Sistemi’ndeki (HGS) tahsilat ve bildirim sorunları, icra süreçleri ve otoyol işletmecilerinin görevlendirdiği hukuk büroları hakkındaki iddiaların araştırılması için verdiği önerge, AKP ve MHP milletvekillerinin oylarıyla reddedildi.

Önerinin gerekçesini açıklayan Yeni Yol Grubu Muğla Milletvekili Selçuk Özdağ, geçiş ücretleri tahsil edilemeyen ya da borçları sisteme geç yansıyan sürücülerin aylar sonra yüksek tutarlı icra bildirimleriyle karşılaştığını söyledi. Özdağ, 1.000 liralık geçiş borcunun 6.385 liraya, 70 bin liralık borcun ise 800 bin liraya çıktığı örneklerini verdi.

Vatandaşlara 15 günlük ödeme süresi tanındığını ancak bu dönemde borçların e-Devlet’te görünmediğini veya bildirim yapılmadığını belirten Özdağ, PTT ve şirketlerin bildirim yükümlülüklerini yerine getirmediğini söyledi. Bakanın 2025’te 25 bin dosyanın incelendiği yönündeki açıklamasını eleştiren Özdağ, HGS borçları nedeniyle başlatılan icra takiplerini yürüten avukatların kim olduğunun ve siyasi bağlantılarının açıklanmasını istedi.

Özdağ, önergenin kapsamına hatalı tahsilatların ve iadelerin yanı sıra otoyol işletmecilerinin hukuk bürolarını görevlendirme usullerinin ve siyasi nüfuz iddialarının da girdiğini belirtti. Meclis araştırması önergesi, Genel Kurul’daki oylamada AKP ve MHP'lilerin oylarıyla reddedildi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: TÜMTİS’ten 29 Kasım çağrısı: “Ortak sorunlarımız etrafında mücadeleyi büyütmek zorundayız”
content:
DİSK’e bağlı 14 sendikanın çağrısıyla 29 Kasım Pazar günü İstanbul Kartal Meydanı’nda “Yoksulluğa, yolsuzluğa ve emperyalist savaşa karşı adalet, ekmek, özgürlük” mitingi yapılacak. Saat 12.00’de toplanılacak, miting 13.00’te başlayacak.

TÜMTİS İstanbul 1 No’lu Şube Başkanı Ersin Türkmen,29 Kasım mitingine çağrı yaparak işçilerin düşük ücret, ağır vergi yükü, hayat pahalılığı ve gelir adaletsizliğiyle karşı karşıya olduğunu söyledi. Türkmen, “Ülkenin bütün zenginliğini üreten işçiler, ürettikleri değerden hak ettikleri payı alamıyor. Vergi yükü emekçinin sırtına yüklenirken sermayeye sağlanan teşvikler ve ayrıcalıklar devam ediyor” dedi.

2027 bütçesinin işçi, emekçi, yoksul ve emeklilerin ihtiyaçlarını esas alması gerektiğini vurgulayan Türkmen, “Bizler bu düzenin değişmesi gerektiğini söylüyoruz” dedi.

Farklı konfederasyonlara bağlı sendikaların ve emek örgütlerinin bir araya gelmesinin önemine dikkat çeken Türkmen, “Sendikal ayrılıkları, farklı örgütsel yapıları bir kenara bırakarak ortak sorunlarımız etrafında mücadeleyi büyütmek zorundayız” dedi. Vergide adalet, gelir dağılımında eşitlik, insanca yaşam, örgütlenmenin önündeki engellerin kaldırılması, güvenceli çalışma ve iş cinayetlerinin son bulmasının ortak talepler olduğunu belirtti.

“Emeğin sömürülmediği, işçilerin insanca yaşayabildiği bir düzen için mücadele etmeye devam edeceğiz” diyen Türkmen, TÜMTİS İstanbul 1 No’lu Şube olarak üyeleriyle birlikte 29 Kasım’da Kartal’da olacaklarını ve taleplerini güçlü biçimde dile getireceklerini söyledi.

author: Unknown
title: Ahmet Saymadi neden hâlâ tutuklu?
content:
Ahmet Saymadi, 5 Ekim 2026’dan bu yana tutuklu. Hakkındaki suçlama, Türk Ceza Kanunu’nun 190. maddesinde düzenlenen “uyuşturucu veya uyarıcı madde kullanılmasını kolaylaştırma” suçu. Ancak aradan geçen zamana, yapılan aramalara ve toplanan delillere rağmen kamuoyunun önüne bu suçlamayı somutlaştıran tek bir olgu konulmuş değil.


Ortada delil olmadığı için bu soru orta yerde durmaya devam ediyor: O zaman Ahmet Saymadi neden hâlâ tutuklu?


3 Ekim gecesi, saat 23.00 sıralarında, Ahmet Saymadi’nin sahibi olduğu Kadim Meyhanesi polisler tarafından basıldı. Bir ihbar gerekçe gösterilerek gerçekleştirilen baskında işletmede bulunan 89 müşterinin kimlik kontrolleri ve üst aramaları yapıldı. İşletme kapsamlı biçimde arandı. Ancak yapılan aramalarda herhangi bir uyuşturucu maddeye veya suç unsuruna rastlanmadı.


Ne işletmede ne Ahmet Saymadi’nin üzerinde ne de çalışanlarında uyuşturucu madde bulunduğuna ilişkin bir bulgu ortaya konuldu. Müşteriler üzerinde yapılan kontrollerde de suçlamayı destekleyecek bir sonuç açıklanmadı.


Buna rağmen Ahmet Saymadi gözaltına alındı ve 5 Ekim’de tutuklandı.


Savcılık ifadesinde kendisine yöneltilen ilk soru uyuşturucu kullanıp kullanmadığıydı. Ahmet, hayatı boyunca uyuşturucu kullanmadığını, sigara dahi içmediğini söyledi. Ardından soruşturmanın odağı değişti. Türkiye İşçi Partisi Milletvekili ve gazeteci Ahmet Şık’ı tanıyıp tanımadığı, aralarında ticari bir ilişki bulunup bulunmadığı ve banka hesapları arasındaki bazı para hareketleri soruldu.


Ahmet, uzun yıllardır dostu olan Ahmet Şık’ın kredi kartıyla işletmesi için bazı alışverişler yaptığını, hesaplar arasındaki para transferlerinin de bu harcamaların karşılığı olduğunu anlattı. Bu açıklamaları destekleyen banka kayıtları avukatları tarafından dosyaya sunuldu.


Peki, bütün bunların uyuşturucu kullanılmasını kolaylaştırma suçlamasıyla nasıl bir bağlantısı var? Ahmet Saymadi’nin kime, ne zaman, nerede ve hangi davranışıyla uyuşturucu kullanımını kolaylaştırdığına ilişkin somut delil nerede?


Bu soruların yanıtı hâlâ kamuoyuna açıklanmış değil.


Tutukluluk, fiilî cezaya dönüşüyor


Ceza yargılamasında tutuklama bir ceza değildir. Henüz suçluluğu kesinleşmemiş bir insanın özgürlüğünün sınırlandırılması ancak kanunun öngördüğü koşullarda ve zorunlu hâllerde başvurulabilecek istisnai bir tedbirdir.


Anayasa’nın 19. maddesi kişi özgürlüğü ve güvenliği hakkını güvence altına alır. Ceza Muhakemesi Kanunu’nun 100. maddesi ise tutuklama için kuvvetli suç şüphesini gösteren somut delillerin ve bir tutuklama nedeninin bulunmasını şart koşar.


Ahmet Saymadi dosyasında ise işletme aranmış, müşteriler kontrol edilmiş, gerekli incelemeler yapılmış ve soruşturmanın konusu olan olası deliller toplanmıştır. Avukatları, bu koşulları ve dosyadaki eksiklikleri göstererek iki kez tutukluluğun gözden geçirilmesi için başvuruda bulundu. Ancak bu başvurulardan sonuç alınamadı. Şimdi yeni bir dilekçe daha savcılığın önünde bekliyor.


Eğer deliller toplanmışsa, aramalar tamamlanmışsa ve karartılabilecek bir delil durumu kalmamışsa tutukluluğun devamını gerektiren neden nedir?


Üstelik Ahmet, bu süreçte Metris Cezaevi’nden Silivri Cezaevi’ne sevk edildi ve uyuşturucu dosyalarından tutuklu bulunan kişilerin kaldığı 50 kişilik bir koğuşa yerleştirildi. Bir insanın özgürlüğünden yoksun bırakılması yetmiyormuş gibi, tutukluluk koşullarının da ayrıca ağırlaşması kabul edilebilir mi?


Ahmet’in tutukluluğu neredeyse iki ayı bulmuş durumda. Bu süre uzadıkça, henüz yargılama sonunda hüküm verilmeden tutuklama fiilî bir cezalandırmaya dönüşmüş oluyor zaten. Polis baskını ve basına yansıyan haberlerin ardından işletmenin zaten ciddi biçimde zorlandığı da biliniyor. Ahmet’in işinin başına dönmesinin, yaşamını sürdürebilmesinin ve savunmasını özgürce hazırlayabilmesinin önünde neden hâlâ engel bulunuyor?


Ahmet Şık ve Yonca Şık hakkındaki iddialar


Ahmet Saymadi’nin tutuklanmasıyla ilgili süreçte kamuoyuna çeşitli iddialar da yansıdı. TİP Milletvekili Ahmet Şık, X hesabından yaptığı bir açıklamada, bir paylaşımını silmemesi hâlinde Ahmet Saymadi’nin tutuklanacağı yönünde kendisine haberler ulaştığını aktarmıştı.


Ardından Ahmet Şık’ın eşi Yonca Şık da “casusluk” iddiasıyla gözaltına alındı. Yonca Şık tutuklanmadı; ancak hakkında yurt dışına çıkış yasağı şeklinde adli kontrol tedbiri uygulandı.


Bu gelişmelerin Ahmet Saymadi’nin tutuklanmasıyla nasıl bir ilişkisi olduğu, soruşturma süreçlerinin hangi bağlantılar üzerinden yürütüldüğü elbette ortaya …

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Federal Judge Permanently Bars Trump From Penalizing Groups Working With the ICC
content:
The ruling is a win against Trump’s attacks on the International Criminal Court amid its probes into the Gaza genocide.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

On Monday, a federal judge permanently barred the Trump administration from penalizing individuals and organizations who submit evidence to the International Criminal Court (ICC), in a victory for organizations that have faced sanctions for their efforts to bring accountability for the genocide in Gaza.

Monday’s ruling by Judge Jesse M. Furman expanded and made permanent a previous court order, issued in October, that blocked the Trump administration from imposing civil or criminal liability on the organizations Democracy for the Arab World Now and Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide.

The two groups had sued the Trump administration in July after President Donald Trump issued an executive order in February threatening fines and up to 20 years in prison for individuals or groups that share evidence with the ICC, UN Special Rapporteur on the Occupied Palestinian Territories Francesca Albanese, or Palestinian human rights groups Al-Haq, Al Mezan, and the Palestinian Center for Human Rights.

This week’s court order extended protections to all Americans who provide evidence to or advocate before the ICC, stating that bringing evidence to the ICC is First Amendment-protected speech. The ruling also rejected the Trump administration’s claims that the U.S. must be protected from the ICC, declaring that the government has failed to establish why it is necessary to penalize every instance of evidence provision to the court.

The ruling is a victory against Trump’s long-standing effort to undermine and attack the ICC for its investigations into war crimes committed in Gaza, which culminated in institutional sanctions against the entire court last month. The Trump administration had already sanctioned 11 ICC judges and prosecutors, preventing them from traveling to the U.S., freezing their U.S.-based assets, and severely limiting their ability to undertake financial transactions.

Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and even former Secretary of State Antony Blinken have all decried the ICC for its attempts to investigate and issue arrest warrants for Israeli officials over the genocide in Gaza.

“This landmark ruling dismantles a core part of Trump’s ICC draconian sanctions regime,” said Omar Shakir, executive director at Democracy for the Arab World Now. “The court has affirmed that every American has the constitutional right to advocate for justice on Palestine without fear of reprisal.”

Joseph Pace, attorney for Democracy for the Arab World Now and Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide, spoke to the weight of the victory.

“Typically, courts can now only offer relief to the plaintiffs — no matter how many thousands of nonparties are being victimized by an unconstitutional policy,” he said. “This decision is a major victory, not just because it invalidates a key part of the ICC sanctions’ regime, but because it universally bars the Trump Administration from using the sanctions to penalize anyone, anywhere in the country, for exercising their First Amendment rights.”

As a result of the decision, rights groups and individuals will be able to work with Albanese and Palestinian rights groups once again.

While the ruling protects evidence submission and advocacy, it leaves intact previously-applied sanctions that have frozen ICC members’ assets, funds, and financial transactions, including on individuals like Albanese.

In a separate ruling on Monday, Furman ruled against three ICC judges who asked to be removed from Trump’s sanctions list and for their frozen assets to be unblocked. The judge denied a preliminary injunction in their favor, stating that “deference here is owed not only to the president but also to Congress.” Furman also gave weight to Trump’s use of an International Emergency Economic Powers Act when he declared a national emergency over the ICC’s actions.

Earlier this month, Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide traveled to The Hague along with activists and human rights lawyers to submit evidence to the ICC. The group called for the ICC to issue arrest warrants for Trump, Rubio, and other U.S. officials for their complicity in the genocide in Gaza. Democracy for the Arab World Now is scheduled to give its own press conference at The Hague …

author: Lilli Akpaleeapik
title: No injuries in Tuesday’s fire in Iqaluit
content:
Nobody was injured in Tuesday’s

house fire

 near the Iqaluit breakwater, says city spokesperson Geoff Byrne.


The Iqaluit Fire Department responded to the incident with two trucks and 12 firefighters.


They contained a “heavy fire” coming from the second floor window of a residential complex located on Nipisa Street, Byrne said Wednesday in an email to Nunatsiaq News.


Crews were able to contain the fire to the room where the fire started and avoid spread to other rooms or units, Byrne said.


The cause of the fire remains unknown. An Iqaluit Fire Department truck was parked outside the residence on Wednesday.


The Government of Nunavut released a public service announcement Tuesday as well encouraging Nunavummiut to be safe with candles, qulliqs and space heaters as tauvik, or the dark season, sets in in Nunavut.


The timing of the public service announcement was coincidental and unrelated to the fire in Iqaluit, said Ryleigh Hubert, communications adviser with Department of Community Services.


Nunatsiaq News reached out to RCMP but did not immediately receive a response.

author: Perseus
title: “Να τσακίσουμε την σκευωρία Marfin”: Δράση στην πορεία για την Εξέγερση του Πολυτεχνείου (Βίντεο)
content:
“Να τσακίσουμε την σκευωρία Marfin”: Δράση στην πορεία για την Εξέγερση του Πολυτεχνείου (Βίντεο)


Βίντεο

 από τη δράση αλληλεγγύης και αντιπληροφόρησης ενάντια στη σκευωρία Marfin Vol. 3 στην πορεία μνήμης για την Εξέγερση του Πολυτεχνείου στις 17 Νοέμβρη 2026.


Λίγα λόγια για την υπόθεση της Marfin, μέσα από αποσπάσματα της εφημερίδας δρόμου

Άπατρις:


“Η ανακίνηση της υπόθεσης Marfin για 3η φορά σηματοδοτεί το πέρασμα σε μια νέα εποχή όσον αφορά τον εγχώριο κοινωνικό-ταξικό ανταγωνισμό.


Στις 10 Ιουλίου εκτελείται τριπλό ένταλμα σύλληψης, και διατάσσονται κατ’ οίκον έρευνες σε 5 άτομα. Συλλαμβάνονται οι σύντροφοι Θύμιος και Κώστας, και η συντρόφισσα Ελένη, κάτοικος εξωτερικού, που μεταφέρεται στα αγγλικά κρατητήρια.


Τα στοιχεία για την υπόθεση είναι ανύπαρκτα: Από την έκθεση της Διεύθυνσης Εγκληματολογικών Ερευνών, όπου αναλύεται το οπτικοακουστικό υλικό, δεν προκύπτει ταυτοποίηση των συντροφιών ως παρόντα στο σημείο μπροστά από την τράπεζα. Μοναδικά στοιχεία η ομοιότητα κάποιων κινητών αντικειμένων, και ένα ανώνυμο email, το οποίο συνέταξε η Διεύθυνση Αντιμετώπισης Οργανωμένου Εγκλήματος που πραγματοποίησε τις συλλήψεις. Η δουλειά της αστυνομίας είναι πολύ πρόχειρη: Στο mail αναφέρεται ως μέλος στο «παρεάκι» που εμπλέκεται στην υπόθεση, άτομο που ήταν στη φυλακή εκείνη την ημέρα· ακόμα, η εκπρόσωπος τύπου της ΕΛ.ΑΣ., Κ. Δημογλίδου, αναφέρει στον ΣΚΑΪ πως το επίμαχο mail είναι στα χέρια της αστυνομίας 1,5 χρόνο, ενώ αυτό έχει ημερομηνία αποστολής 08/04/2026, δηλαδή 3 μήνες πριν τις συλλήψεις.


Οι απολογίες διεξάγονται ενώπιον της ανακρίτριας Σμαράγδας Τασούλη, και της εισαγγελέως Βαρβάρας Γνεσούλη. Τα συντρόφια αρνούνται τις κατηγορίες, υπερασπίζονται την πολιτική τους θέση, όπως και τη συμμετοχή τους στη διαδήλωση, και ζητούν να διερευνηθεί ποιος έστειλε το e-mail.


Και τα 3 συντρόφια προφυλακίζονται παρά την απουσία στοιχείων. Απορρίπτονται και οι προσφυγές τους ενάντια στην απόφαση προφυλάκισης, καθώς τα αρμόδια Συμβούλια πλημμελειοδικών επικυρώνουν τις απορριπτικές προτάσεις των εισαγγελέων, του αντιεισαγγελέα πρωτοδικών Λυμπερόπουλου, και των εισαγγελέων πρωτοδικών Μαρουδά και Ηλιοπούλου. Έχει ενδιαφέρον πως στα σκεπτικά των προφυλακίσεων, όπως και στις απορρίψεις των προσφυγών, υιοθετείται η συλλογιστική από το διαβιβαστικό της αστυνομίας, εμπλουτισμένη με αναφορές σε «ενδείξεις ενοχής» αλλά και σε «οργανωμένη, συλλογική και προπαρασκευασμένη δράση». Σύμφωνα με τους δικαστικούς, υπάρχει ο κίνδυνος τα συντρόφια μας να τελέσουν τα ίδια αδικήματα, μιας και «εδώ και 16 χρόνια κρύβουν επιμελώς τη δράση τους». Τι πιο λογικό άλλωστε;


Η ΔΑΟΕ, κατ’ εντολή του Μιχάλη Χρυσοχοΐδη, έκανε τη δουλειά της. Στο μαγείρεμα παίρνει θέση και η δικαστική εξουσία, έτοιμη να το αναβαθμίσει με την –όχι και τόσο– μυστική συνταγή της. Η υπόθεση μένει στην εποπτεία της ανακρίτριας Τασούλη για τις τελικές πινελιές και το ντεκόρ.


Οι νέες συνταγές, λοιπόν, δεν αργούν. Το μαγειρείο καλά κρατεί: Στις αρχές Οκτώβρη, η ανακρίτρια επιστρατεύει την 1η παράγραφο του νόμου 187Α, αυτήν περί ατομικής τρομοκρατίας.* Μέχρι πρότινος τα 3 συντρόφια κατηγορούνταν για ανθρωποκτονία κατά συρροή και από κοινού, και τα διαθέσιμα «στοιχεία» δεν επαρκούσαν για τη απόδοση κατηγοριών σύστασης οργάνωσης (εγκληματικής ή τρομοκρατικής). Με αυτή τη μεθόδευση, το κατηγορητήριο αναβαθμίζεται. Αυτό επιφέρει επιπλέον κατηγορίες για 24 απόπειρες ανθρωποκτονίας – κατηγορίες που δεν παραγράφονται εφόσον η πράξη υπάγεται στην αντιτρομοκρατική νομοθεσία.


Το σημαντικότερο όλων, όμως, όταν έρθει η ώρα της δίκης, είναι πως τα συντρόφια μας δεν θα οδηγηθούν σε ΜΟΔ, όπως συνέβη με την πρώτη εκδίκαση της υπόθεσης (για ακριβώς τα ίδια αδικήματα, εξαιρουμένου του 187Α). Αντιθέτως, θα δικαστούν από Τριμελές Εφετείο Κακουργημάτων, που θα απαρτίζεται μόνο από επαγγελματίες δικαστές. Έτσι, αφήνεται εκτός ο αστάθμητος παράγων των ενόρκων, που έχουν οδηγήσει σε πανηγυρικές αθωώσεις αγωνιστών ανά τα χρόνια – όπως εξάλλου συνέβη και στην πρώτη version της υπόθεσης, με το ίδιο ακριβώς κατηγορητήριο.


Συνολικά από την πλευρά του κράτους, η ανακίνηση της υπόθεσης Marfin έρχεται ως κλείσιμο ενός ανοιχτού λογαριασμού, που βαστάει τουλάχιστον 2 δεκαετίες – λογαριασμός που άνοιξε με τη μαζικοποίηση των κοινωνικών αντιστάσεων, και την κορύφωσή της κατά την τριετία των αντιμνημονιακών ταραχών (2010-2012). Ο κατασταλτικός μηχανισμός δεν ενδιαφέρεται πραγματικά να βρει τους «ενόχους του τότε», αλλά να τρομοκρατήσει τους «συνενόχους του σήμερα» – όσες και όσους δεν έχουν πλέον πολλές …

author: Amy Goodman
title: National Book Award Winner Links Denial of US Visa to Palestine Advocacy
content:
Egyptian author and former political prisoner Abdelrahman ElGendy speaks about his new memoir, Huna.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

This year’s annual National Book Award ceremony in New York City was marked by the notable absence of nonfiction winner Abdelrahman ElGendy, after the Trump administration denied the Egyptian author entry into the United States. ElGendy’s debut, Huna: A Memoir of Revolution, Prison, and Becoming, chronicles his arrest and over six years of imprisonment, alongside his father, following arrest at a protest against the military dictatorship of Egypt’s President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi. After his release from prison in Egypt, ElGendy obtained an MFA in the United States but was forced to flee once again — this time from the U.S. to Europe — for fear of being targeted by immigration authorities over his criticism of Israel’s war on Gaza and U.S.-Egypt relations.

“It was a gutting thing to not be able to attend the ceremony. But it was also unsurprising,” ElGendy tells Democracy Now! about being barred from receiving the National Book Award in person. “[I] have labored for so long my whole life to get to this point, only to again and again and again be forced to witness it all from afar and detached from the people I love.”

We speak to ElGendy about the weaponization of the visa process, in both the U.S. and Egypt, “as a form of transnational repression,” his arrest and imprisonment beginning at the age of just 17, and the Egyptian government’s ongoing repression of free speech, including its attempted closure of the independent news outlet Mada Masr, whose lawyers were in court today appealing its shutdown.

“Mada carries so much of the archive of our revolutionary history … so to erase it is to erase an archive,” says ElGendy, whose early writings were smuggled out of prison and first published in Mada Masr. “The current Egyptian military dictatorship [is] a frantic project of erasure of everything that has to do with the revolution, and it’s an insistence on erasing every trace that would allow people to remember that revolution has happened, that this rupture has happened before.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman.

We are currently awaiting an Egyptian court decision on whether the closing of Mada Masr, the independent newspaper in Egypt, will stand. We’ll go to Cairo when we hear.

But right now we’re going to turn to what happened in the last few weeks here in this country, in New York, where we are. Novelists, essayists, poets and other writers from around the world took to the stage at the 77th annual National Book Awards ceremony in New York City last week. The winner of this year’s National Book Award for Nonfiction, Egyptian author Abdelrahman ElGendy, though, was notably absent from the event, after the Trump administration denied his U.S. visa application, blocking him from entering the United States.

ElGendy’s debut book is called Huna: A Memoir of Revolution, Prison, and Becoming, and chronicles his more than six years of imprisonment in Egypt following his arrest at the age of 17, alongside his father, during the crackdown on protests after the military coup led by Abdel Fattah el-Sisi in 2013. He and his father were in their car, and Abdelrahman was taking a picture.

This is the moment the prize for nonfiction was presented by panel chair Robert Warrior.

ROBERT WARRIOR: It’s my distinct honor to announce that this year’s National Book Award for Nonfiction goes to Abdelrahman ElGendy for Huna.

AMY GOODMAN: Abdelrahman ElGendy’s editor, Helen Thomaides, then took the stage and read a statement written by ElGendy.

HELEN THOMAIDES: If you’re listening to this, then a years-long dream of mine has come true, and I’m not there to live it with you. Years ago, in my prison cell in Egypt, I used to fantasize about writing a memoir. I would slip under a bright red duvet my mother had bribed the guards to let through, and imagine that everything happening to me would one day end up in a book, that the guard’s baton was battering not my ribs but those of the book’s protagonist, that the slap was landing on the protagonist’s face, not mine. I was the author, concerned only with how to render on the page the torture my body was enduring. The scribbles on a smuggled page became a potential essay …

title: မုအမ္မာ ဂဒါဖီရဲ့ စာအုပ်စိမ်း – အကျိုး၊ အပြစ်နဲ့ ဇော်ကန့်လန့်ခြင်းများ
content:
By

Jordan Jardine

. Original article:

Muammar Gaddafi’s Green Book: The Good, The Bad, and The Weird

, published on March 9, 2022. Translated into Burmese by Hein Htet Kyaw.


မုအမ္မာ ဂဒါဖီဟာ အရင်ကရော၊ ခုရော၊ နောက်လည်း အမြဲတမ်း ငြင်းခုံဝေဖန်စရာ ပုဂ္ဂိုလ်တစ်ယောက် ဖြစ်နေမှာပါ။ ဘဒူအင် (Bedouin) မျိုးနွယ်စု လှည့်လည်သွားလာသူ ဘဝကနေ လစ်ဗျားရဲ့ ခေါင်းဆောင် ဖြစ်လာတာက အားကျစရာကောင်းပေမဲ့၊ တိုင်းပြည်ကို အုပ်ချုပ်နေစဉ်အတွင်း အာဏာရှင်ဆန်ဆန်နဲ့ ပြစ်မှုဆိုင်ရာ ကိစ္စတော်တော်များများကို ကျူးလွန်ခဲ့တာကတော့ ငြင်းလို့မရတဲ့ အချက်ပါ။


ဒါပေမဲ့ ဂဒါဖီဟာ စစချင်းမှာတော့ လွတ်မြောက်ရေးသမားတစ်ယောက်လို စခဲ့တာပါ။ ၁၉၆၀ ပြည့်လွန်နှစ်များ အစောပိုင်းမှာ လစ်ဗျားစစ်တပ်ထဲ ဝင်ခဲ့ပြီး ၁၉၆၉ ခုနှစ် ဘုရင် အိဒ်ရစ် (King Idris) ကို ဖြုတ်ချခဲ့တဲ့ အာဏာသိမ်းပွဲမှာ အဓိက ခေါင်းဆောင်တစ်ယောက် ဖြစ်လာခဲ့ပါတယ်။ ဘုရင်စနစ်ကို အောင်အောင်မြင်မြင် ဖျက်သိမ်းပြီးတဲ့နောက် ဂဒါဖီဟာ အာဏာသိမ်းပြီး လစ်ဗျားကို “လစ်ဗျား အရက်ဘ် သမ္မတနိုင်ငံ” အဖြစ် ပြောင်းလဲခဲ့ပါတယ်။ နောက်ပိုင်းမှာတော့ သူရဲ့ နိုင်ငံရေး၊ လူမှုရေးနဲ့ စီးပွားရေး အမြင်တွေကို ၁၉၇၅ မှာ ပထမဆုံး ထုတ်ဝေခဲ့တဲ့ “စာအုပ်စိမ်း” (The Green Book) ဆိုတဲ့ စာအုပ်တိုလေးထဲမှာ ရေးသားခဲ့ပြီး၊ တစ်နှစ်အကြာမှာတော့ အင်္ဂလိပ်ဘာသာပြန်နဲ့ တစ်ကမ္ဘာလုံးကို ဖြန့်ချိခဲ့ပါတယ်။


အနှစ်ချုပ်


အပိုင်း (၁) – ဒီမိုကရေစီ ပြဿနာရဲ့ အဖြေ


စာအုပ်စိမ်းရဲ့ ဒီအစပိုင်းမှာ ဂဒါဖီက တို့တွေ သိထားကြတဲ့ “ဒီမိုကရေစီ” ဆိုတာတွေဟာ တကယ်တော့ အလွန်အာဏာရှင်ဆန်ပြီး ဒီမိုကရေစီနဲ့ ဆန့်ကျင်ဘက်ဖြစ်တယ်လို့ စုဒ်တက်ထားပါတယ်။ လွှတ်တော်စနစ်တွေဟာ စေတနာကောင်းနဲ့ စခဲ့တာမှန်ပေမဲ့ နောက်ဆုံးမှာ ပြည်သူတွေရဲ့ အကျိုးစီးပွားကို မဖော်ဆောင်နိုင်တော့ဘူးလို့ ဆိုပါတယ်။ ပါတီနိုင်ငံရေးဟာ မဲပေးခဲ့တဲ့ ပြည်သူတွေထက် ပါတီရဲ့ အကျိုးစီးပွားကိုပဲ ကြည့်သွားကြမှာပဲလို့ သူက အခိုင်အမာ ပြောပါတယ်။ ဒါကြောင့် ကိုယ်စားလှယ်ပြု ဒီမိုကရေစီ ဒါမှမဟုတ် လွှတ်တော် ဒီမိုကရေစီအစား “တိုက်ရိုက် ဒီမိုကရေစီ” (Direct Democracy) ကသာ ဒီပြဿနာကို ဖြေရှင်းဖို့ အကောင်းဆုံး နည်းလမ်းပဲလို့ ဂဒါဖီက ဆိုပါတယ်။


ဒါ့အပြင် လူတန်းစား ပဋိပက္ခဟာ အမြဲတမ်း အင်အားကြီးတဲ့ လူတန်းစားက အောက်ခြေလူတန်းစားကို နိုင်ငံရေးနည်းနဲ့ စီးပိုးအုပ်ချုပ်ရာ ရောက်သွားစေတာမို့၊ အထက်တန်းစားတွေက အောက်ခြေလူတန်းစားကို ပုံစံခွက်တစ်ခုထဲနဲ့ ချော့မြှော့ဖို့ ကြိုးစားနေတာဟာ အလကားပဲလို့ ဆိုပါတယ်။ ဘာလို့လဲဆိုတော့ ချော့မြှော့ရုံနဲ့ အောက်ခြေလူတန်းစားတွေ အမြဲ မကြေနပ်နိုင်သလို၊ အုပ်စိုးသူ လူတန်းစားနဲ့ စိတ်ဝင်စားမှုချင်းလည်း ကွဲပြားနေလို့ပါ။ ဂဒါဖီက သူ စိတ်ကူးထားတဲ့ တိုက်ရိုက် ဒီမိုကရေစီ ပုံစံကို ဆက်လက် ဖော်ပြထားပါတယ်။ တိုက်ရိုက် ဒီမိုကရေစီကို “ပြည်သူ့ညီလာခံများ” (Popular Conferences) နဲ့ “ပြည်သူ့ကော်မတီများ” (People’s Committees) ဆိုတာတွေနဲ့ ဖော်ဆောင်ရမယ်လို့ ဆိုပါတယ်။ အခြေခံအားဖြင့် ပြည်သူ့ညီလာခံဆိုတာ ပြည်သူတွေ တိုက်ရိုက်ရွေးချယ်ထားတဲ့ အာဏာခွဲဝေမှုအဖွဲ့အစည်းတွေဖြစ်ပြီး “အခြေခံ ပြည်သူ့ညီလာခံ” နဲ့ “အခြေခံမဟုတ်သော ပြည်သူ့ညီလာခံ” ဆိုပြီး နှစ်မျိုး ခွဲထားပါတယ်။ ဒီညီလာခံတွေကမှတစ်ဆင့် ပြည်သူ့ကော်မတီဝင်တွေကို ပြန်ရွေးချယ်တာပါ။ ဒီမိုကရေစီရဲ့ “အမှန်တကယ် အဓိပ္ပာယ်” ဆိုတာ “ပြည်သူက ပြည်သူကို ကြီးကြပ်ကွပ်ကဲခြင်း” လို့ သူက ဆိုပါတယ်။


နောက်တစ်ခုကတော့ ဥပဒေတွေနဲ့ ပတ်သက်ပြီး ဘာကို အခြေခံရမလဲဆိုတာကို ဂဒါဖီက ဆွေးနွေးထားပါတယ်။ ဥပဒေဆိုတာ ဘာသာရေး ဒါမှမဟုတ် ရိုးရာဓလေ့ မူ Post တွေကို အခြေခံရမယ်လို့ ဆိုပြီး၊ ဘာသာရေးနဲ့ မသက်ဆိုင်တဲ့ ဖွဲ့စည်းပုံအခြေခံဥပဒေတွေဟာ “တရားမဝင်သလို ယုတ္တိလည်းမရှိဘူး” လို့ ဝေဖန်ထားပါတယ်။ နောက်ပိုင်းမှာတော့ တိုက်ရိုက်ဒီမိုကရေစီဟာ စာနယ်ဇင်းလွတ်လပ်ခွင့်ကို ပိုတိုးတက်စေမယ်လို့ ဖော်ပြထားပြီး၊ ပုဂ္ဂိုလ်ရေးရော ကုမ္ပဏီအဖွဲ့အစည်းတွေပါ စာနယ်ဇင်းလွတ်လပ်ခွင့် ရှိသင့်တယ်လို့ ဆိုပါတယ်။


အပိုင်း (၂) – စီးပွားရေး ပြဿနာရဲ့ အဖြေ


ခေတ်သစ် အလုပ်သမားတွေရဲ့ အခြေအနေဟာ စက်မှုတော်လှန်ရေး စတင်ခဲ့ချိန်ကထက်စာရင် သာလွန်ကောင်းမွန်လာတာကို ဂဒါဖီက လက်ခံထားပါတယ်။ ဒါပေမဲ့ အချိန်ပိုကြေးပေးတာ၊ လူမှုဖူလုံရေး၊ သပိတ်မှောက်ခွင့်နဲ့ အလုပ်ချိန် ကန့်သတ်တာမျိုးတွေဟာ ပုံမှန် အလုပ်သမားတစ်ယောက်ရဲ့ ဘဝကို သက်သာရာရစေဖို့ မလုံလောက်သေးဘဲ၊ နိုင်ငံရေးသမားတွေဟာ အလုပ်သမားတွေကို နှိမ့်စက်သူတွေလက်ကနေ အမှန်တကယ် လွတ်မြောက်အောင် မလုပ်ပေးနိုင်ခဲ့ကြဘူးလို့ ဆိုပါတယ်။ ပြည်သူ့ဝန်ထမ်းတွေဟာလည်း ပုဂ္ဂလိက ဝန်ထမ်းတွေထက် သိပ်ပိုမကောင်းလှပါဘူး။ သူက “လုပ်ခလစာယူတဲ့သူတွေဟာ သူတို့ကို ငှားထားတဲ့ သခင်တွေရဲ့ ကျေးကျွန်တွေပဲ။ အချိန်ပိုင်း ကျေးကျွန်တွေဖြစ်ပြီး၊ သူတို့ရဲ့ ကျေးကျွန်ဘဝဟာ ပုဂ္ဂလိကဖြစ်စေ၊ ရေဒီယို/အစိုးရဖြစ်စေ အလုပ်ရှင်ဆီက လစာယူနေသမျှ ကာလပတ်လုံး တည်ရှိနေမှာပဲ” လို့ ထိထိမိမိ ရေးထားပါတယ်။


သူက လုပ်ခလစာစနစ်ကို ဖျက်သိမ်းဖို့နဲ့ ထုတ်လုပ်မှု နည်းလမ်းတွေကို ပူးပေါင်းပိုင်ဆိုင်ဖို့ စိစစ်တင်ပြထားပါတယ်။ နည်းပညာ တိုးတက်လာတာနဲ့အမျှ ကုန်စည်နဲ့ ဝန်ဆောင်မှု ပေးဖို့ လိုအပ်တဲ့ အလုပ်သမားအရေအတွက်နဲ့ အလုပ်ချိန်တွေ လျော့နည်းသွားမယ်လို့လည်း ဆိုပါတယ်။ “လူတစ်ယောက်ရဲ့ လွတ်လပ်ခွင့်ဟာ သူရဲ့ လိုအပ်ချက်တွေကို အခြားသူတွေက ထိန်းချုပ်ထားရင် ဆုံးရှုံးနေတာပဲ။ ဘာလို့လဲဆိုတော့ လိုအပ်ချက်ကနေတစ်ဆင့် တစ်ယောက်က တစ်ယောက်ကို ကျေးကျွန်ပြုတာတွေ ဖြစ်လာနိုင်လို့ပါ။ ဒါ့အပြင် ခေါင်းပုံဖြတ်တာဟာ …

author: Λουκάς Σταμέλλος
title: Το Νήμα | Δεν είναι όλα «απόψεις»
content:
Ρητορική και εγκλήματα μίσους κατά ΛΟΑΤΚΙ+ ατόμων

Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Το Νήμα | Δεν είναι όλα «απόψεις»
