title: 25 novembre 2007 : L'ordre sécuritaire et le soulèvement des quartiers populaires - Retours sur la bataille de Villiers-le-Bel
content:
Extrait de l'ouvrage collectif

«

 

Vengeance d'état - Villiers-le-Bel : des révoltes aux procès

 

»

 écrit par le

collectif Angles Morts

. Cet extrait a été mise en page sous forme de brochure et revient sur la bataille de Villiers-le-Bel fin novembre 2007.


La mini moto des deux adolescents tués dans une collision avec la police à Villiers-le-Bel le 25 nov 2007


Brochure sur la bataille de Villers-le-Bel à télécharger en bas de page. Extrait de l'ouvrage collectif "Vengeance d'état - Villers-le-Bel : des révoltes aux procès" écrit par le collectif Angles Morts et publié aux éditions Syllepse en 2011.


L'ordre sécuritaire et le soulèvement des quartiers populaires - Retours sur la bataille de Villiers-le-Bel


Mathieu Rigouste

 [

1

]


«

 

Que la guerre à la drogue provoque plus d'abus policiers, une répression plus puissante et la suspension des libertés civiles pour tous les habitants des quartiers ne devrait pas surprendre, étant donné la longue histoire de la police des communautés de couleur. La relation coloniale qui structurait originellement la présence policière reste pratiquement inchangée. Comme des armées d'occupation avec quasiment aucun lien organique dans le quartier auquel elles sont assignées, ces forces de police de la grande ville n'opèrent pas différemment des forces impériales d'hier : chaque sujet colonisé est suspect. Il est rare ce policier, même parmi les Noirs, les Latinos et les femmes, qui voit sa tâche principale comme le fait de travailler pour ou d'être employé par les communautés de couleur des quartiers pauvres. Au lieu de ça, la police travaille pour l'État et la municipalité, et son rôle est de garder à vue une population entièrement criminalisée, de contenir le chaos entre les murs du ghetto et de s'assurer que les plus indisciplinés restent dans le rang.

 

»


Robin

D. G.

 Kelley

 [

2

]


L'impérialisme occidental est entré dans une nouvelle phase d'expansion à la fin du 20

e

 siècle. Pour se restructurer, il attaque et dépossède les derniers territoires qui résistent encore à l'accumulation illimitée du profit et de la puissance

 [

3

]

. À l'intérieur même des pays dominants, les quartiers populaires concentrent celles et ceux qui pro­fitent le moins de l'ordre en place et qui ont donc le plus intérêt à s'en débarrasser. Ces quartiers sont pris entre les mâchoires de l'État et du capital : une double stratégie, politique et économique qui cherche à les encadrer et à les provoquer, à les contenir et à les attaquer, pour les soumettre, les transformer ou détruire ceux qui entravent encore l'extension des mégalopoles.


Mais les terrains de chasse du système sécuritaire ne se laissent pas écraser sans combattre. Villiers-le-Bel est une bataille importante dans cette longue campagne inachevée. Elle a permis d'expérimenter de nouvelles technologies de contrôle, de surveillance et de répression, elle a médiatisé ces savoir-faire et les matériels français sur le marché international de la sécurité intérieure. Elle a servi à criminaliser davantage la révolte des quartiers populaires. Mais elle devait aussi offrir une revanche aux policiers victimisés durant les batailles de Clichy-sous-Bois (octobre-décembre 2005). Humiliés une nouvelle fois, caillassés par des adolescents et de jeunes adultes, insultés par leurs parents, méprisés par des retraités, une partie de ces policiers est entrée dans un processus de radicalisation. Pendant la guerre d'Algérie, la contre-insurrection avait déjà débordé. Une fraction fasciste s'était alors constituée à l'intérieur de l'armée et avait tenté de prendre le pouvoir. L'ordre sécuritaire, lui, se confronte à un problème de débordement dans la police.


Il faut montrer que les révoltes des quartiers populaires s'inscrivent dans la longue histoire des résistances à la domination impérialiste. Analyser l'influence des techniques de guerre coloniale sur les nouvelles méthodes de répression, le rôle des marchés politiques et économiques de la sécurité, décrire les contradictions et les failles dans la police. La bataille de Villiers-le-Bel nous parle des transformations à l'oeuvre dans les stratégies et les armes, les forces et les faiblesses de l'oppresseur.


Impérialisme, ségrégation et répression


Les inégalités sociales, économiques et politiques produites par le capitalisme provoquent inévitablement de l'indiscipline et des révoltes dans les classes populaires. Il existe ainsi un phénomène de «

 

crises

 

» cycliques …

author: Brian Hioe
title: How Can We Explain the Rise of Puma Shen’s “Ocean Current”?
content:
MANY COMMENTATORS have been at odds in explaining the meteoric rise of Puma Shen as a DPP candidate in Taipei.

Regardless of the outcome of the race, it seems that Shen will have a political future. It is self-evident at this point that Shen is on track to be the best-performing DPP mayoral candidate in the 30 years since Chen Shui-bian–who, after all, later became Taiwan’s president.

At the same time, it was expected by few that Shen would become not only a household name, but electrify the elections across all of Taiwan. The effect of what has been termed the “Ocean Current” has powerfully affected races across Taiwan, boosting the DPP’s chances in Taiwan as a whole.

Races which were previously thought to be close, such as in New Taipei, may potentially be tipped in the direction of the DPP. Specifically, in New Taipei, Lee Shu-chuan of the KMT was already struggling against Su Chiao-hui of the DPP, probably due to a lack of experience as a campaigner even if he was known as a strong administrator.

In this sense, even if Puma Shen does not win in Taipei, it is possible that the DPP still benefits elsewhere. Puma Shen has, then–to quote Nathan Batto–become something of a “public resource” for the DPP in that he has been called on to campaign for DPP politicians nationwide. Each of those politicians benefits from public appearances with Shen, even if Shen is, of course, only running in Taipei.

The ubiquity of Puma Shen’s “Ocean Current” imagery in urban spaces, then, reminds something of past social movement uprisings in Taiwan. During the course of the 2014 Sunflower Movement, one could readily identify on the subway, on streets, in cafes, who was supportive of the movement–these were usually young people who had ribbons, flags, and other signifiers of the movement attached to their bags, or in the form of stickers on laptops and phones.

Now, it is the ubiquitous Ocean Current ribbon that appears everywhere. To give a sense of how enthusiastic the public is about the Ocean Current phenomenon, DAYBREAK–the cafe that New Bloom runs in Wanhua–is located outside of a DPP city councilor’s office. For merch distribution that starts at 7:00 PM, a line regularly forms at 2:30 PM.

It is possible that the Shen campaign has managed to tap into the merch-crazy impulses of Taiwanese society, in line with Shen’s anime otaku stylings. After all, the urge to collect is now such that main convenience stores–that ubiquitous institution of Taiwanese society–have begun selling anime merchandise or offering raffle lottery tickets for limited-edition merchandise.

Or it could be Shen’s public image. Shen has managed to depict himself as policy-crazy, an otaku anime nerd, in such a way as to convince the public that he is an expert on public policy, tapping into the fact that he was already known as a researcher of Chinese disinformation strong on data analytics.

But at a time in which Japanese anime, manga, and video games are highly popular among young people, Shen has also managed to use his otaku self-depiction to avoid a technocratic image–rather, his interest in anime, manga, and video games has made him relatable to members of the public in a way that his competitor, Chiang Wan-an struggles to–even if it has resulted in some odd moments such as Shen claiming to the media that Neon Genesis Evangelion, the apotheosis of Japanese animated postmodernism, has taught him lessons about responsible urban governance. But by contrast, one is hard-pressed to name any of Chiang’s hobbies off the top of one’s head,

Yet it also does not seem to be merely Shen’s stylings that have made him popular–indeed, something that the KMT failed to understand after its defeat in 2016 in the wake of the Sunflower Movement, somehow seeing the movement as a successful tactical innovation of the DPP. Rather, one must take into account the contents of Shen’s political message.

One has sometimes seen the comparison between Shen and New York mayor Zohran Mamdani, as a left-wing youth candidate whose victory against high odds attracted global attention. But even if Shen’s message has been less about socioeconomic inequality and more about competent and good governance, perhaps Taipei voters are simply tired of nepotistic governance from the usual KMT politicians who usually dominate Taipei–one notes that almost all of Taipei’s KMT mayoral candidates in past decades have hailed from powerful political families, whether that be Ma Ying-jeou, Hau Lung-bin …

author: Administrador
title: Préparatifs Zapatistes pour la Rencontre Étreinte avec les familles Buscadoras. Partie 2 « Le plan D »
content:
18 octobre 2026 – communiqué original ici

« La délégation du Voyage pour la Vie-Chapitre Mexique en train de pratiquer la variante du football connue comme « Foot en commun » ou « Foot en foule ». Aucun ballon n’a été endommagé. En ce qui concerne les joueur·euses et bien… regardez la vidéo ».

Musique : Cuatro Pesos de Propina , « La Verdadera » et « El Maleficio »

Images, édition et production : Terci@s Compas Zapatistas

Préparatifs Zapatistes pour la Rencontre Étreinte avec les familles Buscadoras. Partie 2 « Le plan D »

Frères, sœurs, frœurs de Familles Buscadoras,

Compañeras, compañeros et compañeroas,

Communauté originaire Otomi de la Maison des Peuples Samir Flores Soberanes,

Nous vous informons que le dénommé Plan C a échoué. Nous ne sommes plus 1509 à y aller, comme nous vous l’avions dit. Maintenant, nous sommes 1530. Nous espérons qu’il ne sera pas nécessaire de mettre en place un Plan E, mais on ne sait jamais parce qu’il y en a qui peuvent arriver avec leur air de « on est juste venu dire au revoir » et puis qui grimpent dans le bus et « c’est à vous de gérer ».

Toute la délégation s’est réunie afin de bien se préparer et de vous apporter un bonne parole d’encouragement et de soutien.

Beaucoup d’entre nous, hommes et femmes et autrEs, nous ne parlons pas bien la castilla. Nos langues maternelles sont de racine maya. Nous devons donc préparer aussi celles et ceux qui traduisent. Et nous corriger autant que possible pour que notre parole ne soit pas déformée.

Nous sommes content·es car nous allons pouvoir vous écouter et vous parler et vous serrer dans nos bras. Donc on pratique. Juste, on ne pratique pas les étreintes car vous savez bien qu’après, il y en a qui sont lourds et qui en font trop. Qui en profitent, quoi.

Parfois, on joue entassé·es, au cas où il y a un match de foot qui se fait là-bas.

Dans la délégation, nous sommes :

709 hommes, 622 femmes et 2 autrEs.

24 du Commando Palomitas [Pop Corn] : 10 petits garçons et 14 petites filles.

110 des « jeunes en commun » de communauté : 66 hommes et 43 femmes.

27 de l’équipe de coordination : 7 femmes et 20 hommes.

39 de l’armée : 16 miliciens et 23 miliciennes.

Au total à ce jour (18 octobre 2026) : 1530 délégués, déléguées et délégué·es, et maudits enfants du diable, approximativement. Donc vous verrez bien.

C’est tout pour le moment, compañeras, compañeroas et compañeros, frœurs, frères et sœurs.

S’il y a un changement (et nous prions pour qu’il n’y en ait pas), nous vous tiendrons au courant. Nous continuerons à vous envoyer des vidéos de nos préparatifs.

Nous vous envoyons notre étreinte commune, en espérant bientôt vous la donner personnellement.

Depuis les montagnes du Sud-est mexicain.

Sous-commandant insurgé Moisés.

Coordinateur Général du Voyage pour la Vie – Chapitre Mexique.

title: Préparatifs zapatistes en vue de la rencontre « Abrazo avec les familles Buscadoras » Partie I : Jeunes comédiens
content:
Musique : Caifanes, « Antes de que nos olviden » [Avant qu’on ne nous oublie]

Images : Terci@s Compas Zapatistas

Préparatifs zapatistes en vue de la rencontre « Abrazo avec les familles Buscadoras » Partie I : Jeunes comédiens

SE RETROUVER PARMI LES CAIFANES

J’étais là comme ça, pour ainsi dire, pas plus, sans penser à rien. Mais j’avais mon air, du plus caifan [ndt : mot argotique se référant à une personne du quartier, attentive à son style vestimentaire et vive d’esprit] des caifans, du plus top et du plus cool de la bande et des cools. Je suis comme ça quoi et là comme ça, je le vois qui vient à patte, le Riko, c’est pas son vrai nom de baptême, sûr, mais c’est comme ça qu’il se fait appeler parce que, comme il dit, il est le plus beau du quartier, de la racaille, de la populace, et que toutes les meufs eh ben elles soupirent pour sa petite personne. Riko ou « Rikolin » s’autoproclame, il dit que l’autre jour deux filles se sont disputées pour lui, mais moi j’le sais que oui elles se sont disputées, mais pas pour lui, c’était parce que celle de l’épicerie avait pas bien rendu la monnaie à l’autre. Mais le Riko Rickolin jure et rejure que c’était pour le privilège de ses charmes. Bref, du coup le voilà qui arrive et qui me dit : « Bah alors mon cap ? T’es en mode inconito ? » « Incognito », on dit « incognito », j’le corrige. « Ouais, c’est ça », dit le Riko, et il continue « Bien ou quoi ? » Le Riko croit qu’il parle l’argot du quartier mais, rien que tchi walou. « Tranquille, j’suis planté là à voir c’qui s’passe », j’lui dis pour le suivre dans son délire. Le Riko voit qu’y a personne d’autre et il abandonne la pose aguicheuse numéro 69 de son catalogue, et me demande « Et qu’est-ce t’en penses de ça ? ». « De quoi, ça ? » « Bah, ça » « J’sais pas c’que c’est, ça ». « Bah c’qui se rumeure dans l’coin, le potin quoi. Ou comme disent les jeunEs zapas : « L’information partagée ». En gros, c’est pareil que les potins, mais en plus élégant. » « J’sais rien d’ce truc qui se rumeure ». « Bah voilà, va y avoir une teuf » « Comment ça une teuf ? » Eh beh, on dit une teuf quand y a une bringue, des chansons, un concert quoi. En gros, c’est pas la teuf entre potes en mode vas-y fais tourner, c’est une teuf de musique. » « Ah, ok. Non, j’suis au courant de rien », que j’dis en faisant comme si ça m’intéressait pas, parce que j’sais que ça, c’est c’qui provoque le plus le Riko. Le Riko s’assoit sur le bord du trottoir et me murmure : « Un concert, j’sais pas exactement ni où, ni quand, mais un concert. Genre avec les vrais Caifanes, et puis ma chérie la Ely Guerra, et puis la Vivir Quintana, et puis les Contingentes Jaraneros, et puis le Kevin Kaarl, et puis le Meme del Real. Ensemble, mais pas tous mélangés.

En gros, le tout et les parties, comme on dit. »

« Et où, quand, comment, pourquoi ? », j’lui mets la pression.

« Va savoir », dit le Riko, en allumant ce que je crois être une cigarette, « j’crois qu’ils le disent pas encore parce qu’ils ont peur que la justice leur tombe dessus. »

« Pourquoi la justice leur tomberait dessus ? C’est pour quoi ce concert ? » « Bah pour la rencontre-étreinte avec les familles buscadoras » « Et ça, qu’est-ce que ça a de mal ? Pourquoi les keufs leur tomberaient dessus ? » « Roh mais bordel, bah à cause du Meme, t’es pas au courant qu’ils ont interdit les memes ? Et pis après les keufs, y sont jamais très au courant de rien, et du coup j’crois qu’ils embarquent tous les mecs…et toutes les meufs, ne pas oublier la parité de genre. Pour pas s’louper, qu’ils disent ». « Ah, ouais c’est chaud », je dis en commençant à être dans l’ambiance. « Mais si on sait pas ni quand ni où, comment elle va faire la mif pour v’nir ? », je demande.

« Aucune idée », dit le Riko, « mais j’pense que ça va pas tarder, parce que sinon, bah ouais c’est naze une bringue si personne sait ni où ni quand.

Mais le truc, mon cher capitaine en toc, c’est que personne se fait payer, j’veux dire, ni ceux qui font la zic, ni ceux qui organisent, ni ceux qui produisent, ni ceux qui prêtent le local. Ils récupèrent juste les frais, aucun bénéfice personnel, tout pour la rencontre. D’la vraie bonne solidarité. Et même plus, ni même moi, j’vais les faire payer. J’vais aller comparaître en personne gratuitement. Pour donner un peu, comme on dit, de paillettes et de visibilité à l’événement. Toute la thune est pour la rencontre avec les buscadoras. Tout carré, tout nickel. »

author: Susan Price
title: People’s Climate Summit at COP31: ‘Defend life, rebuild the world!’
content:
As Marxist economist Michael Roberts reported, the United Nations Climate Change Conference 2026 (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, was labeled by climate activists as the “worst COP ever” as delegates divided over the wording of the summit’s final communiqué.

All mention of the need to phase out fossil fuels had, by then, been removed and it fell way short on the climate financing needed for developing nations to deal with climate adaptation and mitigation.

Critics slammed its emphasis on the as-yet untested carbon capture and storage technology as an incentive for the continued investment in fossil fuels and associated infrastructure.

The draft also projected that the world would overshoot 1.5⁰C of global warming.

As Peter Boyle argues in this week’s Green Left: “While the major fossil fuel exporting states, like Australia and Saudi Arabia, are culpable, ultimately it was capitalism and the world’s richest states that hijacked COP31” turning it “into a trade fare for fossil fuel companies, carbon dioxide removal promoters and the AI industry, which descended on Antalya in large numbers to justify the ongoing use of fossil fuels.”

Meanwhile, ecological activists, indigenous peoples and civil society groups came together for a counter People’s Climate Summit in Antalya, from November 14–18. It was organised by three major umbrella organisations of the ecology movement in Türkiye — the Climate Justice Coalition, the Ecology Union and the Environmental Platform of Türkiye.

The summit opened with a march for climate justice, in which thousands participated.

There are restrictions on organising protests in Turkey, with ecological activists reportedly treated as though they are terrorists. Several environmental activists were arrested in the lead up to COP31. In spite of these threats, about 500 people took part in the counter summit, which was assisted by the organisers of the previous People Climate Summit in Belem, Brazil.

Protesters, such as Malaysian climate activist Amalen Sathananthar, also took their protest inside the “blue zone”, interrupting a speech by Murat Kurum, Turkey’s COP president.

As the Guardian reported, “Sathananthar, a member of the Artivist Network, stood on a table holding a noose of red rope around his neck and wearing a T-shirt with the message ‘You are killing the future’ painted on it.

“‘You are killing the future,’ he shouted. ‘Why don’t you just kill me now. The climate crisis is killing us, and you do nothing. You don’t remove fossil fuels, you are killing 1.5C.”

Ahead of the counter summit, Co-Chair of the Pro-Kurdish DEM Parti Tülay Hatimoğulları told the media that states, corporations and civil society groups that support them have “turned COP31 into a pretext to perpetuate a system that is driving the world into darkness and threatening the lives of all living beings”.

The People’s Climate Summit’s adopted a declaration, Defending Life, Rebuilding the World. It slammed the COP’s acceptance of a 1.5⁰C overshoot and demanded that to keep the Earth’s climate stable a safe ecological limit must be 350 parts per million of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.

“Even holding global warming at 1.5°C will have irreversible ecological consequences. It is unacceptable to defer the target to a time when those making the decisions will no longer be alive and to make warming above 1.5°C the new normal for this century,” the declaration said.

“Every increment of warming deepens the destruction and increases irreversible losses. Emissions reduction targets must therefore be revised to meet the needs of nature and peoples, rather than corporate interests. We must insist on avoiding an overshoot and on progressively bringing warming below 1.5°C.”

The declaration highlighted that the climate crisis deepens preexisting inequalities. It rejected “policies that profit from disasters, turn devastation into new opportunities for capital accumulation and use emergencies to entrench exceptional forms of rule and curtail social rights”.

Pointing the blame directly at the economic and political system, the document said: “The climate crisis cannot be understood apart from a capitalist mode of production, that treats nature as something to be used without limit, and human labour as an input whose cost must continually be driven down. The drive to keep accumulating capital is increasingly at odds with the planet’s ecological limits and with what people need to live in dignity.”

The Islamic State (ISIS) militant group has attacked a bus carrying personnel from the Syrian Ministry of Defense in the eastern Syrian province of Deir ez-Zor. The attack took place in al-Baghouz, once ISIS’s last territorial stronghold in Syria.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: ‘I did fear for my life,’ RCMP officer testifies at inquest into shooting death of Rankin Inlet man
content:
In a tense second day at the coroner’s inquest into the death of a 21-year-old Rankin Inlet man, an officer who fired at the victim said that he feared for his safety.


Const. Clark Plaetinck was part of the RCMP’s emergency response team that flew in from Winnipeg on Nov. 6, 2021, while Trey Angootealuk was in a standoff with police. Plaetinck testified that after chemical irritants were deployed through the back window of the truck Angootealuk was in, the man exited with his rifle appearing to be turned toward them.


“I feared for my safety at that point, so I used my firearm to stop him,” Plaetinck told the inquest jury Tuesday in Rankin Inlet.


On Nov. 6, 2021, Angootealuk hijacked a truck, drove it to the outskirts of town, shot at police officers, then began a standoff with police that lasted several hours. Police fatally shot him early the following morning.


The inquest by Nunavut Chief Coroner Marianna Cervantes will determine the circumstances surrounding Angootealuk’s death. It began Monday at the Siniktarvik Hotel in Rankin Inlet and is scheduled to last until Friday. The coroner’s office gave Nunatsiaq News a video link to cover the inquest remotely.


Nikolai Sittman, the Angootealuk family’s lawyer, asked why officers didn’t shoot him somewhere non-fatal.


Plaetnick said they didn’t want to risk missing him because they were shooting from afar.


At one point, during a pause in Plaetnick’s testimony, an audience member could be heard yelling a profanity at him.


Sgt. Russ Hulme, another member of the RCMP’s emergency response team, also testified Tuesday.


He said he flew to Rankin Inlet from Winnipeg the night the standoff began.


Hulme and one other team member launched a gas canister into the stolen truck from its rear window, right before Angootealuk’s death.


Drone footage of that moment was played at the inquest.


It showed Angootealuk exiting the vehicle. Soon after police had shot at him, he laid on the ground outside the driver’s door.


After the footage played, some inquest attendees could be heard crying. Some left the room.


Jury members asked Hulme why his team, which consisted of four members, didn’t consider shooting at the man’s vehicle to immobilize it.


Doing so would not have separated Angootealuk from his gun, and any escalation on their end may have risked a violent reaction from him, Hulme said.


“It sounds like it’s an easy task, but it carries risks,” he said.


Earlier on Tuesday, Sgt. Benjamin Comely, the detachment commander at the time, also testified.

 


Comely said Angootealuk had a tactical advantage at one point during the standoff because of where he was positioned.


“I did fear for my life,” Comely said.

 


Coroner’s inquests are mandatory under Nunavut law for all deaths involving an on-duty police officer. They do not determine the guilt or innocence of anyone involved.


It will resume Tuesday at 9:30 a.m. CT, with more RCMP personnel expected to testify.

author: Dennis Ward
title: Métis country singer Catie St. Germain and her journey from insecurity to the top of the charts
content:
It has only been about three years since Catie St. Germain released his first single but she has been racking up the accolades, ever since.

Growing up, St. Germain says she had a front-row seat to a legendary musician and television host, crushing it on stage every night.

Her grandfather, Ray St. Germain, is a Canadian Country Music Hall of Fame inductee, who also created and hosted a nationally syndicated variety show, Big Sky Country.

However, having a famous grandfather and a very musical family did not ensure she would follow in their footsteps.

St. Germain’s mother even tried to push her in another direction.

“She didn’t have the best experience, I think doing music. The pressure of it all was a lot for her, so, she kind of steered us away. She didn’t want her kids to have to go through the hardships of the music industry and everything,” says St. Germain on the latest episode of Face to Face.

“For a long time I just didn’t think this was something in the cards for me. But I did perform, I did sing. I joined a rock tribute band and was kind of touring with them for a while but I ended up quitting and just having kids myself and thinking it was easier and better to do the 9 to 5 thing and obviously the scheduling worked better for having kids. And then I got back to it though.

“I really wasn’t fulfilled and so I decided to write my original song, The Taxman in 2023 and release that and see what would come of it and it just sparked a whole new passion for me,” adds St. Germain.

The time on the road had St. Germain feeling like she was away from her family all of the time.

Breaking out on her own was also a way to challenge herself and show some bravery.

“I’ve always been somebody who is a little bit more insecure and never would try, I didn’t want to put myself out there. Even in the family too, I would do the family shows with them but I was always the shy one, like I wasn’t the one that was out there, at all. Very shy, very timid. I had my kids and I just really wanted to show them that they could do anything they put their mind to and they can be brave and if I was going to tell them to do that, then I probably should do it too,” says St. Germain.

The reaction to that first song and following EP, Cleaning House (Or Trying) was even more incredible that St. Germain had imagined.

In the three years since then, St. Germain has sang the national anthem at the 2025 CFL Grey Cup in Winnipeg, been named one of Amazon Music’s breakthrough artists, and racked up three number one hits on the Indigenous Music Countdown.

In November at the 2026 Manitoba Country Music Awards, St. Germain was named Female Artist of the Year and took home Interactive Artist, Duo or Group of the Year, for the third straight year.

St. Germain says social media has allowed her to reach a bigger audience.

“I think too, a lot of people get to relate to me as a human, as a person and not just the music, which is really fun. Again, I just create better relationships that way and I think it entices them more to go listen to the music after that,” says St. Germain.

St. Germain’s latest single, a duet with Don Amero called Home hit the Indigenous Music Countdown on November 21.

Her next single, I Ain’t Free will be released on Nov. 27.

Dennis is Métis from southern Manitoba. After spending a decade working in TV in Alberta and Ontario, Dennis returned to Manitoba to join APTN. In 2016, he won a Canadian Association of Journalists award for his story A Soldier Scorned for APTN Investigates. In 2017, he became a host/producer for APTN National News and Face to Face.

author: Fraser Needham
title: AFN calls for strengthening of First Nations Clean Water Act
content:
The national chief of the Assembly of First Nations says the Carney government’s proposed Bill C-37 falls short when it comes to the necessary health, legal and environmental protections to ensure access to clean drinking water.

“Clean drinking water is a human right that has been denied for generations of First Nations families across Canada,” Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak said in a press release.

“Sadly, with Bill C-37, the federal government is still refusing to recognize the human right to water for First Nations in Canada.”

Woodhouse Nepinak was a witness before the Indigenous and Northern Affairs Committee on Tuesday, which is studying the proposed legislation.

The AFN says Bill C-37, also known as the First Nations Clean Water Act, is significantly weaker than legislation drafted by the previous Trudeau government.

Bill C-61, which did not pass because Parliament was prorogued under former prime minister Justin Trudeau, recognized First Nations access to clean drinking water as a human right, but has been weakened under the current legislation to the “progressive realization.”

It took Carney more than a year to reintroduce the new legislation.

According to the United Nations, progressive realization means that states “have a duty to respect, protect and fulfil economic, social and cultural rights,” and are “required to progressively achieve the full realization of these rights over a period of time. Regardless of resource availability, States have an immediate obligation to take appropriate steps to ensure continuous and sustained improvement in the enjoyment of these rights over time.”

The AFN also says the proposed legislation gives provinces a veto, lacks adequate protections for source water and doesn’t live up to Canada’s United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples commitments.

“We are calling on Parliament to take the time needed to work with First Nations on required improvements, clarifications and amendments to Bill C-37 that respect our rights and jurisdiction,” Woodhouse Nepinak said.

Bill C-37 has passed second reading in the House of Commons and is currently in committee.

The previous water legislation was drafted in response to a lawsuit that was settled in 2021.

That bill also included an option for source water protection but failed to pass before Parliament was dissolved for the 2025 election.

The new bill is backed by $4.6 billion in funding over five years, which the federal government describes as the single largest commitment ever made to First Nations water protection.

Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty has said the new legislation was written to “stand the test of time” and insists it does not weaken the protections in the previous bill.

Before joining APTN’s Ottawa bureau, he was news director for the Missinipi Broadcasting Corporation working out of their Prince Albert office. He holds a bachelor of arts degree in political science from Carleton University and a diploma of journalism from Algonquin College.

author: Sonny Melencio
title: Pax Silica: Who benefits, whose industrial strategy? A rejoinder to supporters of Pax Silica
content:
Proponents of Pax Silica promise factories, exports, and skilled jobs. We’ve heard those promises before.

After decades of building export zones and selling electronics abroad, Philippine semiconductor production remains concentrated in assembly, testing and packaging.

Under the terms being offered, Pax Silica will deepen this pattern and further stunt Philippine industrialisation. The government is committing public land, infrastructure and worker training to a foreign-led supply chain without securing the commitments needed to build our own industrial capacity.

The US State Department launched Pax Silica in December 2025 to secure supply chains critical to Washington’s rivalry with China. The founding group included the United States, Israel, Australia, Japan, South Korea, Singapore and Britain. They came to the table with industrial, financial, or technological advantages of their own.

By November 16, the declaration reportedly had 26 signatories, with Singapore and the Philippines reported as the only ASEAN members among them.

The Philippines joined after Washington had set the initiative’s priorities. In an April 9 letter to US Under Secretary of State Jacob Helberg, Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) President Joshua Bingcang proposed a Pax Silica coordination hub in a 4000-acre [1619 hectare] economic security zone in New Clark City, Tarlac.

To sweeten the offer, the BCDA proposed a two-year rent-free period as the Philippine government’s contribution.

Washington has clear economic, geopolitical and military interests in the initiative. It wants reliable access to critical minerals, advanced chips, computing power and data infrastructure. It wants to organise those supply chains around the United States and its partners in its rivalry with China.

Advanced computing serves both civilian and military purposes, and Washington is pursuing Pax Silica alongside its broader military alliance strategy in the Indo-Pacific.

That broader strategy was on display on November 4 in Cebu. On the sidelines of the ASEAN defense ministers’ meeting, US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and his counterparts from the Philippines, Japan and Australia met under the informal grouping known as the “Squad”.

They agreed on a Manila-based coordination centre to align defense investments, intelligence sharing and military deterrence against China.

The Philippines enters this arrangement without a geostrategy of its own. The Philippine Development Plan 2023–2028 gives the state an active role in building infrastructure, training workers and supporting selected industries.

Yet it relies on the neoliberal framework of private investment, public-private partnerships and integration into global supply chains. That leaves investors with considerable power over what gets built and who captures the gains.

This is how dependent capitalism works. Decisions about financing, technology and production are often made abroad.

At home, Philippine oligarchs earn substantial returns from land, property and concessions. For them, building factories, engineering teams and supplier networks takes years of investment with less certain returns.

The semiconductor industry shows where the leverage lies. US-based NVIDIA dominates the market for AI accelerators. Taiwan’s TSMC leads in advanced chip fabrication. The Netherlands’ ASML is the sole commercial supplier of extreme ultraviolet lithography systems. Each controls a capability that takes years and enormous investment to build.

Their governments use these points of leverage to restrict China’s access to advanced technology.

The 2023 agreement among the United States, the Netherlands and Japan covered certain chip-making equipment. Dutch licensing rules restrict exports of advanced ASML machines, while US export controls separately affect certain NVIDIA chip sales and TSMC shipments to China.

The Philippines is offering to host a semiconductor and advanced-manufacturing hub in Tarlac that would serve this supply chain.

The question is what capabilities the country would gain. Building the engineering teams, research institutions, and supplier networks that would give us greater control over what we produce requires an industrial strategy of our own.

Successive Philippine governments have treated access to foreign markets and capital as a substitute for building domestic productive capacity.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Poll: Most Dems Want Congress to Defund War Next Month, Even at Risk of Shutdown
content:
Top Republicans have signaled an openness to defunding the war, as Democrats like Hakeem Jeffries have demurred.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

New polling finds that the majority of Democrats want members of Congress to use next month’s government funding bill to withhold funds for the Iran war, a strategy embraced by progressives and figures like Senate majority leader candidate Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland) to end the war as soon as possible.

According to University of Maryland polling conducted this past weekend, 51 percent of Democrats say that they support the use of the upcoming funding bill, with a deadline of December 11, to defund the war even if it risks a government shutdown or a presidential veto. By contrast, only 16 percent of Democrats said they oppose the idea — a -35 point margin — while 32 percent said they don’t know.

The idea is also narrowly favored when responses from all ideologies are considered, 31 percent support to 28 percent opposition, despite 48 percent of Republicans opposing the idea.

Earlier this month, a group of four senators — Van Hollen, Michael Bennet (D-Colorado), Bernie Sanders (I-Vermont), and Tammy Duckworth (D-Illinois) — vowed in a joint statement to oppose any funding bill that would fund the war. Lawmakers in favor of the effort have made clear that their intention is to effectively dare President Donald Trump to shut down the government in order to fund his war.

“Congress cannot allow Trump to continue his conflict — we must force him to end it,” the lawmakers said. “When we vote on appropriations, we intend to fund the government and stop funds for this war.”

The proposal is imminently achievable. The Washington Post reported this week that top Republicans have said that they are open to allowing the bill to be used to cut off funding for the war in exchange for keeping the government funded. The Post cited Senate Appropriations Committee Chair Susan Collins (R-Maine) and Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-South Dakota) as two Republicans who said they are open to the effort.

Thune said that he is “open to anything that keeps the government funded and makes sure that we’ve got our military and national security requirements and needs met.”

In other words, the Democratic base wants Congress to defund the war at the soonest possible opportunity; several Democrats in Congress are pushing for the proposal; and even Republican leaders may be on board.

Part of the reason for this broad-based support may be the vast unpopularity of the war, in which U.S.-Israeli strikes have killed roughly 3,500 people in Iran.

University of Maryland’s polling found that a staggering 80 percent of Democrats say that they want the war to end now “regardless of the terms,” meaning that they would be fine with accepting any of Iran’s and U.S.’s terms in exchange for the war’s end. A majority of all respondents felt the same, at 55 percent, compared to 21 percent who said they prefer the current course, and 18 percent saying they favor a military escalation.

Experts have said that defunding the war is one of the most effective ways to force President Donald Trump to end the military portion of the war, with options like war powers resolutions unable to force his hand.

Some of the people not in support of the proposal, however, are top Democrats. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York) said last week that he opposes even the idea of barring funds from being used for the war, in favor of a war powers resolution that the Trump administration is likely to ignore. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-New York), facing a challenge to his leadership from one of the top Senate champions of the proposal to defund the war, has been mum on the issue.

The top Democrat on the House Appropriations Committee, Rosa DeLauro (Connecticut), has suggested that she does not want to use the continuing resolution to shut down the war.

“I think that the American people would like to see us end the war. I also believe that the American people may not believe that shutting the government down ends the war,” she said last week, her comments undercut by polling finding otherwise.

As Trump cracks down on political speech, independent media is increasingly necessary.

author: Rindala Alajaji
title: New York and California Age Gating Rules Go Into Effect in the New Year
content:
Come January 2027, everyday social media browsing in two of the country's largest states will look noticeably different. In California, AB 1709 (2026), AB 1043 (2025), and SB 976 (2024) are slated to take effect on January 1, 2027. Meanwhile, state attorney general regulations for New York’s Stop Addictive Feeds Exploitation (SAFE) for Kids Act take effect on January 25, 2027.

EFF has opposed these laws across legislatures, regulatory proceedings, and the courts. The core problem is simple: age-gating mandates trade away everyday user privacy and free expression under the guise of safety, while pushing platforms to gather even more personal data on users.

Three interlocking California laws take effect on January 1, 2027, reshaping how platforms handle age checks and design features for young users. First, SB 976 (2024) requires verifiable parental consent before platforms can offer algorithmic feeds or nighttime notifications to anyone under 18. Second, AB 1709 (2026) goes even further by outright banning "addictive features," including personalized recommendation algorithms, autoplay, and endless scroll, for users under 16, even with parental permission. Third, the Digital Age Assurance Act (AB 1043, 2025) mandates age-assurance checks across devices (operating systems) and apps, serving as the enforcement backbone for those restrictions. Together with the California Attorney General’s proposed rules on SB 976, which outline age-gating methods, accuracy, circumvention, and parental consent, these laws force platforms into a two-tier design that walls young people off from basic content-discovery tools, puts everyone's privacy at risk to prove their age, and has already drawn First Amendment lawsuits from social media companies against both SB 976 and AB 1709.

For example: rather than minimizing corporate surveillance and data collection by passing stronger privacy laws, the SB 976 regulations encourage companies to evaluate behavioral patterns, collected user data, digital interactions, and metadata to estimate age (Sec. 561(a)(2)), alongside location data collected for other purposes (Sec. 565). Good privacy laws should discourage collecting that information in the first place, not reward broader tracking.

At the same time, these age assurance rules build in steep error rates and weak safeguards. They acknowledge that age-verification tools can misclassify young people as adults, allowing false-positive rates of up to 8% for 16-year-olds and 15% for 17-year-olds (Sec. 561(c)(4)(iv)). Yet the rules set no benchmarks at all for false negatives, meaning adults (especially 18- to 20-year-olds) are likely to be wrongly flagged as under 18. They also recognize demographic bias in facial recognition, yet offer no concrete fix, vaguely telling companies to take mitigating measures like correcting dataset imbalances (Sec. 563(a)(6)). While users can appeal wrong age estimates, the rules set no firm deadlines, meaning mistakes can drag on without a prompt fix, blocking user access (Sec. 564). Worse, requiring platforms to let users report others they suspect are under the age of 18 (Sec. 567) invites targeted harassment by bad actors, while rules telling companies to account for users trying to “conceal or misrepresent” their California location (Sec. 565) risk penalizing everyday VPN users.

Along the same lines as the California regulations, New York’s SAFE for Kids Act restricts personalized recommendations and nighttime notifications (between midnight and 6am) without required consent, and mandates that platforms run age assurance and determine user location. If a user does not verify their age or is estimated to be under-18, they will either be relegated to an account with no personalized recommendations and nighttime notifications (if the platform creates one), or prohibited from accessing the platform/service.

As we detailed in our December 2025 comments to the New York Attorney General, age-verification mandates inevitably chill access to online speech. And the final regulations introduce several troubling specifics.

The New York regulations use broad definitions for "age estimation," "age inference," and "age verification" (700.1(h)–(j)) that push companies to collect and retain more personal information from users. Even where privacy protections apply to that information, users cannot sue or enforce those rights themselves, since enforcement rests solely with the Attorney General (700.8). Worse, the rule’s …

author: Amy Goodman
title: Huang’s Return to Nvidia Shows the Unsustainable Power of AI Over the Economy
content:
The scandal over Jensen Huang reflects efforts from establishment hawks to ramp up hostilities between the US and China.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Nvidia stock prices surged over 30% on Monday as the chip maker reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Huang had stepped down earlier in November amid reports he had multiple extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China. Huang and Nvidia have been central to the AI boom, and the leadership turmoil had erased trillions in value from the U.S. stock market. President Donald Trump acknowledged he had encouraged the company’s board to bring Huang back.

“The fact that our markets are so over-indexed on the AI trade, that something like three-fourths of gains in the [S&P 500] this past year have been AI-related, is unsustainable,” says Aya Ibrahim, senior fellow for economic and national security at the AI Now Institute.

We also speak with organizer and researcher Tobita Chow, who says Huang’s “spy scandal” that led to his ouster is part of a larger effort by anti-China figures in the U.S. national security establishment to escalate tensions between the countries.

“The national security leadership in both parties in D.C. has been greatly frustrated with President Trump, who has over the past year pursued policies to maintain very warm relations with Xi Jinping,” says Chow, who notes that Secretary of State Marco Rubio is one of the “chief” frustrated China hawks in the administration.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: Jensen Huang is back as CEO of the chip giant Nvidia, after President Trump personally called into a company board meeting Sunday to push for Huang’s reinstatement. Huang had resigned less than two weeks ago, after news reports revealed he had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who was allegedly in communication with China’s top spy agency. The woman worked with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company suspected of buying advanced Nvidia chips, then diverting them to China in violation of U.S. export rules. On Monday, the Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist.

During an interview on CNBC, Trump was questioned about his role reinstating Huang.

EAMON JAVERS: Mr. President, did you give the board of directors an assurance that Jensen Huang would not be prosecuted at all for any of these —

PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: I didn’t use the word “prosecuted.”

EAMON JAVERS: — questions around export controls?

PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: But I said — I said that we believe — and I put out a statement. I think you probably saw that.

PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: That we believe he’s fine, he’s absolutely fine. I gave them enough —

CARL QUINTANILLA: There was a —

PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: — assurance.

AMY GOODMAN: President Trump also admitted that falling stock prices played a role in his decision to push for Huang to be reinstated. After Huang resigned, Nvidia’s stock fell sharply, along with those of several other AI and technology companies with ties to Nvidia.

One major holder of Nvidia stock has been Cantor Fitzgerald. The Wall Street investment firm is run by the sons of Howard Lutnick, Cantor’s former CEO, who serves as President Trump’s commerce secretary. Cantor Fitzgerald held shares in Nvidia worth hundreds of millions of dollars. The New York Times reports Lutnick pushed to weaken chip export rules that overlapped with his family’s business.

The Financial Times reports President Trump personally made up to $15 million on Monday alone, after Nvidia’s stock soared 30% following Huang’s return.

On Monday, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani responded to the Nvidia news and its impact on working people.

MAYOR ZOHRAN MAMDANI: I do not think that working people across the country signed up for their pensions being tied to the question of Jensen Huang’s fidelity to his marriage. And yet, for many days, that had a massive impact. And what we’re also talking about here, speaking about Mr. Huang, we’re speaking about a divorce settlement that has been rumored to be around $81 billion. That would be the cost of providing universal childcare for every 3- and 4-year-old in the United States of America for an entire year.

And a lot of this just brings to mind what Justice Brandeis said quite some time ago, which is that we can have democracy, we can have great wealth …

title: Bağdat, Kürdistan'ın tüm sınır kapıları ve Erbil kontrolündeki bazı petrol sahalarının devrini emretti stedi
content:
Irak'ta federal hükümet ile Kürdistan Bölgesel Yönetimi (KBY) arasında petrol kaynaklarının işletilmesi, gelirlerin paylaşılması ve tartışmalı bölgelerin statüsü konusunda yıllardır süregelen anlaşmazlık büyüdü: Irak Başbakanı'nın federal güvenlik güçlerine ve kamu kurumlarına verdiği bir dizi talimatla Erbil'in sınır kapıları ve petrol sahalarındaki yetkileri kaldırıldı.


Bağdat'ın kararları


Başbakanın askeri sözcüsü Sabah en-Numan, devlete ait Kuzey Petrol Şirketi sahalarından petrol kaçırıldığı iddialarını araştıran soruşturma komisyonunun raporunun değerlendirilmesinin ardından alınan kararları açıkladı.


Irak Başbakanı'nın talimatları uyarınca:


Kürdistan Bölgesi'nin bütün sınır kapıları Federal Sınır Kapıları İdaresi'nin denetimine geçirilecek.


Kerkük, Diyala, Selahaddin ve Ninova vilayetlerinde Kürt güvenlik güçlerinin denetimindeki ve Bağdat'ın federal Petrol Bakanlığına ait olduğunu belirttiği petrol sahalarının yönetimi Bakanlığa, güvenliği ise federal enerji polisine devredilecek.


KBY, federal Petrol Bakanlığı'nın bilgisi dışında ham petrol ve petrol ürünleri ihracatına izin veremeyecek.


Kürdistan Bölgesi'nin komşu ülkelerle arasındaki gayriresmî sınır geçişleri kapatılacak.


Kürdistan Bölgesi ile söz konusu dört Irak vilayeti arasındaki gayriresmî geçiş yollarının kapatılması için iki ortak güvenlik tugayı görevlendirilecek.


Erbil, Süleymaniye ve Duhok girişlerinde petrol ürünlerinin denetlenmesi için kontrol noktaları kurulacak.


Bağdat yönetimi, kararların ülkenin egemenliğini ve ulusal servetini korumayı amaçladığını savunuyor. Kararların uygulanmasına ilişkin henüz bir takvim açıklanmadı.


Mesrur Barzani: “Hiçbir şekilde kabul edilemez”


KBY Başbakanı Mesrur Barzani, Erbil'de düzenlenen Dünya Gençlik Zirvesi'nde gazetecilerin sorularını yanıtlarken Bağdat'ın kararlarının kısa süre önce gerçekleştirilen görüşmelerde varılan mutabakatla çeliştiğini söyledi:


“Bugün Bağdat'tan çıkan kararlar bizi şaşırttı. Çünkü içerikleri federal makamlarla önceki görüşmelerimizde ulaştığımız sonuçlarla örtüşmüyor.”


Kararları “hiçbir şekilde kabul edilemez” olarak nitelendiren Barzani, anlaşmazlıkların anayasa temelinde çözülmesi için müzakereleri sürdürmeye hazır olduklarını belirtti.


Barzani, 9 Kasım'da Bağdat'ta Irak Başbakanı Zeydi ile bir araya gelmişti. Görüşmede petrol kaynaklarının anayasa uyarınca yönetilmesi ve federal petrol ve doğal gaz yasasının çıkarılması ele alınmıştı.


Irak Halk Seferberlik Güçleri (Haşdi Şabi) Başkanı Falih Feyyad da 21 Kasım'da Erbil'de Kürdistan Bölgesi'nin yöneticileriyle görüşmüştü. KBY, görüşmelerin ardından anlaşmazlıkların anayasa çerçevesinde ve diyalog yoluyla çözülmesi konusunda mutabakata varıldığını açıklamıştı.


KDP ve KYB: “Kürdistan'ın hakları kırmızı çizgimiz”


Bağdat'ın kararları, Ekim 2024'teki Kürdistan Parlamentosu seçimlerinden bu yana yeni bölgesel hükümetin oluşturulması konusunda anlaşamayan iki büyük Kürt partisini ortak tutum almaya yöneltti.


Mesud Barzani liderliğindeki Kürdistan Demokrat Partisi (KDP) ile Bafıl Talabani liderliğindeki Kürdistan Yurtseverler Birliği (KYB), 24 Kasım'da yayımladıkları ortak bildiride Kürdistan Bölgesi'nin, anayasal hakları dışında herhangi bir talepte bulunmadığını, buna karşılık bölgenin anayasal haklarının yıllardır ihlal edildiğini belirttiler.


İki parti, federal hükümet ve Kürdistan Bölgesi arasındaki anlaşmazlıklarda anayasanın nihai başvuru mercii olması gerektiğini vurguladı:


“Kürdistan Bölgesi'nin haklarına ve kazanımlarına yönelik her türlü ihlal kırmızı çizgidir.”


Kürdistan Bölgesi'nin Kürdistan halkının onlarca yıllık mücadelesinin ürünü olduğunu hatırlatan KDP ve KYB, "anayasal çerçeve dışında alınan kararları reddettiklerini, diyalog, şeffaflık ve karşılıklı anlayış yoluyla çözümü desteklediklerini" açıkladılar.


Mesud Barzani: “Boyun eğmeyeceğiz”


KDP Başkanı Mesud Barzani de akşam saatlerinde yayımladığı açıklamada Irak'taki karar merkezlerinde federalizmin ilkelerini ve Kürt halkının haklarını ihlal etmeye yönelik bir hareket geliştiğini söyledi.


Barzani, Saddam Hüseyin rejiminin devrilmesinin ardından kabul edilen anayasanın Irak'ın bütün halklarının haklarını güvence altına alacağına ilişkin beklentilerin karşılanmadığını, Kürt halkının haklarının giderek daha fazla ihlal edildiğini belirtti.


Irak Başbakanı'nın yolsuzluk ve kaçakçılıkla mücadelesini desteklediklerini, ancak bu mücadelenin hukuki ve anayasal yollarla yürütülmesi gerektiğini vurgulayan Barzani şöyle dedi …

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: Nunavut’s child advocate accuses minister of Family Services of delivering ‘absolutely, patently untrue’ statement to legislature
content:
Nunavut’s child advocate says information presented to the territory’s legislature by the minister of Family Services regarding child welfare issues was “absolutely, patently untrue.” 


Jane Bates, the Representative for Children and Youth Nunavut, told APTN News that Gwen Healy Akearok has on multiple occasions made false statements to the territorial legislature.

 


According to Bates, in a May 22 statement, Akearok said her department had “completed a full update of our standards and procedures manual, which now reflects best practices in social work with a priority focus on Inuit culture and maintaining connection to family.”


Bates said she was astonished to hear this announcement.


“I was listening to it thinking, ‘What? Hang on here,’” she said. “So I went back to them and I said, ‘You don’t have any section for children in care and you have no section for foster care. How is it that you’ve got a comprehensive standards and procedures manual?’”


More recently, Bates took issue with the way Healy Akearok handled the acknowledgment that DFS had given incorrect numbers on children in care to the media. 


On Oct. 22, Healy Akearok rose in the legislature and said, “Recent public reporting has raised important questions about information previously provided by Family Services regarding children and youth receiving services. The department identified errors in the information initially provided, apologized, and supplied corrected information before publication.”


Bates, who said she was the one who identified the wrong information, took umbrage at the minister’s claim that her department identified the errors itself.


“That is absolutely, patently untrue,” said Bates. “That is not what happened.”


In fact,

CBC’s reporting acknowledged

 “Nunavut’s representative for children and youth Jane Bates, thought that figure looked suspiciously low, so CBC News asked the department for further clarity.”


Bates provided APTN the text of a letter she wrote to the minister, in which she described Healy Akearok’s statement to the legislature as “factually inaccurate,” adding “your statement inaccurately attributes the identification of the error to the department and implies that it was corrected before the inaccurate information was published.”


Bates also forwarded the text of Healy Akearok’s response, which read, “Thank you for your message, advice, and recommendations. At this time, after careful review, we’re satisfied with the information that was presented in the Assembly.”


Nunavut Legislative Assembly. Photo: APTN


“To be honest,” said Bates, “there are moments when it’s like pure dishonesty around what has been done. I have on numerous occasions caught the department telling me something that’s factually inaccurate.”


APTN has repeatedly requested interviews with Healy Akearok to discuss the issue of child welfare in Nunavut. At first, her office was open to scheduling an interview, but after several follow-ups, we’ve received no response. 


APTN also reached out to Premier John Main, who told

APTN News InFocus

 in May that the territory recognized the need for improvement and was “committed to making improvements” to the child welfare system. His office did not reply to our requests for an interview.

 


‘If I’m being perfectly honest, I’m angry’


Allegations of dishonesty are far from the only source of frustration for Bates, who said the DFS has sat for years on recommendations she’s made for its improvement since 2020.


“If I’m being perfectly honest, I’m angry,” Bates told APTN.

  


In September, Bates tabled her

2025-26 annual

report.

 It noted a series of worsening circumstances, such as the fact that reports of sexualized violence jumped from eight events in 2024-25 to 22 events in 2025-26, though it added, “The Department of Family Services’ reporting of critical injuries also remains problematic, and the figures provided cannot be considered accurate or reliable.”


Bates told APTN that the unwillingness of the department to implement changes is deepening an already longstanding crisis in child protection.


“I’m angry that the department has not made significant change [or] improvement — this is now the fifth report,” she told APTN. “There was one in 2011, 2014, and then in 2023, of course, the report that declared that child welfare was a crisis in Nunavut. And then now we fast-forward to 2025: there were no significant changes again.”

author: CMI Argentina
title: Milton Tolomeo suspendió su huelga de hambre
content:
El preso político Milton Tolomeo, encarcelado por haber participado del rechazo popular contra la regresiva reforma laboral, suspendió la medida tras lograr una serie de conquistas en favor de todo su pabellón.


Compartimos el comunicado de la Coordinadora por la libertad de lxs presxs políticxs:


Milton suspende su huelga de hambre


Luego de haber sostenido dos semanas de huelga de hambre, Milton Tolomeo, preso por haber participado de la movilización popular contra la reforma laboral, decidió suspender la medida porque logró una serie de conquistas en favor de todo su pabellón.


Los detenidos del módulo 4 sector A3B derecho interpusieron un Habeas Corpus Colectivo Correctivo para exigir mejoras en las condiciones de alojamiento del Complejo Penitenciario Federal nº VIII al que fueron trasladados.


A través de este recurso y de otras gestiones judiciales, y tras una audiencia con el Juzgado Federal de Morón, representantes de distintos sectores del personal del complejo se entrevistaron con Milton y se comprometieron a garantizar la puesta en marcha de sus reclamos: acceso a la salud, derecho de estudiar y trabajar, restitución de pertenencias, provisión de agua potable, etcétera.


Es por ello que Milton aceptó suspender por el momento la medida de fuerza, supeditado a que todo lo informado por las autoridades judiciales y penitenciarias se cumpla. Caso contrario, retomará la huelga.


Nuestro compañero está entero, se siente bien de salud y a la espera de que el Servicio Penitenciario cumpla lo que se comprometió a hacer.


Una vez más, decimos todos juntos que luchar sirve.

title: Polis Akademisi Başkanı Prof. Dr. Murat Balcı görevden alındı
content:
Resmi Gazete'de yayımlanan atama kararlarıyla Polis Akademisi Başkanı Prof. Dr. Murat Balcı görevden alındı, yerine Doç. Dr. Mehmet İlker Haktankaçmaz getirildi.

Balcı, Türkiye Emlak Katılım Bankası Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Vekilliği ve Katılım Finans Kefalet AŞ Yönetim Kurulu Başkanlığı görevlerini yürütüyor.

Prof. Dr. Murat Balcı, ceza hukuku alanındaki akademik çalışmaları ve spor hukuku görevleriyle tanınıyor. Rize’deki ilk ve orta öğreniminin ardından Marmara Üniversitesi Hukuk Fakültesi’nden 2002’de mezun oldu. Aynı üniversitede kamu hukuku alanında yüksek lisansını 2004’te, doktorasını 2009’da tamamladı. Ceza ve ceza muhakemesi hukuku alanında 2010’da yardımcı doçent, 2014’te doçent, 2019’da profesör oldu.

Doğuş Üniversitesi’nde görev yaptıktan sonra Fatih Sultan Mehmet Vakıf Üniversitesi Hukuk Fakültesi’ne geçti; 2024’te fakülte dekanı oldu. Kasım 2024’te Polis Akademisi Başkanlığına atanan Balcı, bu görevi yürütüyor.

Balcı, 2012-2022 arasında Türkiye Futbol Federasyonu Tahkim Kurulunda başkanvekilliği ve başkanlık yaptı. Ceza hukuku, spor hukuku ve bankacılık hukuku alanlarında kitap ve makaleler yazdı.

Türkiye Emlak Katılım Bankası Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Vekilliği ve Katılım Finans Kefalet AŞ Yönetim Kurulu Başkanlığı görevlerini yürüttü.

title: Τζιχάντ Αλσομάλι: Η εκπαίδευση υπό γενοκτονία. Το πανεπιστήμιο, το μποϊκοτάζ και πώς να οργανωθούμε για την Παλαιστίνη
content:
Images of war 23-25 from Gaza, by Jaber Badwen


ΣΥΝΕΝΤΕΥΞΗ ΤΟΥ ΠΑΛΑΙΣΤΙΝΙΟΥ ΤΖΙΧΑΝΤ ΑΛΣΟΜΑΛΙ από την Πρωτοβουλία Πανεπιστημιακών ΑΠΘ ΠΑΜΑΚ ΔΙΠΑΕ


Τη μέρα της επετείου της εξέγερσης του Πολυτεχνείου στη Θεσσαλονίκη η Πρωτοβουλία Πανεπιστημιακών ΑΠΘ-ΠΑΜΑΚ-ΔΙΠΑΕ συζήτησε και πήρε συνέντευξη από τον Παλαιστίνιο

Τζιχάντ Αλσομάλι

, μέλος του Διοικητικού Συμβουλίου του

BADIL* (Παλαιστινιακό Κέντρο Πόρων για τα Δικαιώματα Διαμονής και τα Δικαιώματα των Προσφύγων)

 σχετικά με τα εκπαιδευτικά ιδρύματα στην Παλαιστίνη σήμερα, το εκπαιδευτικό μποϋκοτάζ ενάντια στο κράτος του Ισραήλ, καθώς και τις στάσεις των παλαιστινιακών κομμάτων απέναντι στη γενοκτονία. Παρακάτω οι αποκρίσεις του σε τέσσερα συγκεκριμένα ερωτήματά μας.


>Η γενοκτονία του Ισραήλ κατά του παλαιστινιακού λαού περιλαμβάνει την καταστροφή σχολείων και πανεπιστημίων στη Λωρίδα της Γάζας. Ποια είναι η σημερινή κατάσταση της εκπαίδευσης στη Λωρίδα της Γάζας και στη Δυτική Όχθη, συμπεριλαμβανομένης και της Ιερουσαλήμ;


Αυτό που συμβαίνει στην εκπαίδευση στη Γάζα δεν είναι «παράπλευρες απώλειες πολέμου». Είναι η εξόντωση της ίδιας της εκπαίδευσης, scholasticide, όπως την ονομάζουν εμπειρογνώμονες του ΟΗΕ, και αποτελεί αναπόσπαστο μέρος της γενοκτονίας κατά του παλαιστινιακού λαού. Οι αριθμοί μιλούν από μόνοι τους:


Σύμφωνα με την τελευταία της αξιολόγηση (Ιούλιος 2025), η

Ομάδα Εκπαίδευσης του ΟΗΕ

 εκτιμά ότι 518 από τα 564 σχολικά κτίρια (91,8%) χρειάζονται πλήρη ανοικοδόμηση ή εκτεταμένη αποκατάσταση για να λειτουργήσουν ξανά

1

.


Σύμφωνα με τη

UNICEF

, έως τον Απρίλιο του 2026, 700.000 παιδιά ηλικίας τεσσάρων έως δεκαεπτά ετών είχαν στερηθεί σχεδόν

τρία συνεχόμενα σχολικά έτη δια ζώσης εκπαίδευσης

, και περισσότερα από 420.000 παιδιά εξακολουθούν να τη στερούνται μέχρι σήμερα

2

.


Έως τον Ιούλιο του 2026, το

Παλαιστινιακό Κέντρο για τα Ανθρώπινα Δικαιώματα

 είχε καταγράψει τη δολοφονία περίπου 20.051 μαθητών και φοιτητών, περισσότερων από 830 εκπαιδευτικών και εργαζομένων στην εκπαίδευση, και περισσότερων από 194 πανεπιστημιακών και ερευνητών

3

.


Έχουν σκοτωθεί περισσότεροι από 1.372 φοιτητές και 246 πανεπιστημιακοί και εργαζόμενοι πανεπιστημίων, ανάμεσά τους και αρχειονόμοι

4

.


Προσέξτε τους αρχειονόμους. Στόχος δεν είναι μόνο το κτίριο, αλλά η μνήμη και τα μυαλά που παράγουν και μεταδίδουν την παλαιστινιακή γνώση. Στο BADIL το βλέπουμε ως έναν κρίκο σε μια αποικιακή δομή που συνεχίζεται από τη Νάκμπα. Το 1948 λεηλατήθηκαν οι παλαιστινιακές βιβλιοθήκες μαζί με τα σπίτια· σήμερα εξαφανίζονται τα πανεπιστήμια μαζί με τις πόλεις. Ο στόχος είναι ο ίδιος: ένας λαός χωρίς μνήμη δεν διεκδικεί την επιστροφή.


Κι όμως, οι άνθρωποι αντιστέκονται. Τον Σεπτέμβριο του 2026, εκατοντάδες χιλιάδες παιδιά επέστρεψαν σε τάξεις μέσα σε

σκηνές και πρόχειρα καταλύματα

, και τα πανεπιστήμια συνεχίζουν να διδάσκουν εξ αποστάσεως κάτω από τα ερείπια. Όμως οι βομβαρδισμοί δεν σταμάτησαν. Στα τέλη Οκτωβρίου 2026, η

Επιτροπή Έκτακτης Ανάγκης των Πανεπιστημίων της Γάζας

 καταδίκασε τις νέες επιθέσεις στο

Ισλαμικό Πανεπιστήμιο

 και κάλεσε σε «επείγουσα κλιμάκωση» της διεθνούς ακαδημαϊκής αλληλεγγύης.


Στη Δυτική Όχθη, η ίδια γενοκτονία εκτυλίσσεται με πιο αργό ρυθμό. Τα περιστατικά που έπληξαν την εκπαίδευση σχεδόν διπλασιάστηκαν το τρίτο τρίμηνο του 2026 (185 περιστατικά) σε σύγκριση με την ίδια περίοδο του 2025, και αφορούσαν 149 σχολεία και σχεδόν 28.000 μαθητές και εργαζόμενους στην εκπαίδευση

5

.

Ογδόντα τέσσερα σχολεία

 στη Ζώνη Γ και στην Ανατολική Ιερουσαλήμ βρίσκονται ακόμη υπό απειλή κατεδάφισης ή εντολών διακοπής εργασιών.

Η κανονική φοίτηση έχει διακοπεί για περισσότερους από 4.000 μαθητές

 που εκτοπίστηκαν από τους προσφυγικούς καταυλισμούς της βόρειας Δυτικής Όχθης, ενώ

έξι σχολεία

 της

UNRWA

 στην Ανατολική Ιερουσαλήμ παραμένουν κλειστά. Αυτό το τελευταίο δεν είναι λεπτομέρεια: είναι μέρος του πολέμου κατά της UNRWA, δηλαδή κατά του διεθνούς μάρτυρα του προσφυγικού ζητήματος και του δικαιώματος της επιστροφής.


Δύο πύλες, δύο πανεπιστήμια, πενήντα δύο χρόνια απόσταση. Στις 17 Νοεμβρίου 1973, ένα τανκ της χούντας γκρέμισε την πύλη του

Πολυτεχνείου

 της Αθήνας. Στις 6 Ιανουαρίου 2026, στρατιώτες της κατοχής γκρέμισαν την πύλη του

Πανεπιστημίου Μπιρζέιτ

 και άνοιξαν πυρ αδιακρίτως σε μια πανεπιστημιούπολη με περισσότερους από 8.000 φοιτητές, πράξη που εμπειρογνώμονες του ΟΗΕ χαρακτήρισαν συστηματική πολιτική και όχι περιστασιακή βία

6

. Ο χρόνος και ο τόπος άλλαξαν, όμως

author: CMI Argentina
title: ¿Cuánto aguanta el dólar barato?
content:
El salto del riesgo país volvió a poner bajo presión al esquema cambiario. Economistas advierten sobre las tensiones de las bandas y el costo de sostener la divisa estable. ¿Ya nadie confía en el plan de Milei?


24/11/2026


La tensión financiera volvió a trasladarse al mercado cambiario. El 20, “viernes negro”, el riesgo país superó los 1.000 puntos básicos, para llegar este martes 24 hasta su máximo anual de 1.100, y el dólar registró nuevas subas en sus distintas cotizaciones, en jornadas marcadas por la caída de los bonos argentinos en Wall Street.


El movimiento expone las dudas de los inversores sobre el programa financiero del Gobierno, la capacidad de acumular reservas y la sostenibilidad del esquema económico de cara a 2027.


Los números del viernes negro


El indicador que elabora JP Morgan trepó hasta los 1.038 puntos, luego de avanzar 103 en un día, lo que lo colocó en su nivel más alto desde octubre de 2025. En paralelo, los bonos argentinos perdieron en promedio un 3,5% en la plaza neoyorquina y acumularon una baja semanal del 6%. En lo que va del año, los precios de la deuda argentina en dólares retrocedieron, en promedio, un 17%.


La presión también se reflejó en el mercado cambiario. El dólar mayorista cerró en $1.579, mientras que el minorista llegó a $1.595 en el Banco Nación. Entre las cotizaciones financieras, el MEP alcanzó los $1.676 y el contado con liquidación (CCL), los $1.782. La brecha entre este último y el tipo de cambio mayorista se ubicó en torno al 13%, el registro más elevado desde octubre del año pasado.


Sin pausa después del feriado


Luego del fin de semana extendido por el feriado trasladado del Día de la Soberanía, este martes el dólar minorista superó los $1.615 en el Banco Nación y el mayorista subió a $1.593. En cuanto a los tipos de cambios financieros, el CCL se disparó más de 5% y cotiza cercano a los $1.800, con una brecha de más del 13% frente al mayorista; mientras que el MEP llegó a operar arriba de los $1.705.


Las causas


El contexto internacional explica sólo en parte la situación vernácula, que es por demás preocupante.


Como consecuencia de la apertura económica del modelo Milei-Caputo, el mercado argentino quedó expuesto a cualquier cimbronazo puertas afuera. En este marco, los retrocesos en Wall Street y las tasas estadounidenses en alza afectaron con mayor fuerza a los mercados emergentes.


Pero las dudas también tienen raíces locales: la desaceleración de las compras de divisas del Banco Central, las necesidades de financiamiento y la incertidumbre política cuando comienza a acercarse el calendario electoral de 2027 hicieron lo suyo.


Las compras netas de dólares del BCRA promediaron apenas 32 millones diarios durante noviembre, hasta el día 13. La cifra contrasta con los 66 millones de octubre y los 77 millones de promedio diario acumulados en lo que va del año.


Las expectativas


La preocupación no se limita a los vencimientos inmediatos. El analista Emilio Botto, del grupo Mills Capital, señaló en declaraciones a

Infobae

 que en enero el Tesoro deberá afrontar pagos por unos 4.500 millones de dólares a tenedores privados de bonos y que, según estimaciones de economistas del mercado local, las necesidades adicionales de financiamiento para todo 2027 podrían alcanzar al menos los 8.000 millones. También advirtió que algunas fuentes de divisas que estuvieron disponibles este año podrían no repetirse con la misma magnitud.


Parece que el mercado no está dispuesto a seguir sosteniendo el dólar barato que quiere el gobierno.


Flotar es una cosa. Que se los lleven puestos (con Cepo) y tengan que dejarlo subir es otra…


— Carlos Rodriguez (@carod2015)

November 20, 2026


La tensión financiera puede trasladarse, además, al crédito y la actividad. En los próximos días vencen títulos en pesos por unos 25 billones; en diciembre, por 37 billones, y en enero, por 42 billones. La consultora LCG considera que el Tesoro podría renovar esos compromisos, aunque probablemente deba convalidar tasas más altas. Ese encarecimiento repercute sobre el financiamiento de empresas y familias y puede profundizar el freno económico.


Los economistas también pusieron el foco en las tensiones del propio esquema cambiario. En su cuenta de X, Mariano Calixto Fernández, examigo de Javier Milei, cuestionó la regla que ajusta las bandas cambiarias según la inflación pasada: “El Gobierno cometió el error de atrasar el tipo de cambio para bajar la inflación de forma …
