title: Erkunt’ta satış sonrası işçileri ne bekliyor?
content:
Ankara— Erkunt Sanayi A.Ş., Sincan ve Etimesgut'taki fabrikaları ile nisan ayında Hisarlar Makina'ya satılmıştı. Eylül başında yönetim değişikliği tamamlanırken işçiler yeni yönetimden ücret ve çalışma koşullarının beklentisi içerisindeydi. Yeni yönetimle geçen iki ayın ardından Erkunt işçileri ile konuştuk.

Eski yönetime dair çeşitli iddia ve dedikoduların fabrikada yayıldığını anlatan bir döküm işçisi, ''Eski yönetimin mâli hesaplarında bir sürü usulsüzlük olduğuna dair dedikodular duyduk. Buna bizim banka promosyonlarımız da dahil. Yıllardır burada çalışıyorum. İlk defa son banka promosyonunda brüt maaşa endeksli yatırıldı. Kişi başı 100-150 bin TL gibi rakamlar konuşurken herkese 50-60 bin TL yattı. Eski personel müdürünün işine de son verilmiş, mahkemelik oldular diye duyduk eski yönetim için. Şimdi yeni yönetim bu hesapların hepsinin üstüne gidecekmiş. Bizim beklentimiz de öyle yapması. Bizim hakkımızı yiyen varsa cezasını alsın. Varsa haklarımızı versinler'' dedi. Görüştüğümüz başka işçiler de bu iddiaları duyduklarını söylüyor.

Yeni yönetimin Etimesgut'taki fabrikada işçilerin de katıldığı bir toplantı yaptığını aktaran işçiler, ''Ne şikayetiniz varsa söyleyin çözülecek” dediler. Şuan için malzeme eksikliklerinde bir sorun yok. Yemekhane koşulları, yemekler de çok iyileşti. Ancak Hisarlar'ı ilk satın aldıklarında işçilere ek zam verildiğini duyduk. Aynı beklenti bizde de var. Bizim beklentimiz çok ama esas sözleşmede göreceğiz ne kadar işçiyi düşündüklerini'' dediler.

Ek zamma dair somut bir gelişme yokken beyaz yakalı işçiler, kendi çift maaşlarının kesildiğini anlattılar: ''Bizim normalde çift maaş aldığımız aylar vardı. Yeni yönetim sizin eski yönetimle anlaşmanız bizi bağlamaz diyip kestirip attı. Telafi olarak da Ocak ayında fazladan zam yapacağız dediler ama ne kadar yaparlar, bizim çift maaş ikramiyelerini kurtarır mı bilmiyoruz. Biz açıkçası endişeliyiz. Ödeme planlarımızı buna göre ayarlamıştık. Şimdi ne olacak belli bile değil.''

Erkunt'un geçtiğimiz günlere kadar 3 farklı taşeron firma ile anlaşması vardı. Yeni yönetim, bunlardan en büyüğü ile anlaşmasını geçtiğimiz haftalarda sonlandırdı. İşine son verilen taşeron işçilerden kimileri kadroya alınırken kimileri işten çıkarıldı. Kadroya alınan işçilerin başlangıç ücreti de tartışmalara sebep oldu. Etimesgut döküm fabrikasından bir işçi, ''Ben 4 yıldır bu fabrikada çalışıyorum. 1-2 senedir taşeronda çalışanları 60 bin TL'den başlatmışlar diye duyduk. Benim kendi maaşım daha o kadar değil. Bize de iyileştirme yapmaları lazım'' derken, 6 ay önce işe başladığını söyleyen başka bir işçiyse ''Bana verdikleri para 43 bin TL. Ben 6 ay önce taşerondan işe girmiş olsam ve şuan kadroya alınsam en az 50 bin TL verirlerdi bana da. Bize de iyileştirme şart'' dedi.

Erkunt'taki son TİS sürecine işçiler ve yetkili Türk-Metal Sendika'sı arasındaki hararet damgasını vurmuştu. Sendikadan önce taslak hazırlamak için dijital platformları kullanan işçiler, kendi yaptıkları anketler ile taleplerini belirlemişti. Sendika kendi taslağını daha düşük ücret, yan hak zamları ile açıklamasına rağmen işçiler kendi hazırladıkları taslağa sahip çıkmıştı. Bunun için fabrikaya bildiriler dağıtıp, stickerlar yapıştırmış, fabrika önlerine pankartlar asmıştı. İşçiler, sendika temsilcilerini sık sık fabrika içinde sıkıştırırken işçiler ile sendika temsilcileri çeşitli tartışmalarda karşı karşıya gelmişti.

Tüm bunlardan sonra yapılan sendika delege seçimleri ise sessiz geçti. Süreci anlatan bir makine işçisi, ''Delege adayı listeleri asmışlar panolara. Seçim yapacağız diye duyurdular. Her şey çok hızlı gelişti. Sendika temsilcilerine kimler yakınsa onlar seçildi açıkçası'' derken Sincan'daki bir döküm işçisi, ''Bizim sendika temsilcimiz işten çıkarılmıştı. Bizim de başımıza bir anda birini diktiler yeni sendika temsilcisi bu diye. Seçim yok bir şey yok. Nasıl olacak bu iş?'' diye ifade etti.

Geçmiş dönemleri hatırlatan bir işçi, ''Bizim şuan ücretlerimiz diğer döküm fabrikalarına göre düşük. Yeni yönetim belki vergiyi yüzde 15 sabitler diye umuyordum ama ses seda yok. Biz önceki sözleşmeye dair ne yaptıysak aynısını yapmamız lazım. O zaman taleplerimizi belirlemiştik. Herkes arka çıkmıştı beraber hareket ediyorduk. Aynısını yapmadığımız sürece önümüzdeki sözleşme bizim açımızdan sıkıntılı geçer. Bizdeki sendika temsilcileri sırf yeni yönetime yaranmak için düşük taslak bile açıklayabilir. Çok değil Ocak'ta duyurmuş olurlar. Ne yapıyorsak öncesinde yapmamız lazım'' diyerek işçilerin …

author: Daron Letts
title: Lawyers debate accused killer’s mental state during murder trial’s closing submissions
content:
Danny Paul Eyaituk’s mental state was the key issue debated by Crown and defence lawyers who made their final submissions Tuesday in the Sanikiluaq man’s first-degree murder trial.


Eyaituk is on trial in an Iqaluit courtroom for the shooting death of his wife Annie Tracy Oqaituq, 36, who was found dead in their Sanikiluaq home on April 19, 2024.


Defence lawyer Alan Regel told Justice Susan Cooper she should consider “manslaughter at worst,” but Crown lawyer Emma Baasch called for a verdict of second-degree murder “at a minimum.”


Regel argued that expert witness forensic psychiatrist

Dr. Maryana Kravtsenyuk

 expressed enough uncertainty about Eyaituk’s mental state around the time of Oqaituq’s death to cast doubt on whether he had enough control of his senses to be guilty of murder.


“The Crown is, I suggest, relying on speculation that ignores the important evidence of the mental illness and the psychiatric condition that he suffered from,” Regel said.


Throughout the trial, Regel has said Eyaituk was not criminally responsible for the death.


The Criminal Code says a person cannot be held responsible for a crime committed while suffering from a mental health disorder that makes them incapable of appreciating the nature of the act.


Eyaituk had testified earlier in the trial that he had used cocaine and cannabis on the day of Oqaituq’s death. He used the substances on a daily basis, according to previous witness testimony.


Eyaituk had suffered multiple bouts of drug-induced psychosis, including on the day of the alleged shooting, Kravtsenyuk said in her report. In his closing submission, Regel emphasized these as contributing factors to the accused’s mental state.


Baasch argued that, based on the expert witness’ report, Eyaituk “could understand the consequences of his actions and he could plan connected with reality and was cognizant of his actions,” at the time of his wife’s death.


“He had organized thought before and after,” she added, quoting from Kravtsenyuk’s report.


As for Eyaituk’s drug use on the day of the offence, Baasch referred to Kravtsenyuk’s report again: “His thinking and mental state were impaired, but not that they were absent.”


Eyaituk appeared in a blue sweatshirt with his hair tied back in a short ponytail. He leaned back in his seat and wiped his face with a tissue as his lawyer spoke. He rested his cheek on his hand and peered down much of the time as Baasch spoke.


The trial began June 9 in Sanikiluaq and continued until June 25 but stopped while

Kravtsenyuk was on the stand

 due to witness, judge, counsel and courtroom availability, defence lawyer Alan Regel said in an email to Nunatsiaq News. The trial resumed in Iqaluit on Monday.


Cooper will present her verdict at 9:30 a.m. on. Jan. 19. Eyaituk will appear at that hearing by video feed, she said.

author: David Venn
title: Iqaluit firefighters respond to housefire near breakwater
content:
Two fire trucks, two ambulances and 12 firefighters responded to a housefire in Lower Iqaluit Tuesday afternoon.


RCMP vehicles blocked Nipisa Street near The Snack restaurant while the emergency response crews were stationed closer to the breakwater.


As of 3:30 p.m., there was no smoke in the area, and the area was cleared.


It wasn’t clear if there was anyone at home when the fire broke out. The two ambulances left without appearing to take any passengers.


In a public service announcement issued at 2:30 p.m., city spokesperson Geoff Byrne asked residents to avoid the 100s area “where possible to ensure the safety of the public and allow emergency crews to carry out their response efforts without obstruction.”


He also said some residents may experience water delivery delays, as the firefighters are using the trucks.

author: Dionne Phillips, Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: From bending time to 16 names for a berry — a poet finds inspiration in her ancestral languages
content:
Poet Kalli Van Stone’s new collection ‘welík’t’ was published in September. Submitted images


While exploring nsyilxcn (syilx language) and Secwepemctsín (Shuswap language) dictionaries, Kalli Van Stone (Spyu7) found herself drawn to words that held concepts she couldn’t find in English or Latin dictionaries.


In nsyilxcn, for example, she came across a word for the bending of time, which inspired her two-line poem “sumix kaʔɬis medicine power iii.”


These teachings opened up new worlds for Van Stone, which she began exploring through poetry.


Her debut poetry collection titled

welík’t

 — meaning “sparkle” in Secwepemctsín — was published

by Nightwood Editions

 in September.


The collection is divided into three sections: “nsyilxcn,” “english poems with indian names,” and “secwepemctsín.” Translations accompany her poems, alongside her own artwork.


Van Stone, who is syilx and Secwépemc from the north end of Okanagan Lake in “B.C.,” began reclaiming her ancestral languages a decade ago. This collection grew out of that work.


Across the collection’s 77 poems, Van Stone writes about personal experiences, the lives of her ancestors and the differences between her languages.


“They’re meant to be kind of shorter, more musical phrases, and then to kind of highlight any cool curiosities I find in the language,” she told IndigiNews.


‘I don’t let it stop me if I don’t have the words’


Van Stone is particularly drawn to words in nsyilxcn and Secwepemctsín that “challenge the Western concepts of time and personhood,” as well as those that speak to spirituality and ceremony.


Finding new words that displayed inspiring concepts brought up feelings of excitement and fulfilment for Van Stone. She references the nsyilxcn word kʷu ksq́ʷiɬq́ʷɬt, which translates to “you do wonders.” 


Dictionaries are only one place she looks for inspiration. Van Stone also draws on things she’s heard throughout her life, returning to them later when she sits down to write. 


“Mostly, it’ll just be like something cool I’ve heard throughout my life, and I’ll kind of tuck it away and then expand on it later in my own time,” she said.


“Or I find something really cool in the dictionary, or just in other documents or videos, and I’ll be like, ‘Whoa, there’s so much in that one sentence,’ and then I’ll kind of make my own thing.”


Writing in languages she’s still learning has, in part, shaped her aesthetic as a poet.


“I thought it was a really cool challenge to make something beautiful using some of the limitations I have. I know enough to do something creative, but it also makes it more simple, very stripped down to core ideas,” she said.


“I don’t let it stop me if I don’t have the words.”


There is also a musical quality to this brevity. In some of her poems, Van Stone experimented with call and response, drawing on musical traditions from her communities.


In the

notes accompanying her poem

 “nt̓aʔlils,” Van Stone draws a parallel between a drumstick striking a drum and a dancer’s feet striking the earth. She relates these movements to syilx teaching about working through different emotions. 


‘Our languages are sisters’


Van Stone has found similarities between nsyilxcn and Secwepemctsín, both members of the Salishan language family. 


“Our languages are sisters, so I love that there are so many ways where they kind of converge into each other, and then I was really interested in where they’re different,” she explained.


“Then we have really similar but still distinct music styles and a lot of our seasonal round is really similar, so that’s why it just felt so nice to learn both and do both and embrace all my ancestral sides.”


Working between nsyilxcn, Secwepemctsín and English brought its own challenges, particularly when translating and finding words that could convey what she wanted to express.


In “sixteen names of síyaʔ,” Van Stone lists 16 nsyilxcn names for the Saskatoon berry, compared with three English and Latin names. She connects that difference to the relationships her people have developed with the plant over thousands of years. She writes:

title: Hitting the mark: “Grand Theft Capital”, by Fred Magdoff and John Bellamy Foster
content:
REVIEWS


The Guardian

: “Trump’s billionaire-blue collar coalition has been smashed by class politics” by

Aditya Chakrabortty


“…Over decades – through Reagan and Clinton, Bush and Obama – Republicans and Democrats have changed the tax code to reward ownership rather than earning, so the richest 400 households

now pay lower rates of tax

 than the bottom 50% of Americans. As the radical economists Fred Magdoff and John Bellamy Foster show in their new book,

 Grand Theft Capital: What Workers Should Know About the Affordability Crisis

, the share of national income going to ordinary workers has slumped from 30% in the 1960s to 20% today. This is the destruction of working-class lives and dreams in which Republicans and Democrats colluded. This is the American carnage that in 2016 helped propel Trump into the White House. But the most glaring feature of this era of Trumponomics has been its shameless inequality….”

Read more

….

And you can see the A

dam Smith Institute’s miffed response

 to his piece, here…if you are interested in how weak it is.


Red Pepper

 picks: “

Botany, welfare, friendships, work and housing.

David Matthews

 picks six of the best new books for leftists

“


“Capitalism has been stagnating for decades, characterized by sluggish growth. Yet the wealthy continue to grow richer while the rest of us face declining wages and eroding living standards. Focusing on the United States yet deeply relevant to Britain and other capitalist countries, Magdoff and Bellamy Foster make clear that in a climate of economic decline, big business has deliberately and strategically targeted workers as a primary source of wealth extraction. Their conclusion is a call for mass action, from below…”


People’s Voice

(Canada):

“Succinct and accessible, this economic primer hits the mark for working people today”

, by Stéphane Doucet


“Magdoff and Foster have truly hit the mark with this short book…Interesting figures include the precipitous drop of work stoppages involving over 1000 workers, from over 330 per year in 1975 to less than 20 since the 2010’s; the corporate tax rate being more than halved since 1950; the CEO-to-worker pay ratio being multiplied by more than 10 times in 60 years; labour’s share of GDP dropping more than 10 percent since the 1960’s; and private sector workers with defined-benefit pensions dropping for 60 percent to 10 percent of the workforce. All these are very broad, clear, decisive and very powerful figures. The book provides many more, along with the necessary context…”

Read more

Counterpunch

: “

Why Working People Got the Blues

“, by Ron Jacobs


“The lack of affordability is the curse of the working class, whether its individual members are working or not. Politicians talk about it and some might even propose legislation to moderate it, but the cost of almost everything keeps going up more than wages and retirement benefits. The domination of the economy by monopolies and cartels–many of which are invested in the business of war and resource extraction–and by politicians at their service means the bills they rack up are going to be paid by us. When the ruling class tells us they can’t afford to continue providing social services, they’re lying. author: APTN National News
title: APTN and Sportsnet to feature 6 NHL games in Plains Cree, Inuktitut
content:
APTN and Rogers Sportsnet announced that six NHL games will be broadcast in Plains Cree and Inuktitut this season.


The games will air on APTN’s regular network along with its APTN Languages channel.


All the games are on Saturday evening, with the first on Nov. 28 that will feature a game between Gavin McKenna and the Toronto Maple Leafs and Pittsburgh Penguins.


The statement said the first three broadcasts will be presented in Plains Cree, followed by three in Inuktitut. All games will air live and run until April 10.


“This hockey season, APTN delivers a hat trick: exciting game action, opportunities to reclaim Indigenous languages and stronger connections to our communities through the power of sport. Hearing a game called in your language helps keep it part of everyday life, while welcoming fans of every background to share in the experience,” said Mike Omelus, APTN executive director of Content and Programming Strategy, in a

statement on Tuesday. 


“Thanks to our partnership with Rogers and Sportsnet, we’re proud to continue creating space for Indigenous languages to thrive on one of the country’s biggest stages.”


The announcement comes after Sportsnet cancelled Hockey Night in Punjabi after being on the air for 18 seasons.


“Together with APTN, we’re proud to bring NHL games to fans in Plains Cree and Inuktitut and celebrate Indigenous languages that are such an important part of Canada,” said Greg Sansone, president of Sportsnet.


2026-2027 schedule:


Saturday Night Hockey in Plains Cree


Saturday, November 28, 2026: Toronto Maple Leafs at Pittsburgh Penguins, 7 p.m. ET.


Saturday, December 12, 2026: Edmonton Oilers at Ottawa Senators, 7 p.m. ET.


Saturday, January 9, 2027: Utah Mammoth at Winnipeg Jets, 7 p.m. ET.


Saturday Night Hockey in Inuktitut

Saturday, March 13, 2027: Calgary Flames at Boston Bruins, 7 p.m. ET.

title: From Israel to Iran, Schumer’s Positions Contradict Those of Many Dem Voters
content:
Electing Schumer to lead now would be like having a Democratic leader supporting the Vietnam War in the early 1970s.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

For the first time since his ascension to the Democratic Senate leadership a decade ago, Chuck Schumer is facing a serious challenge for the top post by Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland). Once considered a rather cautious center-left figure, Van Hollen has emerged in recent years as one the Democrats’ more progressive voices, proving himself willing to challenge the party’s hawkish foreign policy orthodoxy, even regarding U.S. relations with Israel.

Schumer’s decidedly hawkish views are so far to the right of those of rank-and-file Democrats that his reappointment to majority leader would constitute a major betrayal of the Democratic voters who have made it possible for him to once again hold that powerful position after four years in the minority. Most observers believe that while Van Hollen has been gaining momentum, Schumer will likely receive his colleagues’ endorsement when they vote by secret ballot on December 1.

As even leading Republicans admit, the war on Iran was a major reason for the margin of Democratic victory. Schumer, however, has consistently been an Iran hawk. An NBC News exit poll showed that 74 percent of voters noted the war was a “crucial” or “major” factor in their vote. When President Donald Trump launched the war at the end of February, rather than categorically condemning the illegal and predictably disastrous use of force, Schumer issued a rather ambivalent statement asking the administration to be clearer about “the objectives of these strikes and what comes next,” calling for Trump to follow constitutional procedures but stressing “Iran must never be allowed to attain a nuclear weapon.”

This past June, when a U.S.-Iranian memorandum of understanding gave some hope for de-escalation and an end to the conflict, Schumer attempted to mobilize opposition to the peace effort by referring to the agreement as “the art of surrender” and falsely claimed that it would require the United States to pay Iran $300 billion.

As the war has dragged on and public opposition has grown, his criticisms of the war have increased, but this has come after decades of publicly belittling diplomacy and encouraging a more militaristic outlook toward Iran.

As Barack Obama was negotiating with Iran on the nuclear question during his presidential administration, Schumer repeatedly tried to undermine Obama’s diplomatic approach, signing a 2013 letter from a handful of senators, including then-Senators Lindsey Graham and John McCain, insisting that “a credible military threat remains on the table and we underscore the imperative that the current sanctions be maintained aggressively.” He also supported a Republican-backed resolution introduced by the notorious warmonger Graham, insisting that, in the event of war between Israel and Iran, the United States should provide “diplomatic, military, and economic support to the Government of Israel” — even if Israel attacked Iran first.

When such efforts to sabotage the talks failed and a nuclear deal was signed in 2015, Schumer was one of only two Democratic senators to oppose it.

During Israel’s unprovoked bombing of Iran in June of last year, Schumer insisted that “Israel has a right to defend itself” and reiterated that “[t]he United States’ commitment to Israel’s security and defense must be ironclad.” Just over a week earlier, he criticized Trump for even engaging in negotiations with Iran. Schumer refused to sign on to a war powers resolution proposed by Sen. Tim Kaine which could have prevented the United States from joining the war, as it did the following week. Just prior to the 12-day war Israel launched on Iran, during which the U.S. bombed Iranian nuclear sites, Schumer goaded Trump by posting a video to social media accusing him of “folding on Iran” by attempting to negotiate a deal, bemoaning how “Trump always chickens out” regarding the use of military force.

author: Julia Conley
title: Gaza Health Officials Say Meningitis Outbreak Is Due to Infrastructure Attacks
content:
Israel has attacked health and water infrastructure while blocking aid that could help with treatment.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

On the heels of a major international report that accused Israel of committing “environmental war crimes” in Gaza, including by exposing Palestinians to toxins and endangering the drinking water supply with its continued US-backed bombardment, the exclave’s health ministry on Tuesday issued an “epidemiological alert” warning health workers and communities of a “shocking” rise in meningitis infections.

The Gaza Health Ministry called on the World Health Organization and the United Nations Children’s Fund to send lab supplies and antibiotics, and establish isolation wards as Dr. Nidal Ghunaim, deputy director general of primary healthcare for the agency, said 272 meningitis cases had been reported in October — eight times the usual monthly average.

Bacterial meningitis cases rose from about 10-20 per month to 108 last month, and another 100 have been recorded in November. Fifteen people have died of the illness this year, including five between August-October.

The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported that 77% of cases were in babies under one year of age.

Lab tests suggested the cases were linked to enteroviruses, which can spread through the water supply.

The health ministry said the outbreak was the “inevitable result of the destruction of infrastructure, overcrowding of shelters, mixing of drinking water with sewage, and the disaster being exacerbated by flooding due to rain.”

A report released by Oxfam International Monday warned that, among other harms, the destruction of wastewater treatment plants in Gaza made it more likely that Palestinians could come into contact with water contaminated with pathogens.

The ministry warned that children are particularly at risk for meningitis infections, which cause inflammation of the membranes around the spinal cord and brain.

Officials said that in addition to making the outbreak more likely by destroying infrastructure across Gaza and pushing Palestinians into crowded makeshift shelters, Israel has also made it impossible for healthcare workers to stop the outbreak from spreading, by blocking “maintenance spare parts, sterilization materials, and fuel” from reaching Gaza.

Winter rains earlier this month caused catastrophic flooding that destroyed tens of thousands of tents — the only shelter for more than 1 million people after the vast majority of structures have been decimated by Israel’s bombardment over the past three years. Makeshift encampments have been inundated with rainwater mixed with sewage.

“We hold the [Israeli] occupation fully and directly responsible for the epidemic outbreak,” the ministry said.

Bahaa al-Sous, the father of newborn twin girls, told The New Arab Tuesday that he had discovered his daughter Ilat was sick 10 days ago after the storm.

“I came back from work to our tent, and God inspired me to bend down and kiss my daughter’s forehead. I was shocked by the burning heat coming from her small body,” he said.

His daughter finished treatment at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital, but al-Sous was taking her sister, Elin, to the hospital Tuesday after she became ill.

A woman named Iman also brought her six-year-old daughter to the hospital for treatment, but had to buy some medications from private pharmacies.

“The water we drink is not clean like it was before the war. Nothing has stayed the same; even the air we breathe has changed and been polluted by [Israel’s] bombing and destruction,” Iman told The New Arab.

OCHA’s report on conditions in the territory on November 18 said that 45% of households surveyed by the agency were living less than 10 meters from sewage and sludge following the flooding.

“The severe overcrowding in displacement camps and the absence of a healthy, preventive environment greatly increase the likelihood of transmission,” Dr. Iyad Abu Mu’ailaq, a pediatrician at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital, told The New Arab. “The complications of meningitis are very serious. If the child does not receive the right treatment at the right time, it may leave permanent effects on their growth and future, such as loss of hearing or sight.”

author: Thorin Klosowski
title: Signal Moves to Block AI Agents
content:
Signal announced an update to its mobile apps on iOS and Android that seeks to curb issues with AI agents accessing private chats. This is a useful new barrier against a problem we’ve been highlighting this year in our Encrypt It Already campaign. And good news, it’s enabled by default so you don’t need to do anything except update the app.

Over the last year, both Google and Apple* have released AI features in their operating systems that can read the contents of apps. One of the ways it can do this is through screen analysis. Google calls this feature “Intelligent Screen Context,” while Apple refers to it as either “Onscreen Awareness” or “Visual Intelligence.”

Apple now provides a way to block Siri AI’s access to apps, but by default every app is available to Siri AI, so it’s up to the user to go in and put these guardrails up. Signal requests that protection on your behalf. Google doesn’t currently offer any sort of similar option. So Signal on Android does the best it can, by turning off screenshots when it detects an AI assistant attempting to access the screen. Signal’s solution helps ensure that, unless you go in and change the setting yourself, it defaults to the most private option.

While this is a clever solution to the current issues facing Signal (and potentially useful for any other app that does its best to promise privacy), we need all operating systems to provide stronger methods and clear documentation to developers so they can safeguard their users without needing to jump through hoops. Both developers and users should have the tools they need to safeguard their own data from AI agents and other AI tools.

*Apple is an EFF donor. EFF donors do not influence our agenda or our positions.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Mamdani: Rumored Huang Divorce Deal Could Fund Year of Universal Child Care
content:
Research has found that universal child care plans would cost roughly $35 billion per year.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani threw the Jensen Huang scandal into sharp perspective after Huang’s reinstatement as CEO of Nvidia on Monday, pointing out that just half of the disgraced CEO’s estimated wealth could fund an entire year of universal child care for children across the U.S.

Huang’s reinstatement comes just days after he resigned from the company due to reports of his extramarital affairs, including with a woman alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence.

When asked about Huang’s rehiring by the Nvidia board — a decision attributed by the White House and Nvidia to an intervention by Donald Trump — Mamdani criticized the outsized influence of the Huang scandal and the AI industry in general on the U.S. economy.

“I do not think that working people across the country signed up for their pensions being tied to the question of Jensen Huang’s fidelity to his marriage. And yet, for many days, that had a massive impact,” Mamdani said.

“We’re speaking about a divorce settlement that has been rumored to be around $81 billion,” he went on. “That would be the cost of providing universal child care for every 3- and 4-year-old in the United States of America for an entire year.”

Indeed, if Huang and his wife were to get divorced, it could be one of the largest divorce settlements in history. As Forbes points out, documents have shown that most of Huang’s over 3.5 percent stake in Nvidia is held in trusts in which he and his wife are listed as co-trustees. They also live in California, which has laws specifying that assets acquired during their 40-year marriage must be divided evenly in the case of a divorce.

Huang’s net worth has fluctuated significantly in the past few weeks amid the scandal, as the Nvidia stock has fallen and risen. Before the scandal and his resignation earlier this month, Huang’s net worth was roughly $180 billion, according to Forbes, and as of Tuesday, it was down to $134 billion.

Trump said on Monday that Huang and his “very, very, very good wife” have “worked it out,” suggesting that they may not divorce, though it’s unclear what Trump was basing this assertion on. At the same time, Huang reportedly admitted to the board before his reinstatement that he had had even more affairs than the ones already revealed to the public.

“A lot of this just brings to mind what [Supreme Court] Justice [Louis] Brandeis said quite some time ago, which is: ‘We can have democracy. We can have great wealth concentrated in the hands of a few. We cannot have both,’” said Mamdani.

Such wealth could, indeed, fund a significant proportion of proposed universal child care plans. University of Pennsylvania research found in 2022 that universal pre-K for 3- and 4-year-olds would cost $351 billion over the next 10 years, including $41 billion in initial costs to build the necessary facilities. This would average out to roughly $35 billion per year.

During his presidential campaign in 2020, Sen. Bernie Sanders’s (I-Vermont) campaign introduced a plan for free universal child care covering children from 0 to 4, which his campaign said would cost $1.5 trillion over the next decade, or roughly $150 billion a year.

Mamdani and New York Gov. Kathy Hochul have taken steps toward implementing universal child care for children 3 and under in the state. A program to fund free child care for children under 2 for two years and expand free child care for 3-year-olds in the state unveiled in January has a price tag of $1.7 billion.

Meanwhile, Mamdani also raised the concern that the U.S. economy, and millions of Americans’ retirement plans, are so closely tied to the success of a handful of major tech companies.

“When you look at our stock market, and you look at how disproportionately dependent it is on artificial intelligence-related stocks, it cannot help but give you a sense of concern about just how much this technology is now dominant — not just in terms of the discourse that we are having around it on a day-to-day basis, but also the strength of the United States economy,” Mamdani said.

author: Jonathan Shorman
title: Trump’s DOJ Is Already Working to Undermine Congressional Oversight
content:
The Justice Department is sending threatening letters to lawmakers likely to investigate the Trump administration.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

As the Trump administration prepares for Democrats to launch an onslaught of investigations in the next Congress, the U.S. Department of Justice is turning to a three-word phrase to preemptively fight back: “Legitimate legislative purpose.”

The Justice Department has sent letters in recent days to leading Democratic lawmakers raising the possibility they’ll face criminal prosecution for conducting aggressive oversight of President Donald Trump and his aides. Legal experts have widely dismissed the threats as empty because the U.S. Constitution affords lawmakers wide protections from prosecution for official actions taken in Congress.

But the letters — and that short phrase within them — offer a blueprint for how the White House will try to undermine the investigations themselves, in addition to discrediting the investigators. Democrats will take control of Congress with majorities in both the House and Senate in early January.

The Justice Department is signaling it will attack congressional subpoenas seeking documents and testimony from federal officials as driven by retribution and outside the bounds of traditional oversight. The government appears ready to argue such requests cross a line into illegality.

The DOJ letters allege Democrats intend to violate federal laws that prohibit individuals acting in an official capacity from violating the constitutional rights of others. In this case, those supposedly having their rights violated would be Trump’s associates.

“As you should know, whatever investigations you and your fellow Democrats have planned must have a legitimate legislative purpose,” U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz, the top Justice Department official in the Southern District of Texas, wrote on Nov. 19 to Rep. Jamie Raskin, a Maryland Democrat.

Reitz, a former Republican candidate for Texas attorney general, included similar language in letters to Rep. Robert Garcia and Sen. Adam Schiff of California, Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan and Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts. All are Democrats likely to play prominent roles in investigating the Trump administration after the party takes control of Congress in January.

Additionally, Will Scharf, the White House counsel, in a Nov. 9 letter to Garcia wrote that “abusive and capricious threats” were spreading among Democratic legislators. He warned that the Trump administration “will not be extorted” and expected lawmakers to investigate within settled constitutional limits.

The defiant posture comes as Trump braces for a final two years in office marked by aggressive oversight from House and Senate committees, as Democrats probe alleged corruption and mismanagement.

Many Democrats credit the blue tsunami that gave the party large majorities in both chambers to voters’ frustration with self-enrichment by Trump and other government officials.

In addition to the Justice Department letters, Trump on Nov. 20 signed an executive order that requires federal contractors to notify the White House of any congressional requests for information. Contractors are also required to abide by any White House instructions to withhold communications that the Trump administration says are covered by executive privilege.

Democrats are now on a collision course with the Trump administration that could end up in the courts.

Raskin pressed forward with his oversight efforts despite Reitz’s letters. The ranking Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, Raskin sent letters on Nov. 20 to the DOJ, FBI, Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the U.S. Bureau of Prisons — demanding that they preserve all records, including Signal chats, which can be set to auto-delete.

Slotkin responded to Reitz in a letter last week, calling congressional oversight an important constitutional responsibility. She called the DOJ official’s threats frivolous and a violation of his ethical duties as an attorney. The nonpartisan watchdog group Campaign for Accountability has filed a complaint against Reitz with the State Bar of Texas.

author: Unknown
title: C'est quoi l'époque contemporaine ?
content:
Pistes pour la terminer


17 octobre : fin de l'époque contemporaine. « Mais vous voulez la remplacer par quoi au juste ? » demanderont les micros et les éternels repoussoirs à révolution. On va plutôt prendre le temps de parler d'avec quoi on veut en finir.


L'époque contemporaine s'est ouverte sur une série de révolutions face à laquelle les gouvernements ont du trouver des nouvelles techniques de contre-insurrection. La récupération s'est ajoutée à la répression. Le pouvoir s'est réformé et renforcé par sa propre critique. Sortir de l'époque contemporaine c'est faire une révolution qui ne renforce pas ce qu'elle combat.


À L'époque contemporaine, même les mots de la contestation sont des outils du pouvoir. Démocratie, Peuple, émancipation, nation, classe, intérêt, légitimité, pouvoir, etc : les concepts à disposition empêchent une véritable rupture avec le paradigme dominant. Il est temps que les insurgés s'arment de leur propre langage.


L'époque contemporaine a pris nos armes et les a données aux assemblées et aux constitutions. Depuis près de 200 ans, tout a été fait pour isoler nos « voix » dans les isoloirs. Nous ne céderons plus jamais notre puissance.


L'époque contemporaine a décidé à notre place ce que nous sommes. En nous imposant des identités nationales, de genre, de classe, on nous a empêché d'exister depuis un autre « Nous ». On nous a imposé la « Société » et la soumission qui va avec. Elle a ordonné la destruction de tout ce qui résiste. Nous assumons notre refus de collaborer avec la société.


L'époque contemporaine est une période où, sous couvert de progrès, tous ont cru au mythe d'une production qui améliorerait les conditions de vie. Il faut enterrer le marxisme parce qu'il ne permet pas de comprendre que nous ne pouvons rien faire des moyens de production. Nous sommes entrés dans l'ère des insurrections du déclin. Plus personne ne croit que la croissance (même écologique, sociale ou raisonnable) ramènera un niveau de vie « convenable ». Contre le paradigme de la production, qui n'est qu'enfermement et mise au travail, il nous faut une nouvelle culture technique, de débrouillardise et de mise en commun.


L'époque contemporaine n'était pas une étape civilisée de plus. Elle a unifié toutes les logiques de production et d'institution qu'elle a eues sous la main. Patriarcat, féodalisme, esclavage, colonialisme, racisme et salariat ont tous servi au fonctionnement globalisé de l'économie. Sortir de l'époque contemporaine, ce n'est pas ouvrir une nouvelle époque de la civilisation mais faire une révolution qui détruit la civilisation.


La Révolution est un saut dans les ténèbres

content:
Pour le lancement de l'épicerie populaire, on vous invite à passer la soirée à l'Ostau et à venir chercher votre premier panier de pain, fruits et légumes à prix libre !


Musicien.nes et chanteureuses la scène vous sera ouverte pour jammer ;)


Nous sommes fier.es de vous inviter à la soirée de lancement de l'Épicerie Populaire ! 🎉🥖🥦🍊🎉

 🗓️ Ce jeudi 5 novembre de 18h à 22h

 📍 À L'Ostau dau País Marselhés, 18 rue de l'Olivier, 13005


Ce sera l'occasion de passer un moment convivial avec nous et de venir chercher votre premier panier de pain, fruits et légumes à prix libre !


Une épicerie populaire à Marseille ?


Ça sert à quoi ?


 Donner accès à une alimentation de qualité, quel que soit tes moyens.

 Proposer un moment convivial plein de douceurs. Viens prendre le petit dej, on a du bon café, du thé et des petites viennoiseries !


Comment on fonctionne ?


 Tout le monde est bienvenu, sans condition, sans inscription.

 Fruits et légumes produits en agriculture biologique ou raisonnée qu'on achète au prix fixé par les producteurices du coin.

 Pains et viennoiseries : invendus de la veille de boulangeries marseillaises.

 On vend à prix libre, à partir de la gratuité, pour que celleux qui ont plus puissent contribuer pour celleux qui ont moins.

 On fonctionne sans subventions. Si tu peux mettre un peu de moula ça nous permet de maintenir un équilibre économique.

title: Projection sur le mouvement des Gilets jaunes
content:
A l'occasion du mouvement social en cours, la Bobine Engagée propose une projection du documentaire « Les Magnifiques Sauvages » de Cerveaux Non Disponibles, en présence de camarades street médics.


PROJECTION SUR LE MOUVEMENT DES GILETS JAUNES


Mercredi 11 novembre (férié) 18h30 à la Base (3 rue Pierre roche)


A l'occasion du mouvement social en cours, le collectif La Bobine Engagée propose une projection du documentaire « Les Magnifiques Sauvages » de Cerveaux Non Disponibles.


Après la projection, on aura le plaisir d'accueillir les Street Medic Marseille avec un temps d'échange pour discuter de leurs expériences vécues sur le terrain.


Un goûter de soutien vous sera proposé, et les fonds récoltés seront versés aux médics. (Cash only)


Synopsis :


Que retiendra-t-on des Gilets Jaunes dans quelques décennies ? Si l'on laisse le pouvoir politico médiatique décider, les gilets jaunes resteront dans l'histoire comme un mouvement de sauvages ayant tout détruit pour pouvoir rouler moins cher.


Un épiphénomène, certes spectaculaire, mais qui ne laissera aucune trace dans la société.


Sauf que nous savons que la réalité est tout autre.


Et puisqu'il est encore temps de le rappeler, ce film donne la parole à quelques-uns des dizaines de milliers de magnifiques sauvages qui ont vécu, de l'intérieur ou comme observateurs, cette bataille pour un monde meilleur, plus humain, plus juste, réellement démocratique.


L'occasion de se souvenir à quel point l'amour et l'amitié ont été le principal moteur de ce feu de joie.


Hâte de vous y voir !


La Bobine Engagée

author: Chris Walker
title: Wisconsin’s Former GOP Maps Would Have Blocked Democratic “Blue Wave” — Analysis
content:
Had a previously gerrymandered map been allowed to remain, Wisconsin voters’ preferences would have been ignored.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

A new analysis of election data suggests that, had a Republican gerrymandered map in Wisconsin remained in place for this year’s midterm races, it would have blocked the state’s “blue wave” of Democratic victories — enabling the GOP to maintain control of the legislature despite most voters’ preferences.

The midterm elections in Wisconsin, like in many other states, resulted in a Democratic “trifecta,” with Democrat David Crowley winning the governor’s race and the party wresting control of both the Assembly and Senate. It’s the first time that Democrats have had a trifecta in that state since 2008.

The result of the statewide legislative races means that Democrats will have a 53-46 seat majority in the Assembly in January. That result mirrors Crowley’s statewide performance, as he defeated U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany (R) by 54 percent to 46 percent.

Those results wouldn’t have happened, however, were it not for a series of events that dismantled maps drawn by legislative Republicans over the past 15 years, which gave them a significant advantage over Democrats by making most districts noncompetitive.

Liberal victories in statewide Supreme Court races led to that court reexamining the maps drawn by Republicans. In 2023, the court ruled they were illegal gerrymanders, and ordered new maps to be submitted by interested parties, including by Gov. Tony Evers’s (D) office and the Republican-held legislature. But before those proposals could be examined by the court, Evers and the Republicans agreed on compromise maps for the Senate and Assembly, passing them into law in 2024.

Had the court ruled differently in 2023, and had those new maps never come to pass, “the will of the majority of Wisconsin voters would still not be reflected in their Legislature” in this year’s midterm elections, a joint analysis from the Election Law Clinic at Harvard Law School and Wisconsin-based Law Forward found.

That analysis, published on Monday, examined election data from this year’s midterms, but placed voters’ partisan preferences into models using the old maps’ borders. “Even if Democrats had performed at 2026 levels, the Republican Party would have held a 61-38 majority of 23 seats in the Assembly,” likely resulting in Republicans maintaining control of the state legislature, the analysis concluded.

The analysis suggested that researchers’ findings provided ample argument for reforming the redistricting process.

“Wisconsin’s experience from 2011-2026 demonstrates the need for fundamental and sweeping reform in Wisconsin, as well as nationally, to ban the partisan gerrymandering of state legislative districts to prevent such efforts in the future,” the analysis said.

Doug Poland, an attorney for Law Forward, reiterated the analysis’s points in an interview with Wisconsin Public Radio.

“Yes, there was a wave election [for Democrats], and it was big. But guess what? As big as it was, if we had had those heavily gerrymandered districts, it wouldn’t have been enough to overcome the gerrymander,” Poland said. “And that’s the lesson to draw from this.”

Amid mid-census redistricting that Republicans initiated last year in hopes of diminishing likely losses in this year’s midterms, a group of Democrats submitted legislation to reform the process.

Among other provisions, the Redistricting Reform Act of 2025 would have required states to establish commissions that represent, in equal fashion, the top two political parties that won previous state legislative races. The bill also called for a ban on any state redistricting commission drawing maps between U.S. Census cycles, unless a court found that their previous maps were crafted unlawfully.

Voters likely would have supported that bill’s aims, and could back a similar bill if Democrats introduce one next year. An Economist/YouGov poll in April asked respondents their views on partisan gerrymandering, questioning whether political parties in charge of state legislatures should be allowed to intentionally draw maps favoring themselves. According to the poll, only 7 percent of Americans said that should be permitted, while 71 percent said parties shouldn’t be allowed to have that map-drawing advantage.

title: Roma: Fisica occupata a seguito della morte di Alessandro. Università di Fisica occupata a Torino: le rivendicazioni.
content:
In queste ore a Roma una grande mobilitazione universitaria sta occupando diversi spazi in risposta alla morte di Alessandro, studente di Fisica alla Sapienza, che da mesi dormiva in tenda per protestare contro l’inaccessibilità degli affitti in assenza di un posto in uno studentato.


Centinaia di studenti e studentesse universitarie dopo aver sanzionato il rettorato questa mattina, sono partiti in corteo e hanno occupato LazioDisco, l’ente per il diritto allo studio della Regione Lazio e, infine, hanno occupato la facoltà di Fisica alla Sapienza da dove partirà un corteo alle ore 18 di martedì 24 novembre.


Pubblichiamo il comunicato dell’Assemblea di Fisica, il dipartimento è stato occupato a Torino sulla scia delle occupazioni universitarie di questo periodo all’interno della mobilitazione generale contro riarmo e carovita.


L’Assemblea di Fisica in data odierna 23/11/2026, dichiara iniziata l’occupazione all’interno del Dipartimento di Fisica. Nelle ultime settimane numerose persone che vivono il nostro dipartimento si sono attivate per confrontarsi su condizioni critiche ed emergenziali che toccano tutta la nostra società, interessando anche i centri della ricerca, del sapere, dell’educazione e non meno il nostro dipartimento.


In un contesto globale di guerre, conflitti economici, crisi climatica e politiche di tagli allo stato sociale il nostro governo continua a portare avanti agende politiche cieche e a difesa degli interessi di gruppi elitari. Queste scelte si ripercuotono pesantemente nel nostro contesto con costanti tagli all’educazione, alla ricerca e a istituzioni come Edisu responsabili del diritto allo studio.

Ne risentono fortemente l* student* fuorisede che devono fare fronte a una mancanza di alloggi pubblici e affitti sempre più cari, mentre continua ad essere agevolata la costruzione di studentati privati dai prezzi proibitivi, sulla riga dei finanziamenti del PNRR. Il costante definanziamento dell’università, come il taglio al Fondo di Finanziamento Ordinario per il 2026 a fronte di un aumento degli investimenti alla Difesa, per di più fa sì che si strutturalizzi la precarietà come norma per l’inquadramento delle figure che portano avanti la ricerca pubblica. Nelle università italiane, il 39% del personale accademico si trova in situzioni di lavoro precario, sottopagato e sfruttato.


Inoltre, questo spinge l’università pubblica a ricercare finanziamenti da enti privati che permettono e promuovono l’intromissione di realtà coinvolte anche nel settore bellico. Ne è esemplare il recente accordo quadro con Confindustria, assieme alle altre collaborazioni con aziende come Leonardo o Thales Alenia Space tramite master, eventi di orientamento e borse di studio. Il recente accordo quadro con Telt, società impegnata in prima linea nella devastazione in atto in Val di Susa per il progetto TAV Torino-Lione, esemplifica ulteriormente la collusione dell’università con aziende dal dubbio impegno etico in un progetto centrale al piano europeo di riarmo.


All’interno del nostro dipartimento questa situazione si realizza: nel quotidiano in una mancanza cronica di aule per svolgere lezioni e di spazi di studio e di socialità a servizio dell* student*, nella presenza di accordi con aziende coinvolte con l’industria del “dual-use” e nella situazione di precarietà lavorativa a cui le persone che intraprendono la strada della ricerca sono sottoposte, minacciata ultimamente anche dall’utilizzo dell’IA.


L’Assemblea di Fisica, dunque, si pone:

-Contro la guerra, il riarmo e l’utilizzo del nostro sapere in contesti bellici.

-Contro la costante precarietà nel mondo della ricerca, che lascia l* student* a dover scegliere tra instabilità economica o lavorare nel settore privato sempre più coinvolto nella filiera delle industrie delle tecnologie dual use.

-Contro la devastazione ambientale in tutte le sue forme, in particolare come quella dovuta al progetto della TAV in Val di Susa e come quella prevista per i progetti di costruzione dei data center nelle periferie della nostra città, mentre il nostro ateneo sostiene di impegnarsi a “Incrementare la responsabilità sociale […] e ambientale”.

-Contro una politica universitaria fatta di tagli, definanziamenti e mancanza sistematica di spazi.

-Contro le politiche statali di austerità alla base dei definanziamaneti alla scuola, all’università, alla ricerca e alla sanità.

title: Gelawêj Ewrîn: Jin Jiyan Azadî is a philosophy beyond borders - Part One
content:
Gelawêj Ewrîn, spokesperson for the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), spoke to ANF about state repression against women in Iran and Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilat), the struggle for women's freedom, the philosophy of Jin Jiyan Azadî (Woman, Life, Freedom) and the impact of war on women. Ewrîn also highlighted the significance of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on 25 November, saying that women's struggle for freedom in Iran goes beyond regime change and that women must directly determine their own future.


Gelawêj Ewrîn said that wartime conditions in Iran have further intensified state repression and violence against women in society, leaving women confronted with both the state's repressive policies and the devastation caused by war. Ewrîn stressed that the atmosphere of war must not be allowed to push women's demands for freedom into the background. She said that Kurdish women's struggle is not limited to national and cultural rights but represents the pursuit of a democratic life for all peoples and women in Iran. Gelawêj Ewrîn emphasised the importance of women's struggle for freedom, equality and the right to determine their own future in Eastern Kurdistan.


PJAK spokesperson Gelawêj Ewrîn shared the following assessments:


How do you assess the current extent of state repression against women in Iran?


Repression against women in Iran cannot be explained solely through the anti-women policies of the current government. Behind this repression lie the patriarchal mentality, power relations and the systematic deprivation of society's will that have been shaped over thousands of years within state-centred civilisation. The Islamic Republic has reproduced this historical mentality within its own ideological and political structure, turning women's bodies and identities into areas of its domination. The state believes it has the right to decide how women should dress, how they should live, whom they should have relationships with, which areas of life they should participate in and how they should present their identities in society. In essence, this is an attempt to eliminate women's will. The compulsory hijab policy is one of the most visible instruments of this system. The state seeks to subjugate society as a whole through control over women's bodies. A system that seeks to break women's will also seeks to break society's free will.


However, the Jin Jiyan Azadî Revolution that developed following the killing of Jina Amini shook this mentality and dealt it a historic blow. Women did not take to the streets merely to oppose compulsory hijab. They asserted their determination to have a say over their own lives, identities and futures. They made the struggle and demand for freedom, which had been accumulating in Iranian society for a long time and had developed enormous potential, much more visible. Today, the presence of women without headscarves in public spaces across many Iranian cities demonstrates that the social control imposed by the state for years has been significantly weakened. However, this cannot be interpreted as the end of state repression. Alongside direct interventions in the streets, the state seeks to maintain its control through pressure on workplaces and businesses, legal proceedings and financial penalties.


The important point here is that the state is not concerned because it can no longer control women's hair, clothing or lives, but because it fears women's struggle. It fears the possibility that women will establish a new social life through their own will and take the lead in society. This is the most significant change brought about by Jin Jiyan Azadî. Women no longer accept others making decisions on their behalf. They are asserting that they are the owners of their own lives and must govern them themselves. For this reason, the Jin Jiyan Azadî Revolution is not merely the name of a protest movement. It is a philosophy and method of struggle aimed at rebuilding society on the foundation of women's freedom. In other words, change is taking place in emotions, attitudes and ways of thinking.


What forms of repression do Kurdish women face because of both their gender and Kurdish identity? How are they resisting this repression?

title: Zeynep Oduncu: Women must have a say in building peace
content:
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) MP for Batman (Êlih) Zeynep Oduncu spoke to ANF about 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, and the role of women in building peace within the framework of the Peace and Democratic Society Process initiated by Abdullah Öcalan.


Zeynep Oduncu said that the women's freedom struggle developed alongside the Kurdish Freedom Movement and that building a democratic society and peace is essential to creating spaces where women can live freely. She stated that women are engaged in a twofold struggle for existence, both because of their Kurdish identity and because they are women.


 


'

Building a democratic society is extremely valuable for women'


Zeynep Oduncu said that building peace is something they have dreamed of for many years and want to see become a reality. She explained that the women's freedom struggle began alongside the Kurdish Freedom Movement: "The realization of peace is something we have dreamed of for a long time and want to see become a reality. The women's freedom struggle began with the emergence of the Kurdish Freedom Movement. We are at an important stage in enabling women to establish their presence in society, make their voices heard, rise up and stand against violence, denial and marginalization. The Kurdish Freedom Movement has created a foundation through which women can participate in every sphere of life, establish their own existence and assert themselves as individuals.


Building democracy and peace is the clearest indication that spaces can be created where women can have a say in their own lives and discover themselves. Today, building a democratic society in Turkey and the Middle East means creating spaces where women can participate alongside men in every sphere of life, express themselves and make their voices heard."


Zeynep Oduncu said that women face a twofold struggle because of both their Kurdish identity and their gender. She pointed out that women's struggle to establish their place in society is also a struggle for freedom.


Zeynep Oduncu stated that women around the world face massacres, oppression, enforced disappearances, harassment and rape. She said that building a democratic society is crucial to enabling women to live free from violence.


'Women's bodies are the first to be exploited in wars'


Zeynep Oduncu said that the patriarchal mentality turns wars into environments where violence against women and their exploitation intensify: "Today, as women, we find ourselves at the very center of war. The reality of war creates an environment in which the patriarchal mentality is prepared to subject women to harassment, rape and massacres in every sphere. Throughout history, whenever there has been war, women's bodies have been the first to be exploited. Unfortunately, in wars, the patriarchal mentality considers itself entitled to exploit women. Women are threatened and treated as spoils of war.


During the wars in Shengal and Kobanê in 2015 and 2016, women were sold in slave markets. Even in the 21st century, at a time when we believe we have made so much progress, women are unfortunately still treated as spoils of war. Women from Shengal were sold in slave markets. There was a mentality that targeted women first during war, seeking to massacre and destroy them."


Zeynep Oduncu pointed to the mentality behind ISIS attacks against women and said that women had never abandoned their struggle, even under the harshest conditions of war.


Jin, Jiyan, Azadî has spread across the world'


Zeynep Oduncu said that the struggle waged by women in Kobanê against the darkness of ISIS had become an example for women around the world. She emphasized that women asserted their existence on the battlefields through their songs and ululations: "In the victory of Kobanê, we witnessed women's victory, their existence and how they asserted themselves in the struggle. Women established their existence while fighting against ISIS barbarism. This struggle became an example for the entire world. Women's struggle, their existence and the way they asserted themselves on the battlefield through their songs and ululations truly became an example for the whole world. Today, the slogan 'Jin, Jiyan, Azadî (Woman, Life, Freedom)' has spread across the world.


Women demonstrated that they feared nothing in their struggle to participate in every sphere of life, even during war. They fought for their own …

title: Ayten Kordu: Men and states started wars, but women will bring peace
content:
Ayten Kordu, Dersim MP for the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), answered ANF's questions about the Peace and Democratic Society Process initiated by Abdullah Öcalan's call on 27 February 2025, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on 25 November, the relationship between women's freedom and peace, and women's expectations of the process.


Ayten Kordu said that the struggle against violence against women is not limited to 25 November, noting that the Kurdish women's movement and women's movements in Turkey have fought for many years against violence, massacres, harassment, rape, exploitation and policies of denial. Kordu said that Kurdish women have significant historical experience in this struggle and continue their activities under the slogan "We have a voice for a free and equal life, and we rebel against violence."


 


'The women's struggle aims for social transformation'


Ayten Kordu said that Kurdish women have fought for their identity, existence and freedom for many years, explaining that this struggle extends beyond gender-based demands. Kordu pointed out that women have challenged the patriarchal mentality established over thousands of years, as well as centralism and militarism: "For a long time, Kurdish women's struggle for identity, existence and their demands as women was not only a women's struggle but also a social struggle. When we speak of the patriarchal mentality, we are actually questioning the centralist and militarist mentality embodied in the state today. Women have approached their demands for equality and freedom in life as inseparable from social transformation."


Ayten Kordu said that one of the characteristics distinguishing the women's movement from other struggles is its aim of transforming society. Kordu added that the struggle carried out alongside women's movements in Turkey has gone through difficult periods.


'Violence against women targets society as a whole'


Ayten Kordu said that women are struggling against violence and massacres in almost every part of Turkey, adding that suspicious deaths of women, harassment, rape, impoverishment and labour exploitation also threaten women's lives.


Kordu said that special warfare policies have been implemented in Kurdistan for many years and that violence against women has developed into a mechanism affecting society as a whole. Kordu said, "Every form of violence against women has become a mechanism of violence that spreads throughout society and targets society as a whole."


Ayten Kordu argued that the patriarchal mentality has grown stronger, particularly under the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government, pointing to Turkey's withdrawal from the Istanbul Convention and the failure to effectively implement Law No. 6284.


Kordu said that violence has increased despite official declarations of zero tolerance towards violence against women, adding that women have not abandoned their rights and continue their resistance in the streets and through organised struggle.


'Women's spaces of organisation have been targeted'


Ayten Kordu said that women have never abandoned their struggle or efforts to organise. Women's associations and cooperatives have been established, but these organisations have repeatedly been shut down.


Kordu also said that the appointment of government trustees to municipalities has targeted women's spaces of organisation: "This centralist mentality, this patriarchal state mentality, has always intervened first in places where women's spaces and organisations exist. This has always been the case. Women have established their own structures and developed an autonomous women's struggle in politics, workplaces, fields, streets, political parties and everywhere else. Through their own experiences, women have learned that organisation is their most essential means of self-defence."


Ayten Kordu said that women's labour is present in every aspect of life, yet women continue to be ignored and face attempts to confine them to their homes and restrict their living spaces. Kordu added that women in prisons also face various rights violations.


Kordu pointed out that women held in Sincan Women's Closed Prison have repeatedly had their release postponed through decisions by prison administrative and observation boards. Women prisoners also face difficulties accessing medical treatment.

title: Baghdad orders takeover of Kurdish border crossings and disputed oil fields
content:
The Iraqi central government has ordered sweeping measures to take control of border crossings and oil fields in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI) and the disputed territories. The decisions announced on Tuesday by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi stipulate that all border crossings in the region be placed under the authority of the federal border crossings agency and that Baghdad’s powers over oil production and the export of petroleum products be expanded. The orders follow investigations into suspected oil smuggling and could exacerbate longstanding tensions between Baghdad and Hewlêr (Erbil).


According to Sabah al-Numan, spokesperson for the prime minister and commander-in-chief of the Iraqi armed forces, the Kurdistan Regional Government will henceforth be required to process export permits for crude oil and petroleum products exclusively through the Federal Ministry of Oil. Baghdad is thus asserting greater control over the region’s oil trade. Since oil exports via Turkey resumed in September 2025, they have already been subject to an agreement between the central government and the Kurdistan Regional Government.


Oil fields in disputed territories affected


The orders have particularly far-reaching implications for oil fields in the provinces of Diyala, Kirkuk, Salahaddin, and Nineveh. They affect facilities that Baghdad considers to fall under the authority of the Federal Ministry of Oil but that remain under the security control of the Kurdistan Regional Government. Their administration is to be placed directly under the Iraqi Ministry of Oil.


Control over oil production has been one of the central points of contention between Baghdad and Hewlêr for years. The dispute concerns both the distribution of revenues and political and administrative control over territories whose status remains contested between the central government and the Kurdistan Region of Iraq.


Following the 2017 independence referendum, the Iraqi central government regained military control of Kirkuk and other disputed territories. Legal disputes over the independent production and marketing of Kurdish oil also remain unresolved.


Closure of unofficial border crossings ordered


In addition to interventions in the oil sector, the package of measures provides for tighter border controls. All unofficial crossing points along Iraq’s international borders are to be closed. This explicitly includes the Kurdistan Region. The Iraqi Ministry of Defense has also been instructed to block unauthorized routes connecting the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI) with the provinces of Diyala, Salahaddin, Kirkuk, and Nineveh.


Personnel from the Ministry of Oil, the Energy Police, and national security agencies are to be stationed at entry points to Hewlêr, Sulaymaniyah, and Duhok. Newly established laboratories will inspect petroleum products transported into the region. At the same time, Iraq’s Commission of Integrity is to investigate possible irregularities in oil exports, supply contracts, and refinery supplies.


Additional technical measures are planned to strengthen oversight of the oil sector. All oil fields in Iraq are to be secured by the Energy Police and monitored by surveillance cameras. Electronic meters at production facilities and a nationwide digital pipeline monitoring system are intended to help detect unrecorded oil shipments.


Oil smuggling investigations lead to dismissals and suspensions


The decisions come amid investigations into suspected smuggling networks in Iraq’s oil sector. One of the main focuses is the state-owned North Oil Company, which is responsible for oil and gas fields in the north of the country. According to Iraqi authorities, substantial quantities of crude oil are believed to have been illegally diverted and sold over a period of several years.


The investigations have also led to allegations against the pro-Iranian militia Kataib Hezbollah, which is suspected of involvement in a smuggling network in the city of Jurf al-Sakhar, southwest of Baghdad. The organization denies the allegations.


Prime Minister al-Zaidi has ordered several personnel changes. The head of the Federal Border Crossings Authority was dismissed, while the Director General of the North Oil Company and his deputies were suspended pending further investigations. Senior police and security officials in Kirkuk were also removed from their posts.

title: Call for an independent investigation after the discovery of bones and skulls in Silvan
content:
Following the discovery of numerous human skulls and bones in a three-level cave near Silvan district, in the province of Amed (Diyarbakır), the Initiative for Respect for the Dead and Justice called for an independent investigation. The organization believes the remains may belong to people who were forcibly abducted or extrajudicially executed in the 1990s. This possibility must not be left uninvestigated, the initiative said in a statement on Tuesday.


The Mezopotamya News Agency (MA) reported the discovery on Monday and published footage of the human remains. It remains unknown how many individuals the bones belong to, or when and under what circumstances they died.


Indications of a possible clandestine burial site


The initiative recalled that Silvan and the surrounding areas were the scene of serious human rights violations, particularly in the 1990s. During the Turkish state’s dirty war against the Kurdish guerrillas, numerous cases of enforced disappearances and extrajudicial executions occurred in the region. “The fact that the remains belong to several individuals and are scattered across different levels of the cave raises the question of whether the site may have been used as a clandestine burial ground. Such a possibility must be examined through an independent and effective investigation.”


Families’ right to truth and farewell


The initiative emphasized that leaving human remains unidentified and separated from their identities and loved ones violates not only the right to life but also the principles of human dignity and respect for the dead.


In addition to a criminal investigation, the initiative highlighted the rights of the families of missing persons to learn the fate of their loved ones so they can mourn them and provide them with a dignified burial. “The bodies of deceased individuals must not be treated as nameless and unclaimed remains. We must not forget that behind every single human remain lies a person’s life, identity, and past—and family members who are waiting for news of them,” the initiative stated.

title: PJAK: There can be no social liberation without women’s freedom
content:
The Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK) emphasized the central importance of women’s liberation for a democratic society on the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on November 25. In a statement released on Tuesday, the party described patriarchal violence as a manifestation of social and political power structures that cannot be overcome through legal reforms alone.


With regard to Iran and Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilat), the PJAK pointed to the systematic oppression of women, political imprisonment, and executions. It called for strengthening recent protest campaigns led by women and continuing resistance until all imprisoned women are released. At the same time, it emphasized the international dimension of the struggle against patriarchal violence, exploitation, and war.


The PJAK statement, titled “Without the struggle for women’s freedom, neither a revolution nor a society is on the path to freedom,” reads as follows:


"November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, is a day on which we commemorate women’s historic struggle against all forms of violence, domination, discrimination, and patriarchal systems. It is a day when the voices of freedom-loving women grow louder in the face of oppressive structures, and the struggle for freedom, equality, and human dignity once again becomes a historic and social responsibility.


Women’s freedom is the foundation of social liberation


Violence against women is not an individual phenomenon that can be reduced to personal behavior. Rather, its roots lie in power structures, the patriarchal mentality, systems of domination, and social, political, and economic conditions. Therefore, the struggle against violence against women is also a struggle for the fundamental transformation of society and the liberation of humanity from all forms of domination.


In our philosophy of struggle, women’s freedom is neither a secondary issue nor merely a legal demand. Rather, it forms the foundation of social freedom and serves as the benchmark for the realization of genuine democracy. A society in which women are not free cannot be considered a free society.


The domination of women is the first and most deeply rooted form of domination in human social history. Through the continuous reproduction of power relations, sexist attitudes, and unequal structures, the patriarchal system restricts the freedom of both women and men. Women’s liberation therefore cannot be achieved through legislative changes or superficial reforms alone. Instead, it requires a revolution in mentality, the development of an independent consciousness, women’s autonomous organization based on freedom, and the restructuring of social relations on the basis of freedom, equality, and democratic coexistence.


“Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” is a vision for social transformation


The pioneering role of Kurdish women in the freedom struggle is one of the most remarkable expressions of women’s historic determination to break the chains of oppression and reclaim their identity, their will, and the right to determine their own destiny. Guided by the philosophy of “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” [Woman, Life, Freedom], Kurdish women have demonstrated through their struggle, organization, consciousness, and resistance that women are not passive victims of circumstances but a driving force in transforming society and building a free future.


This pioneering role is not limited to the struggle against gender-based discrimination. It also challenges the mentality of enslavement, authoritarianism, extreme nationalism, state domination, and all structures that subject life to subjugation. By linking women’s freedom, the right to life, and the freedom of society, the philosophy of “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” offers a new vision for human liberation and the establishment of a democratic, ethical, and free society in Iran and Eastern Kurdistan.


Resistance against the systematic oppression of women in Iran


In Iran, misogyny and the systematic oppression of women have become one of the main pillars sustaining the Islamic Republic’s regime. Through the enforcement of discriminatory laws, control over women’s bodies and clothing, restrictions on individual and social rights and freedoms, and the use of organized violence, the regime has taken patriarchal domination to its extreme.
